One Hundred and Eighty Against Two

[Będzin — opinion: unemployment, poverty and begging.] (Our arithmetic, poverty and want. — Do we see it? Do we react to the terrible phenomena in our life?)
L. Szpigelman.
If only people would complain among us that things are bad, that we are oppressed and that we have nothing to do; if only people would say that the Jewish situation is bitter and sad. Who invented such lies? Who dares to say that Jews in Poland have nothing to do? True, there is in Poland, and here in Zagłębie, a certain percentage of unemployment, but that is surely only among Christians, among the Christian workers, and by no means among the Jewish population.
You do not believe it? But what use to us is your not believing. You doubt it? But what for? Will you doubt that it can be proven to you in black and white?
There is in Poland a town which surely many of you and of us know. The town has been called since olden times Będzin. And Będzin you surely all know, we know it too, so why should you not know it. It is, no evil eye, a Jewish town "ver tsu got hot"[?], but it is important to say — Jewish: it has no more and no less than 85 per cent Jews, and that is interesting. Last week the Będzin Magistrat [town council] paid out urgent winter relief to 180 unemployed; among these 180 unemployed there were registered in all 2 Jews — read: two. Well then, we ask you — on the contrary, say it yourselves: are there unemployed Jews among us? Are there young people who have nothing to do? Do we have poor people? Here is the best proof that what we lament[?] so much is nothing more than staged affairs; it is nothing more than a way to make the public think that not everybody among us is well off, whereas in truth we are so well off that it could not be better..
Exactly such praises and laudations will our "kind-hearted" antisemitic councillors sing at [printed "oyf oyf", a doubled word] our address whenever someone wants to argue[?] about the bitter Jewish situation in the town, when a subsidy is needed for a charitable institution and one will then have to describe the want and the pain that poverty puts us through.
At such a moment our antisemites will flare up and ask their Jewish colleagues: what kind of show are you putting on? Whom are you fooling? What do you want to hush up from us? What do we need your false tears for, when with you everything is in the best order, when you are well and fine. On the contrary — they will cry out — let us see where poverty, misery and want prevail. When the Będzin Magistrat gave urgent relief to the unemployed, whom did we see, Jews or Christians? Yes — they will triumph — we understand your "facts"[?] perfectly well, you play your roles well. And what — one asks — will the Jewish councillors then answer to these well-argued reproaches? In what situation will our representatives then find themselves?
And yet, when Rosh Chodesh comes — but why just Rosh Chodesh, it is the same every day and all week long — young people march from house to house holding out their hands for alms; and if you try to ask them why they hold out their hands, they will show you that they were craftsmen, that they were workers and today have nothing to do — and there is much truth in that too. Unfortunately, however, fate has brought them to the point where in time they have become professional beggars, and the truth may be said loudly and openly to everyone: now they no longer feel like working, even if they were to get work. We see it before Passover too: when matzos have to be baked, Christian helpers are taken, because there are no Jewish ones; when cleaning has to be done, no Jewish woman will go — not to speak of laundry and other household work. For that they have no time, they are busy with begging, and they cannot split themselves in two — even with the best will they cannot be everywhere.
And we — we do give, after all; we are, after all, somehow the people of compassion, the true, ancient, traditional merciful sons of the merciful.
A rather large percentage of the Jewish population gives right and left, whether they can afford it or not, whether one ought to give or not. Giving is certainly no sin, after all — so thinks a Jewish "khakhter"[?] — and meanwhile, meanwhile we are in this way systematically raising a generation of beggars and idlers, of sick and hungry people. That is the result of our good-heartedness, of this giving without a system, without which there is control [sic; meaning: without any control].
It is sad and painful enough that the Jewish situation in the country is bitter to the highest degree, that we are pushed out everywhere we are, and where we are not, we are surely not let in; so one must see at such a moment to save the worst of the situation as far as possible. If we lose certain positions, we must become productive in another field. One must[?] not allow those who lose their productive work to fall straight into the terrible state of begging. We now have a very, very large percentage of such people, and it happened only because nobody takes an interest in the newly fallen, who in the best case are sent to hold out their hands — and then the person is lost for ever and ever: he will not work any more after that, he becomes neglected and lazy and indifferent to everyone and everything.
And this neglect we already see in the fact that even the unemployed we do have do not know how to register, and so the picture arises that there is no poverty among us.
But when one reflects on the Jewish situation, when one looks deeper into our poor cellar and attic dwellings, we see the sadness in its true form, and then we see how bitter is the want of the working Jewish families, who show themselves to nobody but languish in darkness. So why do these very people, who work hard and bitterly and are now unemployed, not register? Why is it not explained to them that it is no disgrace to come for support at a moment when one is forced to go hungry? Above all it should be borne in mind that the support is not private but public, coming from the municipal self-government.
The Jewish unemployed must surely be told that by being ashamed to present themselves at the Magistrat they create a false opinion of the Jewish situation, which our antisemites exploit whenever an opportune moment arises.
The Jewish worker must be taught not to lose heart at the moment when he has no work.
After all, in Europe and in America and in other parts of the world so much attention is paid to the unemployed element, and all this is done only so that he should not lose heart, should not enter the stage of begging, of becoming an idler and unproductive.
After all, we too have democratic and left-wing representatives in the town council — so why do they not see to educating their voters? Why do they not instil self-awareness in people? Why do they not explain how important it is to be registered in a municipal institution as workers, as productive people?
Are our representatives of an 85-per-cent Jewish community not ashamed that among 180 unemployed there are in all two Jews? Is it any wonder, then, that in this way no very favourable opinion of us is formed? Let us not forget that we have before us figures which speak for themselves: 180 against 2.
At a Serious Moment.

[Będzin — education; the "Yavneh" Jewish gymnasium.] The Będzin Jewish gymnasium, which for 12 years was in poor technical conditions because of the kind of premises it had, which were not suited to the needs of a gymnasium, has since the beginning of this school year moved into a permanent home, into the magnificent building which was erected for this purpose by the benefactor and patron esteemed by all of us, Mr. S. Fürstenberg [Szymon Fürstenberg]. This is not the place, and now is not the time, to give an appraisal of Mr. Fürstenberg's great deed. Too[?] close is the distance at which we stand to be able to appraise the event properly; on the other hand, we must draw up a little summary of the past and consider the prospects for the future.
Twelve years ago a group of Jewish national activists founded the local Jewish gymnasium with the famous historical name "Yavneh".
Unfortunately, three of the most devoted and most active co-workers, who achieved so much for the building-up of the "Yavneh" gymnasium — namely R' Berisz Frenger[?], R' Szaja Hendel Ehrlich and R' Moszek Szajn, of blessed memory — have departed to the World of Truth, and with that the circle of school activists has shrunk, and consequently the burden on the remaining ones, who have carried it to this very day, has grown even heavier.
What did the founders aim at in building the "Yavneh" gymnasium?
They aimed at educating a true Jewish generation, imbued first of all with Jewish learning (chochmat Yahadut), general knowledge, and with a burning love for the Jewish people and land; and this was concentrated in the name given, "Yavneh"; the historical name "Yavneh" was regarded as a symbol, as a programme, which greatly obliges the founders.
Now the question arises: has the school fulfilled the hopes that were placed in it?
Unfortunately we must answer this question: No! In the field of Jewish learning, and even in the national field, the school has accomplished very little; on the other hand, in the field of general knowledge the school has made enormous progress.
And what actually are the reasons that have hindered its national development? This is not the place to enumerate all the reasons, but in general — because the school has always lived in very difficult conditions; it had to fight all kinds of obstacles and stumbling blocks, and many forces rose up and aimed[?] to swallow it up; and only a small handful of people, a select few, know that only thanks to the extraordinary efforts and self-sacrifice of a handful of members of the supervisory board did they succeed in keeping the school alive and continuing its course[?] of development.
And thanks to this, the efforts of the supervisory board with the Kuratorium [school-district authority] three years ago — to obtain government rights (state recognition) for the school — were also crowned with due success, and indeed from then on the gymnasium's period of flowering begins, up to the last school year.
As mentioned above, from this school year the gymnasium has moved into the magnificent building of the foundation of the Fürstenberg family, and as an equivalent and in gratitude for the great deed, the supervisory board parted — admittedly with pain in its heart — with the so symbolic and historical name "Yavneh", and from that moment changed the name and called it after the great benefactor, "Szymonostwa Fürstenbergów" [i.e. "of Mr. and Mrs. Szymon Fürstenberg"], in the hope that the school would now attain its lofty goal.
Mr. Fürstenberg, for his part, solemnly declared at a series of meetings of the supervisory board that he had set himself as a goal in his life the founding of the school in order to perpetuate his name, whereas the social character and the management of the school would remain under the influence of the supervisory board. Unfortunately there are grounds for judging that the further development is not proceeding along the straight line that was mapped out in advance. Above all, Mr. Potasz's resignation gives us reason to think that this supposition is correct. Mr. Potasz stood like a loyal soldier on guard for 12 years at the head of the school, and was the official representative and the embodiment of the supervisory board. It is indeed unbelievable that after 12 years of devoted and laborious work, and after so many efforts by the supervisory board to get Mr. Potasz to withdraw his resignation — it did not succeed in any way; and one cannot by any means believe that merely for purely material reasons, without deeper reasons of principle, Mr. Potasz tendered his resignation so categorically. This fact leaves much to think about.
In any case, the task of the supervisory board must now be to strive to fill Mr. Potasz's post with a responsible person in whom one can have absolute confidence that he will be able to protect the school so that it does not lose its social character and national content, for long years of practice have already shown us that without a stable representative of the supervisory board the existence of the school was threatened, and further such experiments would again put it in danger.
The moment is a serious one and the question must be considered at once.
Y. Wygodzki.
A Celebration Among Us Should Not Be an Ordeal.

[Community life — customs; weddings.] (A few words about the disorder that prevails among us at weddings.)
A few days ago I was invited to a wedding at an acquaintance's, and seeing the disorder that prevails among us at such celebrations, I was no longer surprised why people run away from holding traditional weddings. And here I happened to see how, even before the guests had sat down at the table, they were surrounded by collectors from various institutions and societies, so that it simply looked like the eve of Yom Kippur in the synagogue at Mincha..
But that is still not where the whole disorder lies. After all, this is an accepted custom, and everyone who goes to a wedding probably reckons in advance that he must donate so-and-so much to charity. Our societies, too, actually draw up their budgets counting on certain sums that will come in at celebrations.
I noticed, however, another undesirable phenomenon, namely: around the table that was intended for the invited guests, uninvited people plonked themselves down — professional beggars, schnorrers and the like. However much the organisers of the wedding pleaded with them to give up the places to the invited guests, it was all of no help. The house in which the wedding took place happened not to be a large one, and many of the invited guests therefore had to leave. This led to the in-laws of the wedding becoming very upset, and instead of a celebration it turned for them into an unpleasantness.
A chapter of its own are the shamashim [synagogue beadles] at a wedding. In no other town does one notice such a phenomenon, that however many shamashim there are in town, they should all come to the wedding as one man.
All the remarks that I make here are therefore meant to draw the attention of our communities[?] to these phenomena, so that they introduce certain improvements in this respect. As a result this may possibly lead to the holding of the old traditional weddings being perhaps renewed[?], and our well-to-do people[?] too will not run away to foreign places when holding a wedding, as has unfortunately been the practice lately. Our klezmorim will then not need to complain, and the income of our kehilla will also increase thereby.
A. Higer.
The Educational Institution

[Sosnowiec — artisans, education.] (The Sosnowiec artisans' organisation, then and now. — What must and can be made of it?)
For a long time there was turmoil among the Sosnowiec artisans; for a long while a terrible chaos reigned there, and however many times people tried to find a way out of the terrible disharmony, they did not succeed; and not only did they not succeed, but on the contrary — they sank ever deeper into the unpleasant situation, from which they were never able to free themselves.
More than once the writer of these lines asked himself the question: what is going on there among the artisans, that they cannot get onto the straight path? How is it that such a productive organisation, which has such good chances to prosper, should fall so low and must [?] be unable to raise itself to the proper level? Nobody gave us the answer, but we saw it in the air: at every meeting it was plainly evident that the problem was not being approached honestly and with a clear conscience. Every time one could sense that the top was taken over by politics and intrigues, which flared up so much that they brought the useful institution to complete ruin.
Now that a different wind has begun [?] to blow there, the institution is reorganising itself and we see that there is good will to bring the association into proper shape — this is truly to be welcomed. And the newly formed board deserves to be welcomed already for not having been ashamed to start from aleph. We hold that the opening of evening courses for the members is one of the most important things, and that the courses were needed one can already see from the great success that the courses enjoy. Is it a trifle that an organised institution should allow such a large number of members to be found who cannot even sign their names? Whoever heard of conscious people in our day allowing their own comrades to sink so low? Must one really wait with such elementary learning until the government compels it? What man can get by in the twentieth century when he is unable to take a pen in hand?
In the columns of this very newspaper it has been pointed out more than once that the artisans should carry on fewer intrigues and even occupy themselves less with politics, and instead they should rather study, educate themselves more as cultured people as well as productive professional specialists. The leaders were often fond of taking offence at being shown what they ought to do, and instead of educating themselves and holding popular lectures on questions that should interest the artisans, they preferred to meddle in everything, not caring whether it brought benefit or harm; and out of this arose frictions and intrigues which gradually turned everything into a heap of ruins.
Now we see a gratifying phenomenon: apparently the goal has been set of educating conscious members, which is very desirable and should have been done long ago. At the same time, however, it must be pointed out that the work should not proceed the way people in Sosnowiec always like to do things: one sets about it with fire, with enthusiasm, with tremendous pomp, which as usual does not last long, and after a short time everything begins to weaken; the next day one forgets what was so solemnly promised yesterday, and the flame that burned so beautifully and gave off such rays of hope begins minute by minute to grow weaker and weaker, so that before one can turn around no trace of it all is left...
That is what is dangerous, that is what is harmful. Better not to go about it with such pomp, better not to do everything superficially and on one foot. Learn to take firm steps; better to go more slowly but surely, with calculation and deliberation. If one wants success in any activity whatsoever, if one wants the work not to go to waste, it must be done in a calculated way, systematically and according to a definite plan.
Evening courses are not only useful but also necessary, and therefore every possible means must be used to recruit as many students as possible. At the same time one must not forget that courses have the drawback of being dry and hard, so that they can quickly become tiresome to the students; therefore care must also be taken to bring a little life and warmth into them, so that they attract the students. The courses must be linked [?] in such a way that they are interesting for the students and attract them. For this purpose a director is needed, an expert, who should not merely know how to teach, but must always bear in mind what kind of pupils he has. There must therefore be a firm hand that understands how to run such an undertaking.
The most important thing, therefore, is to go along a sure path — slowly, with calculation and systematically, and thus steadily, step by step, gain one position after another. That is to say: work intensively and honestly. Only in this way can one hope that the present board, if it follows such a system, will be able to gain much both for itself and for the community.
And one more thing is important: to remember on every occasion that the institution is a professional one and must only take care to improve [?] the interests of its citizens [sic] and to solve their painful questions.
There is a broad field that begs to be worked, but for that one must know how to go about it. For we have already seen that when one approaches [?] it without knowing how, not only does one gain nothing from the work, but one loses a great deal, and even what one once had is destroyed.
Our artisans' organisation has every chance of occupying a respected place in the town. It can and must be represented everywhere. But representation is desirable only when it delegates representatives who are conscious and mature; otherwise they only help to degrade the prestige of those who sent them there. The organisation must therefore be run with full awareness, and the leaders must always remember that the association should be for them an ideal that must constantly be polished and purified. This will bring the members to understand as far as possible that they do not stand at the proper height, and that will already be a gain that cannot be estimated, because only in that case will it be possible to educate the members systematically to a higher level — and by that the association already gains in any case.
The present board holds the helm of the useful institution in its hands; let it remember this, so that it may succeed in making of the institution what it ought to be, what it will have to be once it has conscious, intelligent and trained artisans.
Whatever [?] the present leaders want to accomplish for the institution and for its members, they can achieve only now, while they stand at the helm of the institution they represent; and if they lack useful people, they can co-opt such — as long as what is needed gets done, what the artisans' organisation and its members are in need of.
Dr. Papuri.
The Voice of Mother Rachel

[Poetry — Land of Israel; the 1929 riots.]
I have a promise from the Almighty:
not forever in a state of exile
shall my children, Israel, be,
but they shall also flourish in their land.

Not forever trampled, crushed,
burned at the stake,
not forever spat in the face
by every scoundrel ("an hent" — doubtful reading).

Not forever shall they draw their customs
only from the foreign spring,
but they shall be a people
with its own pure morality.

When at this time I mourn
in my thousand-year sleep,
that at last there may already receive [it]
my forsaken sheep.

Ah! The time has come,
the morning star with its ray
has lit up the ruins of Judah
and chased the jackal away from them.

My children already stream
into their old-new home,
whoever plants vineyards
and whoever kneads the clay for building.

One dances from the joy of work,
youth and old together,
hand and shoulder joined,
for, after all, one works on one's own land.

But suddenly Satan
darkened my joy:
a slaughter of my children
was murderously prepared.

You children of Ishmael,
why did you slaughter
my hard-working sons,
who lit up your darkness?

Why did you slaughter little chicks
sucking at their mothers' breasts,
torture women to death
murderously before the men's eyes?

Torah scholars slaughtered
while sitting absorbed in God's teaching;
from your murderous hands
their blood still drips...

But know this, you barbarians:
not by the power of the sword
will you drive my children
from their inherited soil.

Rather they shall flourish forever
on the dreamed-of mountain,
for God's word and promise
are holy, mighty and strong.

Shlomo Holcblat.
Our Panorama

(Hasidim who whistle. — Goes to the mikveh and curses heretics. — A kingdom of Circassians. — A Jewish in-law at a gentile wedding. — An "attentat" [?] on a library. — Gabbaim who climb onto tables. — A Torah reader angry at Grünbaum. — "Hashomer Hatzair" studies "Shnayim Ochazin". — Armistice in the Będzin Talmud Torah.)
King Solomon said: "There is nothing new under the sun." Nevertheless we see many things that are indeed novelties. We always knew that the "Torah-true" "distinguish" themselves in the field of politics, "occupation" [taking over posts], disgracing rebbes and rabbis who are not of our own circle; but that they can also whistle — that we did not know. Now comes all [?] of Strzemieszyce and announces to the world that they have "sharp" Ger Hasidim who deserve the Nobel Prize for their whistling...
They do not whistle just like that, but, for instance, at a siyum of a Torah scroll, when the public sings "Hatikvah" — then the Ger Hasidim accompany the anthem. Reb Leibishl and Reb Dudl excelled with their "mouth music"...
— Bravo, Strzemieszyce! Happy are you, well for you, that your community possesses whistling Hasidim..
———
In Sławków too a rare "antique" has been discovered. But we small folk are not capable of appraising the value of the "discovery", so we give the floor to our "poetic" correspondent.
There is with us in Sławków — he writes — a "Hasidic bar-nash" [fellow]: his colour is yellow, mikveh water drips from his sidelocks, he walks in straw slippers, he curses the heretics, the Mizrachists [printed "Morchim"] and the Zionists, and he does not hate what others love. — Here come 9 dots. Perhaps you know, faithful readers, male and female, the meaning of the 9 "kropki" [dots]?...
———
Dańdówka outdoes the Strzemieszyce whistlers and the Sławków "antique". It may be that the Dańdówka report will cause unpleasantness for the inhabitants of Zagłębie; it will be "lucky" for us if the secret police in Zagłębie, God forbid, does not stir, given that in Dańdówka there exists a "kingdom of the Romanov dynasty": the gabbai's portfolio has been taken over by — Stessel, "per"-gabbai [?] — a Cossack with a big, long moustache, a genuine Circassian; besides him there is a large number of Circassians there, who are led under the command of Kuropatkin and of a "Major without a moustache"...
The "Circassian government" eats a great deal of onion, and since their wives cannot bear the onion smell, they run away from their husbands. The latter take revenge and do not let the wives hear Kiddush. Already 3 Sabbaths have passed and the Dańdówka wives (so our correspondent assures us) have not heard any Kiddush... and the "koyles" [voices, [?]] of the "eyshes-khayels" [women of valour] reach up to the seventh heaven"... In short, Dańdówka is a "mahkim pidanyes" [?]; as if the trouble with the Circassians were not enough, it happened there again that katsaps [Russians, derogatory] grind meat on the Sabbath, Jewish "fraylins" [young ladies] teach shkotsim [gentile lads] to dance, and a Jewish "mekhitn" [in-law] danced with an old woman at a gentile "khasene" [wedding]..
Well, that one can still digest; the trouble is great, however, in that the in-law fell down with the old woman and all the Circassians applauded "bravo"..
Because of the tragic accident that befell the Jewish in-law, we must shorten the report; we fulfil only the heart-rending request of the reporter, who asks us to come out with an outcry to the world of justice — he says [?]: "How much longer will the Dańdówka wives drag themselves around beneath the windows of their husbands, the Circassians, who will not make Kiddush but only eat a lot of onion"!...
———
The youth of Czeladź has a different complaint. They want to find justice with "the robbed Cossack".
Today European civilization has entered Czeladź: carriages without horses and "kolejki" [trains/trams] without "whistlers" have begun running through the streets. — So the local youth reflected and decided that "one must go with the current".
The first public step of the youth in the Jewish street of Czeladź was — to found a library!
They rented premises, bought books, and the "thirsty" drank from the cultural "spring"...
When the local "Agudah" leaders heard that the Sitra Achra had grabbed its way into Czeladź, there was an uproar among them; at once a meeting was held, and
— "Come, let us deal wisely!"
The "magicians of Egypt" proved that "the library is a house of ill repute" and that "when there befalleth any war", when the people of the house of ill repute grow stronger, there will be "and so get them up out of the land" — the holy "Agudah" must go under, Heaven forfend...
The "wonders" of the magicians convinced few, so the "Agudah" contented itself with the first plague: shedding blood... But for this "plague" they had no cure; the landlord of the library premises, who was persecuted and suffered insults and humiliations in the beit midrash, resorted to a better means
— "with a strong hand" [?]...
And the means worked: a "great fear" fell upon "God's Cossacks", and they are already at "Nirtzah" [the end of the Seder, i.e. giving in]; they already agree that the library may exist, so that their daughters will not be among the "guests" on the Milowice road...
———
"Sielce wished to dwell in tranquillity": in Sielce peace and tranquillity always reigned, then they took a fancy to founding a minyan, to be like other people. For this purpose a meeting was called, and over a glass of liquor a "Regency Council" was elected of 3 gabbaim, 3 "pomocniki" [assistants] and above them — a premier...
When the minyan came into force, the "Regency Council" issued the following ordinances:
1) A worshipper of the Sielce minyan may not recognise any other kingdom whatsoever, i.e. he may not travel to any rebbe at all.
2) During the Torah reading the "Regency Council" stands at the bimah and the "congregation" at a distance.
3) Whoever transgresses the ordinances will be severely punished.
And it came to pass one day, it was a fine morning (so we are assured), that the Council received news that one of the "people" had rebelled and travelled to a rebbe...
A meeting was immediately held, at which the ruling was issued that the recalcitrant shall not receive an aliyah until Simchat Torah...
When the verdict was published, the "congregation" held a secret assembly. The first to speak was the condemned man, who was holding Lenin's [?] picture. On it he swore a solemn oath that "even if it costs head and neck", such gabbaim may not approach the Torah scroll.
The "Regency Council" did not sit with folded hands either, and introduced strict precautions so that the rebellious "people" could not break into the "royal palace". For this purpose the bimah was fixed to the eastern wall, the Holy Ark was barricaded, and when the Torah is taken out the gabbai must climb onto the table...
As our correspondent reports from secret sources, preparations are being made for the "congregation" too to get up onto the table...
———
In the Sosnowiec town synagogue, too, an "uprising" broke out. But there the fire was soon extinguished.
The Torah reader in the synagogue, reading to the public Pharaoh's dream that "the 7 lean cows ate up the 7 fat cows", became very angry: how can it be? Such impudence, that cows should permit themselves such a thing?! And as he thinks about Pharaoh's dream, he recalls that the same is happening today before our eyes, and the proof: "such a lean Yitzhak Grünbaum swallows so many pot-bellied souls"...
— No! It must not stay like this! I, the Torah reader of the Sosnowiec synagogue, will not allow some Yitzhakl to disgrace the ringleaders of the "Agudah", yes? The time has come! The hour has come — I will take my revenge on the "Mizrachi" [printed "Morchi"], which evicted me from their synagogue.
— What is the matter with you? Reb [?], you look so melancholy!
— You guessed it, Itshke: still [?] that Grünbaum...
The public heard this and kept silent; but "Mordecai bowed not": there is a Mordecai in the synagogue who did not keep silent but began to interpret the Torah reader's dream..
A "miracle" happened, for the public was already about to "throw up"; otherwise the comic dream would have turned into a sad reality...
———
Speaking of real matters, one must not ignore the great deeds of the Sosnowiec Keren Kayemet committee.!
The Keren Kayemet committee in Sosnowiec saw to it year in, year out, that the kehilla budget should contain a subsidy for the "Keren Kayemet".
The committee won every time; the parnassim allotted such a subsidy — and the minister struck it out, because in the course of the whole year the committee "forgot" that the subsidy has to be collected from the gmina...
"Hashomer Hatzair" remembered the subsidy; it has candidates for Eretz [Israel], only they lack the travel costs.
And "Hashomer Hatzair" applied to the kehilla with a request that they grant it the subsidy "for poor emigrants to Palestine".
When the committee learned of this "hafuze" [?], "Pharaoh awoke": what [?] — money for the "Keren Kayemet"?! And where are we?! True, for 2 whole years we have not received a single grosz; so what if this was said while everyone was asleep; but if "Hashomer Hatzair" wants it — then it teaches us that we want it too...
So they take up the Gemara and study with a Gemara chant: "Two hold a Keren Kayemet subsidy?! This one says 'it is all mine'" — the committee shouts to the kehilla: the subsidy belongs to us; "and that one says" — and "Hashomer Hatzair" demonstrates with proofs that "it is all mine", for we are the true heirs..
— Well, how does one rule? Let them divide it, no?
"Splien getes" [?], they come to meetings, threaten war, and only the Creator of the world knows the way out of this "khad kati betrei varki" [?]..
———
It is also curious who will win — the Ger Hasidim or the Talmud Torah gabbaim in Będzin.
Several devoted people took it upon themselves to bring the Będzin "Talmud Torah" out of darkness into light and out of bondage into redemption, to see to it that the melamdim should not starve and that the poor children should receive a proper education.
When the Talmud Torah was under the "supervision" of the "Machzikei Hadat", one melamed drilled 104 pupils.. (may they multiply).
So the new committee understood the sad consequences of such an "order" and engaged another melamed.
And it came to pass one day — and we hold that everywhere the word "vayehi" denotes trouble — and here too, with the melamed, there was trouble.
— What trouble?
— The melamed is not a Ger Hasid but an Aleksander Hasid.. Be astonished, O heavens!
When the Ger gabbaim learned of this "outrageous deed", a great tumult arose in their camp. How can it be! Such a scandal should happen in Będzin!
A meeting was held, it went off very stormily, and an "ingenious" proposal was adopted:
— An armistice for 4 weeks! During this time — there is a supposition — the forces of both sides will be strengthened and...
— Is it prophecy? We shall wait and see..
Ben Amotz.
The Tragedy of the Jewish Small Trader

[Economy — small traders.] The small trader is regarded as a "merchant", and it is forgotten that his situation is worse than a worker's.
The more one speaks and warns and points out that such-and-such an attitude toward the Jewish small traders will only bring ruin and the economic destruction of the whole small-trader class, the more one does — as if out of spite toward this warning — exactly the opposite. And yet one cannot and must not keep silent. After all, this is not about some trifle. It is about the life and death of a large part of Polish Jewry.
Let the dry facts speak. The small trader, who even until now has struggled under the hardest conditions with his bitter fate, fought with self-sacrifice for his scrap of livelihood, has in recent days become desperate and disappointed. The hope he placed in the takings of the pre-holiday season [the Christian holidays] has not been fulfilled. In the pre-holiday season people took in no more than during the whole year. Now he is unable to meet the obligations he undertook to pay precisely in these days.
And a fresh flood of protested bills and bankruptcies threatens, which as a consequence will make the whole small trade even harder than until now. If the situation of the merchant in general is hard, if there is not a single economic field that has been spared and remained untouched by the chaotic state of the Polish economy, then the situation of the small traders is doubly miserable. The small merchant is placed in uniquely bad conditions, which make it impossible for him to rescue himself by his own strength from his lamentable situation...
Whereas the big merchant, when he finds himself in a bad financial situation, when he is forced into bankruptcy, performs the well-known "Caesarean section" and everything stays as before. He remains the same merchant as before, and enjoys the same — if not an even larger — credit than before. The small merchant, however, must in the case of bankruptcy go completely under, because he does it mostly when the knife is already at his throat, when he no longer has anything to pay with, when he sits by empty shelves; then, together with his credit, he also loses his means of existence.
One need not be a prophet to foresee that this wheel of fate will not spare a single small merchant — sooner or later — and he will have to go the tragic way...
And it occurs to no one to count the small trader too — who economically stands on a much lower level than the workers who suffer [?], and whose toil is perhaps even greater than that of the workers — as part of the proletarian class, and to let him also enjoy all the benefits that society applies to the proletariat.
The false opinion is still generally accepted that the small trader is an independent person who practises a free and independent profession. Yes, he is independent in the sense that he stands in life by himself, abandoned by everyone and left to his fate. Even legislation, through the false identification of the small trader with the merchant, arrives at curious conclusions. When, for example, a law is made in favour of the eight-hour working day, and the merchant is compelled to keep his business open only [printed "gor"] at certain hours of the day so that his employees should not have to work more than the legal eight hours, a report is also drawn up and the small trader who sits with his stall or booth in the market square is punished for violating the law, although it is known that he has no employees.
And this false view accompanies the small trader at every step. Who else, like the small trader — through the unhygienic conditions in which he has to live — is so prone to various illnesses?! Always standing outdoors, he is exposed to the direct effect of various atmospheric influences, which ruin his body and make a wreck of him, so that he often has to be in close contact with the doctor and needs medical help. Yet he is not accepted into the sickness fund (Kasa Chorych). All because of his so-called independence...
The small trader, however, bears his suffering within himself and, silent, does not protest, like a true martyr; therefore one neither sees nor hears anyone take up his grievance [?], anyone care about the tragic fate of the sorely tried small trader.
Therefore, in the present hour of need and misery, a mighty voice must be raised so that help may come to the desperate and disappointed Jewish small traders!
Y. Grosman.
At the Market (A Miniature)

[Literature — miniature.] Kehos Kliger.
At the Market.
(A miniature).
1.
A gloomy, overcast day, the sky grey, the air damp, cold.
Wrapped in rags, a soaked-through little Jew stands in the market, trembling with cold.
His face shrivelled, old, not a drop of life in it, no sign of having eaten his fill.
Hungry eyes, a hand stretched out to the people hurrying past.
"Give a donation to a poor Jew!"
Quietly the Jew stands, quiet and mute.
People run past him; no one spares even a glance at the little bundle of wrapped-up bones. They hurry, they rush, fortune drives them as with whips — no time to open the purse, to give a donation. —
* * *
At the corner of "Piast". A beggar, a Christian beggar with a clean-shaven mug, in a warm jacket, sits on the pavement.
He throws himself down, crosses himself, the beggar, before the greatest and before the smallest, mumbles something incomprehensible under his nose, shakes his big, [—] moustache.
People throw ringing coins into his outstretched cap with the shiny visor.
They throw — and the cap is full, almost overflowing...
Again he crosses himself, mumbles under his nose, shakes his drawn-out [?] moustache, [—] with his thick lips — he thanks, he blesses
and — perhaps he is actually cursing?! —
2.
At the "Bazaar".
Among the big, countless fruit crates a host of women bustles about.
It is Thursday today. People are buying for the Sabbath. Everyone is taking in money, everyone's face shines with the big takings..
To one side, set apart from the long row of stalls, a young girl sits by two small crates of fruit — a girl with two braided black plaits.
She sits and looks out for a customer — today she has not even had a "początek" [first sale of the day].
All the women shout, call the customer, and the young girl is silent.
All alone she sits and is silent.
She has not called anyone to her even once, she, the girl with the braided plaits.
She sits and [?] in her place: "What — will she really take in nothing at all [?]"?!
— — — — —
The "Bazaar" is already empty, the big square already thinned out.
Women who like to haggle [?] over a grosz still hang about by the apple crates. — —
The goods are already being carried off, night is already falling, it is already late. — — —
The last to leave the "Bazaar" was the young girl with the braided plaits.
Tearful, with an oppressed heart.
If you want to take in money, you must call the customer, persuade, talk him round.
She cannot shout, call, persuade, talk round.
So she left the "Bazaar" without a "początek", she, the young, poor girl with the braided black plaits.
„Herbatki“ (Tea Parties). (A Little Feuilleton).

One of the reforms that the old-new premier Bartel has decided to carry out is — that officials should begin to conduct themselves more decently and not carouse[?] so much in the night-restaurants and cabarets...
The press snapped this up like a treat[?] and went further still — and what about the „herbatki“ [official tea parties], which cost the state treasury a fortune[?] in money and make a sizeable hole in the state treasury?...
And why should we not say it? The press is not entirely wrong[?] here.
On the surface it may indeed seem a trifle — what is a „herbatka“, after all? One drinks a few glasses of sweet tea...
So what of it? Is there really such a calamity in it? Is it really such poverty, especially for a state?...
If things really are so[?], then there would be nothing left for us but one thing — to abolish the „herbatki“!
And here I am reminded of a similar story in a certain Sosnowiec society.
There too the members of the board used to drink sweet tea in the society every evening, and also to play a hand of cards until...
One fine morning they took stock and saw that the society was suffering badly from the „club“, and it was decided: no more „club“, no more...
So what do you think was the end of it? You think that thanks to this „reform“ the society was put right? Not a bit of it[?]! On the contrary, the hole only grew bigger. For since there was not even a sweet glass of tea any more, what was the point of coming to the society at all? And the ship drifted off without a rudder...
I therefore think that the trouble with the „herbatki“ is quite a different one — the calamity lies not so much in the tea as in the sugar[?] that is put into the tea...
Just imagine: an official sits down with his good pals to drink tea „at the public's expense“ and „sweetens“ it so much that one comes away with sticky fingers...
That is why the „herbatki“ have provoked such protests!..
Onkelos.
A Few Words on This Year's Kehilla Budget

In my previous article I already pointed to the economic policy of the kehilla, how no account at all is taken of the ability of the "etat"-payer [payer of the communal tax] or of today's critical time, when the whole merchant class is being crushed under the burden of the enormous tax press. In the present article I want to point further to some concrete figures in connection with the kehilla budget for the year 1930.
Already in the first item of the revenues the picture becomes clear, in which direction the whole budget will be cut: at a time when the etat of last year, i.e. 1929, amounted in all to 128 thousand złoty, this year's budget already provides for an etat revenue of 173 thousand złoty, i.e. a surplus of 45 thousand złoty, which comes to 35 per cent more than last year. Has the situation of the Jewish merchants really improved so much that one can already allow oneself to raise the etat by 35 per cent?
It is enough to become acquainted with the statistical figures of the number of patents [trade licences] purchased and the number of protested bills of exchange and bankruptcies, in comparison with the previous year, in order to get an idea of the terrible ruin that reigns in the Jewish street — and a shudder seizes everyone before the dreadful figures, which clearly show that we stand before a mass pauperisation. And in such a situation one can allow oneself to raise the etat by 45 thousand zł.? And on what are the 45 thousand zł. being spent?
On the rabbinate account we see a new item of 500 zł. for droshkies and travel expenses for the rabbinate and the board, and a supplement for the morei hora'a [rabbinical decisors] [?] of 250 zł.
On the synagogue account we see that the item for the conductor and choir has been increased by 3 600 zł., at a time when the previous conductor, Mr. Kalmus, received in all 3 000 zł. together with the choir. Self-evidently the pay was too little to maintain himself with the choir, and because of that the well-known dispute broke out between the conductor and the kehilla, and because of various misunderstandings the kehilla dismissed Mr. Kalmus — and now 6,600 zł. have so easily been fixed for the conductor with the choir, whereas had one given Mr. Kalmus a supplement of 1,000 zł. he would have been satisfied. And I must admit [?] that in this respect I too, not being well oriented in the situation, bear a little of the blame — "and my sins I recall this day"...
Now, the shechita account is already known to the reader from my last article, about the contracts concluded with the shochtim for 10 000 zł. a year, which amounts to an increase of 7,000 zł. yearly. Then comes the item in the shape of a creature that keeps crying "give, give" and is never sated — that is the mikve item: one keeps building and constantly spending money.
Permanent committees to collect voluntary donations, and like a holey sack that never becomes full and does not budge from its place — and will this year's 25000 zł. really help it move forward a little? Who knows, one does not want to believe it.
In the item of subsidies this year they handed out "to the right" [?] very generously to dead and living institutions; even the Agudah's Bnos Yisroel found favour this year too and received a gift out of a donated block [?] — a sum of 300 zł.
Revenge was taken on the "Yavne", whose gymnasium stood in all budgets higher than all the other schools, which is a self-evident thing in comparison with the expenses; this year it was reduced by 2000 zł. and today's "Fürstenberg gymnasium was put on a par with a cheder "Yesodei ha-Torah"...
One single item can indeed be counted as a positive: the 15000 zł. for the orphanage. The remaining tens of thousands of zł. could quite easily have been saved, and part of them avoided altogether, and it would be worthwhile that the council, when it deals with the budget, should think well over every item and not pass over the budget so hastily. The council must take into account today's economic crisis of the whole of Jewry (Klal Yisrael).
Note Landner.
„The New Programme of Jewish Nationalism“.

(From the Polish press).
In the Chadecja [Christian Democratic] organ in Upper Silesia, „Polonia“ (No. 1886), we find under the above-mentioned title a lengthy treatise on Jewish nationalism. The author, a certain Iza Moszczeńska, no excessively great friend of the Jews, writes at length[?] about Zionism, Palestine and other delicate matters of which she has, to begin with, not the slightest knowledge. But let us just see what the „great wisdom“ relates:
„The political programme of the Zionists has always found greater recognition and support in Christian society than among the Jews themselves. They (the Zionists) had widely ramified connections, mighty influence, great means to realise their ideals, but at the same time political Zionism evoked only a weak echo among those whom one wanted to colonise in Palestine, i.e. among the broad Jewish popular masses. Whoever knew the Jews well, and therefore was also well acquainted with Palestine, could not delude himself that Balfour's consent (?) [the Balfour Declaration] would yield real and solid results“.
Here the author goes on to describe the general development that followed last August's events [the riots of August 1929] and comes to the conclusion that Jewish emigration to Palestine was not at all as large as one might have thought:
„We attach very great importance to the fact that actual emigration to Palestine has lately been very small, and re-emigration has even exceeded it in recent times, even before the pogroms in the country took place[?]. In 1927, 839 Jews left Poland for Palestine, while 2214 came back from Palestine in the same year. In 1928 only 393 Jews left[?] Poland for Palestine. It appears that neither religion nor historical traditions can move even the more pious Jews to settle on the land of their forefathers, thereby abandoning foreign countries to which they are bound not by any lofty ideals but only by more real interests“.
In the second part of her treatise the writer of the article poses a crude question, to which she herself finds an answer: „Why do the Jews have no fatherland? The destruction of Jerusalem by Titus means nothing. At that time, when the catastrophe of the Destruction happened, none of today's European countries yet existed. The same right that served all other peoples to create homes for themselves also served the Jews. There was plenty of room in new countries. If, however, the Jews did not do so even 19 centuries later and remained an exterritorial people, it is for no other reason than that they lacked the abilities and the desire to build a state of their own. To take a desolate land again and give it to the Jews as a country is senseless, because draining swamps, living in the desert, fighting wild beasts and cutting a way through thorns is not in the nature of the Jews“.
Well then, if we had no desire and abilities to create a state of our own, it is surely no reproach to us. We would, however, wish that such „experts on Jews and Palestine“ would hop over to Eretz Israel in order to see with their own eyes a Nahalal, Tel Aviv and other such wonders[?] which the „good-for-nothing and lazy Jew“ has managed to create in a short time. We would also advise them to read through a page of Jewish history of the very latest times, so that they might at least see how many Jewish pioneers (halutzim) perished draining swamps. If they, all these „sages of every kind“, had known and read all that, they would have written differently. But, between ourselves, this is merely a means to an end, and what the end is we shall see presently:
„When the experiment of the Zionists — we read further in the mentioned article — did not succeed, Jewish nationalism comes forward with a new programme (?), which it propagates on this and the other side of the Atlantic. This time the matter touches us more closely, for it is a question of no more and no less than designating Poland as the actual home of the Jews, i.e. to create a joint state for them and for us — the entire Jewish emigration from all countries is to go to Poland (!), where such conditions would be created for them that they could live comfortably, as at home — in a word, a sort of Jewish-Polish condominium is to be born here, and at the same time it is to be a metropolis for all of Jewry, which is scattered over the whole[?] world“.
A thousand times have we already heard, and will perhaps hear as many times again, that „the Jews want to seize Poland and want to create a „Judeo-Polonia““.
This is, after all, the eternal spectre that lurks — not since today — in the poor heads of the Polish antisemites.
Sh. Shtroykh.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: The Małobądz Power Station Still Has Its Old Appetite...

[Section „What's new in Zagłębie?“ — Będzin, municipality and electricity.]
What's new in Zagłębie?
Friday, 17 Tevet 5690. — Piątek 17 stycznia 1930 [Friday, 17 January 1930].
Będzin
The Małobądz power station still has its old appetite...
The owners of the power station (elektrownia) in Małobądz are angry that the local magistrate [town council] has obtained from the ministry a concession for the municipal power station. The matter will be heard today, Friday, by the tribunal court in Warsaw. On behalf of the town, President [mayor] Michel[?] and the delegate of the voivodeship, Dr Kaluski[?], will appear.
The Będzin Kehilla Is to Take Over the Shechita of Czeladź and Grodziec

[Będzin — kehilla and ritual slaughter.] The starosta [district head] has approached the kehilla administration with a proposal to take over the income and expenditure of the shechita [ritual slaughter] in Czeladź and of Groytse [Grodziec?].
The Magistrate and the Sejmik Study „Shnayim Ochazin“...

[Będzin — municipality and hospital.] For quite some time now the magistrate [town council], on the strength of legal documents, has been conducting a campaign to have the stat[?] hospital belong to the town. The present owners, the gentlemen of the sejmik [county council], do not want to let the hospital out of their hands and claim „kulah sheli“ [„it is all mine“] — the hospital belongs to us, we have a chazaka [right of possession]..

The Commission Will Decide on the „Kol Me-Vaser“...

[Będzin — municipality and water.] Next Monday the water-supply commission will hold a meeting at which the quota and price for water will be fixed.
— Gentlemen of the commission! We ask[?] you that the „kol me-vaser“ [pun: „kol mevaser“, a herald's voice / „voice of water“] should not be pitched in too high an octave..
Electric Motors on Instalments

[Będzin — electricity and crafts.] In order to ease the situation of small industrialists and artisans, the management of the power station has decided to arrange for electric motors and installations to be paid off in instalments.
The Kehilla Council and the Budget
[Będzin — kehilla and budget.] On Saturday evening a meeting of the kehilla council took place to consider the new kehilla budget. The council referred the budget to the budget committee.
Appeals, Declarations and Advance Payments

[Będzin — taxes and merchants.] The „Merchants' Association“ announces that: 1) merchants who have been refused, without any proper grounds, the benefit of the 1-percent tax reliefs should register by the 29th of this month. 2) Turnover declarations (zeznania) for 1929 must be submitted by 15 luty [February], and 3) the new advance payments (zaliczki) of the industrial tax for 1929 must already be paid.
The Situation Is “Improving”... / Again 600 Unemployed.

[Zagłębie — labour and industry.]
The management of the “Saturn” coal mine has cut 600 workers. The reason is that there is no market for the coal stocks[?].
The “Zawiercie” joint-stock company, too, has reduced working time to 3 days a week.
A Lung-Disease “Specialist”...

[Czeladź — crime; Będzin — artisans.]
The police in Czeladź arrested a Christian woman who had been posing there as a “specialist” in lung diseases. She had her own female patients, from whom she took money.
She came to grief with a Christian widow whom she treated with “pigułki” [pills], for which the sick woman paid 765 zł.
—o—
A Large Meeting of Artisans.
Last Sunday a large meeting took place on the premises of the Artisans' Association, at which the following agenda was dealt with:
1) report from the plenary session of the Chamber of Crafts in Kielce, 2) strengthening and broadening the evening and vocational courses, 3) loans for artisans, and 4) report of the “Bank Spółdzielczy”[?] [Cooperative Bank].
Chairman Grossman opens the meeting and the floor is given to Mr. Hampel, who delivers a report on the plenary session of the Kielce Chamber of Crafts, which took place on 29 December of this year [as printed, “p. y.”]. From the report it emerges that in 1931 examinations for craftsmen will have to be held, and therefore steps must be taken at once to prepare the Jewish craftsmen so that they do not fail the examinations. The speaker explains the importance of broadening, at the present moment, the activity of the evening courses.
Mr. Klajman supplements the report and calls on all members to enrol in the evening courses, for which nobody will have to pay any fee whatsoever; against members who do not enrol, stricter measures will be applied.
Messrs. Fajgenblat and Rudaler (Herszel) also speak, and the following resolution is adopted:
“The general meeting, numbering 300 members, calls on the artisans' representatives in the kehilla and in the city council to obtain larger subsidies for the evening and vocational courses, so that when the Jewish craftsmen are examined they will not suffer failure.”
Mr. Wingański[?] appeals to those assembled to continue depositing their savings in the “Bank Spółdzielczy”, which is the only bank for artisans. Mr. Wingański explains that in the month of December the bank earned 10 thousand zł.
The closing speech is given by Mr. Icchak Rudaler, and with that the meeting is closed.
Sosnowiec — A President and Vice-President of the Kehilla Elected.

[Sosnowiec — kehilla, rabbinate.]
Several weeks ago the kehilla board adopted a resolution that the kehilla should engage the rabbis Halberstam (a brother-in-law[?] of the Radomsko Rebbe) and Hager as honorary rabbis of the local kehilla. In connection with this the board notified the rabbis by letters of the kehilla resolution, but Mr. Zendel, as kehilla president, refused to sign the letters. Because of this a sharp conflict arose between Mr. Zendel and the other board members, and the conflict led to Mr. Zendel tendering his resignation.
On Tuesday evening the board held a session at which the matter was dealt with. Since Mr. Zendel declared categorically that he would not withdraw his resignation, elections of a president and vice-president took place.
The elections gave the following result: Mr. Icze Saks was elected president, and Mr. Abraham Sztyglic vice-president.
3,000 Taxpayers Released from the “Book of Remembrance”.

[Sosnowiec — taxes.]
On the basis of a special okólnik [circular] the local “Urząd” [tax office] invited representatives of merchants and artisans, and together with them the list of tax debtors for the years 1924, 25, 26, 27 and 28 was reviewed. About 3 thousand taxpayers without means were released from their debts.
1,653 Passengers Rode “na gapę” [Without a Ticket]...

[Sosnowiec — transport.]
From the tramway management we have received the following statistics: in the year 1929 the staff of tram conductors stopped 1,653 passengers who were riding the tram without tickets. Of that number, 1,397 passengers paid fourfold according to the regulations, and the remaining 256, who refused to pay a fine, were handed over to the court, which has already punished some of them.
Conference on the Crisis in the Tanneries.

[Sosnowiec — industry, commerce.]
In the local Chamber of Commerce, under the chairmanship of Eng. Gadomski[?], a conference of the commerce commission took place, which dealt with the critical situation of the tanning industry.
On this question Eng. Ruszczkowski[?] reported; he pointed to the fall in prices of raw hides and the critical situation of the tanneries, which are reducing the number of workers because of it.
The speaker puts forward the following proposals: 1) to introduce a protective duty on foreign shoes, and the duty on luxury leather should be raised, 2) to reduce the turnover tax, 3) to grant credits to the owners of tanneries.
Around these proposals a discussion developed, in which the councillors [radcy] concerned took part, and they spoke out in favour of organising the tanning industry on sound foundations.
Municipal Officials as Swindlers.

[Sosnowiec — municipality, court.]
In its time a great sensation was caused by the news of the abuses committed by several officials of the local magistrate [municipality], Messrs. Grabiański and Zawistowski. The officials had been authorised to inspect the sanitary condition of the bakeries.
At that time the Będzin starostwo [district office] closed the bakery of Henech Szajer. The latter, in despair, sought various ways and stratagems to reopen his bakery.
After some time Szajer met the starszy [head] of the bakers' guild, Mr. Rengli, before whom Szajer described his bitter situation. The head of the guild gave Szajer a piece of “advice”: to turn to the official Dziarkowski about the matter.
Szajer did so, and soon the above-mentioned officials came to him together[?]; after the “inspection” they declared that for 1,000 zł. they could arrange for the bakery to be reopened. The deal was made, and the officials took the first instalment of 200 zł.
When several weeks had passed and the bakery was still sealed, Szajer only then realised that he had been swindled, and handed the matter over to the prosecutor.
The trial took place this week. Hearing the witnesses took a whole day. After the speeches of the defence the court sentenced them to nine months' prison.
A Candidate for the President's Chair Has Been Found After All..

[Municipality — election of the city president.]
The parliamentary crisis in the local magistrate [city council] is over. After a long search a candidate has been found after all who agreed to occupy the president's chair in the local magistrate. The new president is the former vice-commissioner in the sickness fund, Mr. Aleksander Wipner[?].
The election procedure took place 3 times; only on the 3rd time did Mr. Wilner[?] receive 20 votes from the Endeks [National Democrats] and the P.P.S. [Polish Socialist Party].
The “Be-Be” [BBWR, the pro-government Nonpartisan Bloc] and the Jews took no part in the election.
On Tuesday the new president already took over his office.

A Lost Item Found in a Sensational Way.
The Katowice merchant Aleksander Bruk travelled on the Kraków express train to Lemberg [Lwów]. He carried with him a leather briefcase in which there were bills of exchange totalling 9300 zł., 1200 dollars and 4000 zł. in cash.
In Lemberg he drove to Baczewski's factory, where he had a number of matters to settle.
In the factory he noticed that he did not have the briefcase. In despair he went out to the car that had been waiting for him in front of the factory. The briefcase was searched for but not found.
The merchant began to suspect the chauffeur, but the latter defended himself, saying he had not even known whether the passenger had a bag with him. A policeman was called and the chauffeur was taken to the police station.
At the corner of Bałagowa[?] and Żółkiewska streets the merchant, thanks to the car's lamps, caught sight of his bag, which had lain in the street for over an hour without anyone noticing it.

So the Husband Has a Sweet Tooth...
Last Friday a tragicomic story happened here. On that day the baker's wife, Mrs. S., lived through the following 2 “tragedies”: 1) her husband “nibbled” the compote she had prepared in honour of the Sabbath, and 2) the baker's journeyman was not careful and 4 loaves of bread were spoiled.

An Artist-Painter Who Is Also an "Artist" at Setting Up Wedding Canopies...

[Zawiercie — society; a swindle.]
From Zawiercie we are written: the beit midrash of the Krimilov [probably Kromołów] Rebbe, may he live long, was renovated and painted. A painter from Będzin, a certain P—d, was engaged as the painter.
During the work the painter became acquainted with a local Jew, an intimate of the Rebbe. The acquaintance led to the painter becoming a regular guest at the house of the Rebbe's intimate. And since the latter has an unmarried daughter, who indeed took the fancy of the painter, who had introduced himself as a "cavalier" [an eligible bachelor], you can guess the rest...
After finishing the work in the beit midrash the "bridegroom" left for Będzin. Before leaving, an agreement was reached between both sides, i.e. between the bride's parents and the bridegroom, that the following Sunday the bride's father should come to Będzin, where the dowry would be paid and the wedding date fixed...
And so it was. The in-law came to Będzin at the appointed date, where he discussed with his future son-in-law the future life of the enamoured couple.
The "bridegroom" presented his plan for the future and depicted in bright colours the happy life with his God-destined educated bride.
"I," the "bridegroom" declared, "have renounced beauty; for me the main thing is education, and since your daughter is an educated woman and holds a post in a pharmaceutical warehouse [skład apteczny], I hope to spend a happy life with her..."
The bride's father was "moved" by the "happiness" awaiting his daughter and with a joyful heart took leave of his future son-in-law.
But coming onto Mandżejewer [probably Modrzejowska] Street he was disappointed. He happened to meet a Będzin Jew, a Krimilov Hasid, to whom he told that he had arranged a wedding date here...
— Who is the bridegroom from Będzin?! — the Będzin man asked.
— He lives "on the hill", he is an artist-painter, makes a good impression, wears glasses and is a good earner.
— Master of the Universe! What are you saying, have you lost your mind, God forbid?!
— What is the matter?
— Why, he has a wife and 2 children; the woman he told you is his sister is in fact his own wife...
People began to investigate and inquire, and only then did the in-law's "eyes open", and he saw what a net the artist-painter had spread to catch his daughter...

What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — news.] A sensational operation by railway thieves.
For some time now strange thefts of butter have been occurring in Katowice. When shipments of butter were sent off to Poland, what arrived there was "kartofl-mist" [?] [probably potato mash/potato flour]. It was hard to get to the bottom of the theft. Finally, at the freight station, a large crate was noticed that had been standing there a long time and that nobody had come to collect. The crate was opened and it was found that a comfortable bedroom had been fitted out inside. Forged railway forms, receipts, etc. were also found there. The investigation established that railway thieves had shipped one of their partners in this crate. On the way he used to come out of the crate and, while the train was moving, he simply swapped the labels on the barrels: on the barrels of butter he stuck labels for "kartofl-mist", and on the barrels of "kartofl-mist" he stuck labels for butter. Later his partners redeemed from the railway the crate with the thief, and together with it the barrels of butter. The railway authorities got on the thieves' trail, but the railway workers let the secret slip. The thieves found out about it and no longer came to redeem the crate.

A Tale of Hershele Ostropolier

[Theatre — Będzin.] (On today's premiere by the "Vilner" at the "Corso" [?]).
The "Vilner" troupe [the Vilna Troupe] is once again giving us a pleasant surprise. Only 8 days ago it staged "Yidn-shtot" ("Jewish Town") by Aaron Zeitlin in Będzin and in Sosnowiec, and already they are treating us to a new premiere, an original Yiddish comedy by M. Lifshits, "A Tale of Hershele Ostropolier". It should be stressed in this connection that the premieres the Vilner stage in Zagłębie are prepared with the same care and refinement [?] as the premieres in Warsaw. For every premiere special sets are painted, new costumes made, special music written.
In the premiere of "A Tale of Hershele Ostropolier" two worlds meet — on one side the rebbe Reb Dovidl, who embodies melancholy and cold resignation, and on the other side — joy, Hershele.
Hershele's appearances at the Zhivi...ter [?] "court" drive the gloom out of it and bring merriment into every corner. Hershele swaps clothes with the rebbe: he gives the rebbe his own poor, torn clothes and puts on the rebbe's fine clothes. But Hershele is, after all, a shlimazl: when they come to arrest the rebbe, they arrest Hershele. This "miracle" has such a strong effect that the worst misnaged becomes the rebbe's hasid... The author has skilfully used this episode to illuminate the rebbes' miracles. The exchange of clothes misleads not only the hasidim but even the rebbetzin..
The comedy ends with Hershele's disappearance. He vanishes as suddenly as he came, leaving behind a cheerful anecdote and a heartfelt, luminous melody that runs [?] through all four acts.
Tonight we shall see "Hershele" in Będzin.
Yiddish Scientific Institute (YIVO). Second Competition of the Ethnographic Commission

[Culture — YIVO.] The Ethnographic Commission announces a competition for the best and richest collections of war folklore that arose in the war years and reflects the war in all its phases, such as: tales, songs about the outbreak of the war, about expulsions, refugees ("biezhentses" [Polish bieżeńcy, refugees]), pogroms, from the time of the various occupations, forced-labour camps, military hospitals, prisons; tales, legends or various calculations (gematrias) created during the war; soldiers' songs or tales about the call-up ["prizyv", Russian for conscription], from the front, from the prisoner-of-war camp; beliefs and superstitions ["zabobones", Polish zabobony] that spread during the war; new words that arose in the war, parodies of German words ("Trauerkarten" [mourning cards] instead of "Dauerkarten" [season tickets], and others); jokes and anecdotes from the World War (about emperors, war leaders), puns and anecdotes arising from people not understanding one another, about courage and cowardice, giving oneself up into captivity, etc., etc.

The materials must be collected and written down according to our rules for collectors. If you do not have them, write to us and we will send them to you. The names of all participants in the competition will be printed in YIVO's "Yedies".
