President Nahum Sokolow's Visit to Katowice

[Upper Silesia — Zionism.]
On Monday, by the evening express train, President Nahum Sokolow arrived in Katowice, accompanied by his daughter Dr. Tsilena [?] [presumably Dr. Celina Sokolow]. While passing through Zagłębie, Sokolow took an interest in the Jewish population of Zagłębie and in particular in that of Będzin. When the train arrived at Sosnowiec, a large crowd welcomed him on the platform and stormily demanded that Sokolow show himself to his admirers. When Sokolow appeared, the air resounded with cries of "Yechi!" ("Long live!"). Seeing the enthusiastic crowd, Sokolow asked: Is this Będzin? The representative of "Unzer Tsaytung" ("Our Newspaper"), who was in the carriage with the president, only then explained to him that this was Sosnowiec. But Sokolow did not forget Będzin as the town of great achievements for the "Keren Hayesod", and he values its deeds as the largest Jewish community in Zagłębie.
On the way from Sosnowiec to Katowice, in a conversation with the writer of these lines, the president expressed the hope that the situation in Eretz Israel would soon improve, and he believes that Polish Jewry, which despite the severe crisis still fulfils its duty towards the upbuilding of Eretz Israel [will continue to do so].
In Katowice, although no reception had been announced, hundreds of people waited at the railway station; because of the heavy crush Sokolow was led out through the 4th-class platform. From the station Sokolow and his daughter were taken to the Hotel "Monopol".
The next day, Tuesday, in honour of the distinguished guest there took place
A festive session at the Kehilla
with the participation of Rabbi Fogelman [Dr. Mordechai Vogelmann, rabbi of Katowice], community leaders and invited guests. The holiday attire and the splendidly decorated hall created a festive atmosphere.
A specially decorated chair had been prepared for Sokolow, above which blue-and-white flags fluttered. The first greeting was delivered by the president of the community, Mr. Altman, who stressed that when Sokolow is in Katowice, "he is its glory, he is its splendour, he is its majesty"..
On behalf of the Katowice rabbinate Dr. Rabbi Fogelman greeted him; he began in Hebrew and went over to German. In his speech Dr. Fogelman declared that Sokolow belongs to the pleiad of great men who united in themselves the Jew and the human being.
Then the honoured guest replied to the greetings, drawing a parallel between Jerusalem and Katowice: although geography separates the cities, there is something in common between them. Sokolow recalled the first conference of "Hibbat Zion" in Katowice — that was a historic moment and remains unforgettable in the history of Zionism. The speaker called for further deeds for the spiritual capital, Jerusalem. There are — he said — Zionists and non-Zionists. But I want — says Sokolow — that there should be Zionists and not-yet Zionists. And that Katowice Jewry should help to create the great Zionist work.
In the afternoon Sokolow was received by the Voivode, with whom he conferred on important matters.
At 5 o'clock there took place at the Hotel "Monopol"
A press conference,
attended by representatives of the Jewish and non-Jewish newspapers in Zagłębie and in Upper Silesia.
In the evening at 8.30, in the hall of the "Powstańcy" [Silesian Insurgents], there took place a
Festive academy.
The start was delayed by a whole hour, a sign that Katowice has already adopted "Jewish punctuality".
The stage on which the presidium sits is beautifully decorated with garlands and blue-and-white flags. The academy was opened by Dr. Schwarzbart of Kraków, who greeted the representatives of the local authorities, the press and all participants in the academy. In his greeting the speaker emphasised that President Sokolow is the synthesis of the Jewish renaissance, of Jewish culture.
On behalf of the Zionist Organisation in Beuthen [Bytom], Mr. Wieger greeted him. On behalf of national Jewry [?] in Zagłębie, Rabbi Hager of Sosnowiec greeted him. The rabbi said that Sokolow was the one who bored the ears of the enslaved people that had declared "I love my master"... the one who tore apart the slave chains of the Jewish people.
Rabbi Hager's greeting was loudly applauded.
Also speaking: on behalf of the Zionist Org. in Katowice — Mr. Eisenberg; for the Merchants' Association — city councillor L. Żmigród [?]; for "WIZO" — city councillor Mrs. Ratner. Mrs. Ratner's greeting in Hebrew was interrupted several times by applause.
Enthusiastic and long-lasting were the ovations of the audience when Sokolow rose from the decorated chair and stepped up to give his lecture. If we — Sokolow began his lecture in Polish — were now to come to the world power with a project concerning Eretz Israel, we would depend on optimists and pessimists; but thank God, we come to the international forum with wondrous deeds that we have created in Palestine within so short a time. We have brought in 100 thousand vigorous, strong Jews, acquired large tracts of land, spread a school network, improved the sanitary situation, etc. Speaking of the attitude of the European states to the Eretz Israel question, President Sokolow expressed thanks to the Polish government for its warm attitude towards the upbuilding of Eretz Israel.
Sokolow delivered the second part of the lecture in Yiddish. Here one did not see Sokolow the scholar, the European, the diplomat, but Sokolow the Talmid Chacham, who refreshes his Hasidim with casual talk. Sokolow possesses above all an overflowing treasure of a pearly Yiddish language; he is folksy, his tone is fatherly-warm and rich.
The audience swallowed his words as Sokolow told how Tel Aviv and other towns and kvutzot were created. Like a quiet, calm stream the language flowed, and the audience listened like children to the beautiful stories of their father, who answers wisely the naive questions "What good is Eretz Israel to us?" and says: "Dear old Polish Jews, I do not know whether I will have the privilege of seeing you again, but do not abandon our positions; create and build for the Jewish future, for the Jewish people — a Jewish home."
The hall thundered with applause. Dr. Schwarzbart closed the academy; "Hatikvah" and "Tehezaknah" were sung, and the audience, among them Hasidic Jews and old men, rushed up onto the platform and took heartfelt leave of their old favourite, the refresher of souls of "Mi-Shabbat le-Shabbat" — Nahum Sokolow.
Later a banquet took place in the splendid Jewish restaurant "Piccadilly".
On Wednesday Sokolow visited Bielsko and from there departed for London.
The heavy tax burden — (Will it really be eased? Until when must one stand on guard and hold the positions.)

(Will it really be eased? Until when must one stand on guard and hold the positions.)
For a year now the newspapers have kept reporting that taxes will be reduced, and for several months now we have seen that the government has become more yielding, and in merchant circles people are almost convinced that the tax screw has finally loosened and that it will no longer squeeze so hard the small and middle-class citizens, whom the taxes strangle year after year.
Now people already believe in the relief, because they see that the government feels the crisis, which has spread across the whole country. One sees that the painful [?] question is already being discussed in the Sejm, and people are almost certain that certain changes will come [?] in this field, intended to ease the payment of taxes. We fear only one thing: that thanks to all these promises our people will let their wings droop [?], and that in public circles the questions will not be dealt with.
At the same time, however, one must not forget one thing: that we must not deceive ourselves, must not rely on any miracles and must not believe in anything at all. The taxes are draining all our strength. They suck the marrow out of the citizens; therefore one must indeed stand on guard and protect all this like the apple of one's eye.
The heaviest and most terrible tax, which crushes us to the utmost, is the turnover tax. When we hear about an "obrotowy" tax [podatek obrotowy, turnover tax] we shudder, after all, and when there is so much talk about that tax being reformed, then — then one must be alert and look and examine carefully for whom the reforms will be: for the citizens or — a question on a story [i.e. no wonder] — perhaps for the government. Thus it is known from authoritative sources that despite the severe crisis we lived through last year, there is good reason to fear that taxes will once again, as every year, be raised. We know from practice, after all, that the government only wants to get ever more revenue, so that our offices ["ushandn", urzędy — tax offices] in Zagłębie will surely have instructions "from the high windows" that the general income taxes should not only not be smaller but, on the contrary, larger. And even if we were to say that they will insist on collecting the same sums as last year, it will still be necessary to tax the existing firms with higher sums, because the offices will take into account that they will not be able to tax the firms that have gone out of the market and did not buy their patents [trade licences]; therefore they will have to take larger taxes from those who are still in the market, from those who are still standing on their feet.
The situation is therefore very serious, and the question must be considered from all sides, carefully [?] and systematically. We must be aware and alert; we must remember precisely that in the second month the offices will already start assessing last year's turnover.
We know, after all, that at the time [?] when the turnover tax is assessed it is a kind of Day of Judgement for every merchant, and no wonder, because this one and only tax is capable of ruining a firm completely once the assessed sum is excessive. No other tax is so complicated or turns a person into a ruin so quickly as the turnover tax.
Often the tax question is taken lightly among us, however heavy and frightening it may be. Thus last year the income tax ["dochodowy", podatek dochodowy] was neglected: the commissions did not keep watch and for the most part did not come to the sessions; one relied on the other, each thought the other had gone, and in reality nobody was there. At best, mute judges were put forward [?], who played the role of representatives and, of course, had no knowledge of anyone and consequently did not know the way in from the way out; to say nothing of the fact that whoever had to obtain relief or fight and defend was certainly, certainly not the authoritative person. That is why it is no wonder that the income tax ruined people to the utmost. People were perhaps never as terrified of the income tax as in this last year. People who had not yet lost the ground from under their feet wept and counted [as printed; perhaps "paid"]. Others were left as debtors and had sequestrations imposed on them.
Now the turnover tax comes up for consideration, where representatives from our side will sit. So let the question not be taken lightly; let our representatives know beforehand why they are entering the commissions, what they have to do there and what tasks lie before them. It is no longer a matter now of fighting so that X or Y should pay as little turnover tax as possible. It is simply a matter of the tax not driving this or that element into complete anarchy [?], because of which he would have to lose his place entirely.
It goes without saying that one cannot demand of people that they know what is really going on with every single person, and for that very reason an all-round mutual understanding is important. We know that nobody knows what is going on in another's pocket, nor can he know it, but with a certain planned public activity a great deal can be done. How? Very simply. Since [?] representatives of all the professional institutions sit there, let the institutions therefore acquaint themselves already now with the situation of every member, and on the basis of documents they will be able to know how and with what to defend each member separately. It goes without saying that it is important that our representatives keep in contact with one another, and this will make it possible to help a great deal regarding the heavy tax system in general and the turnover tax in particular.
Our representatives need to know only one thing: that it is now a matter of nothing more and nothing less than existence or ruin. The representatives on the assessment commissions must now formulate it this way, because there is no other way. In reality it is not otherwise.
Let the question not be regarded as a trifle. Let it be remembered that things have already come to "the waters have come up to the soul", and if our representatives in the offices will not want to help us, then who will help us?
One cannot, after all, let things come to such a state that he who still pays a bill of exchange should reach the point where he can no longer meet even that. The most important thing, therefore, is a practi- [continued in the left-hand column — see 2.12]
[Conclusion:] The heavy tax burden

[...The most important thing, therefore, is a practi]cal and planned understanding among themselves and with the members, and on that basis they will know what tasks they have taken upon themselves.
We do not want to forget for a single minute that the work is not an easy one and the responsibility is unquestionably greater still; we also know that the representatives have no pleasure while they sit there, but there is no helping it: as soon as it is a matter of existence or ruin, one cannot play at what is proper or improper, at etiquette and sentiments — as the saying goes: the goyim are breaking in!
At this very moment [?] our people's emissaries must be [—] present, and that is precisely why the preparation must be a real and consistent one; those who will sit on the assessment commissions must know exactly the situation and the turnover of every single person, and they must act as their conscience dictates to them and as practical justice demands.
The work must not be taken lightly, the activity must not be a haphazard one; everything must be worked out precisely and from all sides, both vis-à-vis the government and vis-à-vis the citizen-members, for whom it is hard to carry on the struggle for present-day life.
R. Les.
Our Panorama

(There is no crisis. — A war over beards. — Must a gabbai be a "Pharisee" or a "Don Juan". — The grievances of Modrzejów. — A practical "rebbe". — A chevra kadisha that deals with the living. — A commandant defends Zionist interests.)
Who made it up that we are living through a crisis today, that nothing could be worse, that Jews have no livelihood, that they are dying for a grosz and so on? Don't believe all these blabbers; just pop over to Ząbkowice, on the contrary, and you will see for yourselves that all this talk is empty — you will find a real war between brothers there. And over what, do you think? — Over beards...
The Ząbkowice kehilla, which numbers, no evil eye, about 4 minyanim, is split into two camps; each camp has its own interests, for which fierce battles are fought every Sabbath.
The most important cause of the battles is that it should be settled once and for all whether a gabbai who hands out aliyot must wear a beard or not.
On this difficult question opinions are divided. The bearded side shows with clear proofs that a gabbai must have a beard; other deeds [?] are kosher, as long as there is a beard — and the longer, the better.
The "clean-shaven" side argues the opposite: that a gabbai must not carry on romances with Ząbkowice "Maryśkas" [gentile girls]. Without a beard — they shout — the gabbai may be, as long as he is a kosher one, without Maryśkas.
And since both sides refuse to agree to a compromise, it is "la-yehudim" there. On the Sabbath, when the Torah scroll lies spread out on the bimah, a passionate discussion is held about [?] "bearded gabbaim with or without Maryśkas"... The discussion goes on until a policeman appears, delivers a moral sermon to the "Żydki" and announces that the continuation will be read at the Sosnowiec district court...
———
Modrzejów has long been famous for its sensations, but the latest "sensation" surpasses them all. Listen to an interesting thing: the chevra kadisha in Modrzejów does not, as is the custom in all the dispersions of Israel, deal with the dead, but rather with the living...
And to tell the truth, at first we thought that the Modrzejów "custom" was an invented thing, but when they start threatening us from Sosnowiec that we should publish the "sensation", we are "powerless" — so let the "world" learn what happened in the famous border shtetl — Modrzejów.
So Modrzejów has the floor:
"Here in Modrzejów — the correspondent relates — there is a Jew who was a frequent visitor ('yotze ve-nikhnas') at a certain rebbe, who died in Sosnowiec several months ago.
After the rebbe's passing, the Modrzejów intimate of the household looked after the widow, the rebbetzin; he arranged matches for her and also saw to it that she should lack nothing.
And it came to pass one day that the rebbetzin's provider [?] made up his mind that, in order to fulfil 'to raise up a rebbe in Israel', he would divorce his Gitele and marry the rebbetzin...
Gitele, poor thing, agreed to it, travelled with her 'destined one' to Będzin, and came back home a divorcee...
Let us leave the divorcee in peace for a while and take a look at what our 'bridegroom' is doing...
When he was free of Gitele, he grew a beard and sidelocks, dressed in a broad fur coat and a shtreimel, and went off with his 'young wife' to Galicia, to help [?] barren women there and to give Jews a livelihood...
Once, on a dark night, when a terrible wind was raging [?] outside, the 'rebbe' remembered his first little wife, for whom his 'first love had not yet gone out'...
That night the rebbe's successor could not sleep, and at daybreak he left the rebbetzin and — off to Modrzejów, to fall on his knees before his first, faithful wife, who because of his demand had received a get from him...
He arrived in Modrzejów on Thursday evening, at the time when Gitele the modest one was sitting and thinking about the coming Sabbath... At that moment the door opened and...
— Oh God [?], you! How did you get here? Where did you leave your rebbetzin?...
To these questions our 'rebbe' gave no answer, and in the blink of an eye threw off his clothes and...
— into bed...
Gitele was not impressed by the 'trick'; she ran out into the market square crying 'gevalt', at which a crowd came running; the police came too, with the commandant at their head, who ordered:
— Out of bed...
— Panie komendancie — declared the lying-down 'rebbe' — przecież to moja żona [but this is my wife]...
— Co za żona [what wife]? — Gitele began to scream — ja mam get od rabina z Będzina [I have a get from the rabbi of Będzin]...
The commandant did not recognise the Jewish get and left, leaving the 'mąż' [husband] lying in bed...
And once the commandant had left — well, there is no other way. Heh, heh, the world is not ownerless: the chevra kadisha came with all its attendants, and the 'living bar-minan' [deceased] was carried out of the house without a tahara. Gitele followed him and begged the 'rebbe' for forgiveness...
———
The Modrzejów chevra kadisha [?] deals with 'living dead', and the police in Działoszyce 'sing "Od lo avda" with the Zionists'...
There is a library in Działoszyce; it was founded by Zionists, later it passed into the hands of 'former' Zionists; above all, the library's latest proprietors kept accounts like the one-time Talmud Torah gabbaim in Będzin...
Well, how long can this go on? Several young Zionists spoke up: Stop! Enough lording it as householders — get down from the benches, and the like [?].
And since the old strongmen had no wish to take their leave [?], a meeting was called at which they studied the Mishnah 'Two hold on to a library; this one says it is all mine and that one says it is all mine', and when one side had already said 'let them divide it' [?], the local commandant took over the chairmanship of the meeting and 'took the heated crowd on the cymbal' [made a laughing stock of them].
The end was that the old Zionists won, and the library, thanks to the chairman, passed to its first proprietors.
— Bravo, Działoszyce! Happy are you to have such commandants...
———
How needed it would be for such a commandant to come to Czeladź and make a little order there among the Czeladź 'holy flock'. First of all he — the commandant, that is — would pay a visit to the Artisans' Association, stop [?] with some of the leaders and tell them thus:
— 'Panowie rzemieślnicy' [gentlemen artisans], it 'dziwi' [surprises] me very, very much that you, the persecuted and oppressed mass, give no thought to finding a way out — how to ease your bitter situation, how to secure your economic interests — but day and night busy yourselves with intrigues, quarrels, gossip and plain foolishness...
Yes, that is what he would tell them; but what comes of it, when the commandant is in Działoszyce and the [—] [?] artisans 'siredy' [?] — in Czeladź...
When One Does Not Understand One's Tasks

(The Dąbrowa town council and the pettiness of its Jewish representatives.)
A small, barely noticeable item crept onto the columns of our paper last week. The item bore the heading: “The B. B. [BBWR — the Nonpartisan Bloc for Cooperation with the Government] strikes Jewish subsidies”, and with that, it seems, everything was said. The Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza] town council, when drawing up the new budget — and as usual, every year, now too certain subsidies for Jewish institutions were found — here no questions at all were raised, no one considered whether it hurts anyone[?], that it is an injustice; rather, why and wherefore[?] they struck out what is Jewish, precisely where help ought to come to us.
How far the friendly relations between the B. B. and the Jews of Dąbrowa extend may be shown by the fact[?] that even such an innocent subsidy, which had been designated for social purposes, was also struck out.
The B. B. — who does not remember what means they used before the elections so that we should go with them hand in hand; they simply promised us “the little plate from heaven” [the moon and the stars], if only we kept to their right side; with liquorice-sweet words they simply intoxicated us, and more than once certain Jews had it in mind that we should be happy as soon as an understanding was reached between us and them. It looked then almost like the time of the “Ugoda” [the 1925 Polish-Jewish agreement], when every Jew beamed with joy, because it seemed to him that here salvation had come, here had been achieved what we need so badly in order to lead a quiet, honest life and to remain good citizens and loyal patriots in the country where we live.
But here too we were disappointed. Despite everything the Jewish voters of Dąbrowa conceded to them, they can no longer [recall] this[?]; apparently they forgot everything as soon as they came to the helm. Yes, they will surely remember us then — when they need to take from us; yes, then they forget nothing about us; at every step, at such a moment, they have the Jew in mind. With the revenues for the local self-government they will so contrive[?] that the money comes in as much as possible from those who trade, from those who hold patents [trade licences].
And our councillors who sit there — what do they do? What do they do when they see that the Jew is treated this way? With a bit of flattery, with a smile, with a little promise — they are bought. The indifference, the ice-cold[?] attitude of the Dąbrowa councillors towards their voters is unheard of; they take offence at nothing; barely do they hear a word from the “porets” [the lord, the master] than they tremble, and out of fear and deference they bow down threefold, just so as not to be regarded as “recalcitrant”, just so as to behave as father, mother and pious people bid.
For a heap[?] of lies they sell you the birthright. Otherwise they would not have dared to let themselves be trampled underfoot, as has happened more than once; otherwise they would have had to react on the spot when they were insulted in the name of the Jewish citizens. But the Jewish councillors of Dąbrowa unfortunately do not know what such a thing as Jewish dignity, Jewish honour, Jewish pride is, and therefore they accepted everything with love. More than once Jewish dignity has been publicly insulted there in such a way that every Jew should have blushed with shame; but the Dąbrowa representatives in the self-government are small-minded and exchange the dignity and the insults of the people for a kopeck of self-interest, for a bit of private business.
Their Christian colleagues know what sort of “Żydki” [little Jews, a Polish slur] they have sitting beside them, and that has led to the present situation, in which they allow themselves to do anything at the Jewish address. They know that these people are petty and have no understanding of how to keep themselves on the proper level; otherwise Jews there would not have been insulted to such an extent.
Had we had as councillors conscious Jews, who would understand their tasks and react systematically to every Jewish injustice, their Christian colleagues would have treated them with respect. They would in that case have understood that with simpleton's talk[?] one gets nowhere with them, and that they cannot be bought with a bit of flattery and a kind word.
We know they will defend themselves by saying that they are few in number and with the best will can achieve nothing, but that is no answer. For, firstly, from not achieving anything to being slighted and humiliated as representatives is quite a long way. One may be able to achieve nothing, the opponent can defend and guard his position, but he will know how to respect his opponent as a person, as a representative and spokesman of so-and-so many voters. And secondly, even a small minority can sometimes achieve a great deal, as soon as it has understanding and duties[?], as soon as it knows where it stands, in what atmosphere it breathes. One need only know how to be calculating and hold the balance in one's hand, and whoever knows consciously how to preserve the equilibrium can at such a moment help a great deal to create[?] and keep the dignity of the people at the proper height. And when the Christian colleagues see that, they will not have the nerve to slight the Jewish voters as is now happening in Dąbrowa.
Striking Jewish items at a time when revenues are demanded[?] from Jews means mocking you, means humiliating and provoking you; otherwise they would not have dared[?] to offend you so deeply.
We said earlier that one must be conscious and know where one stands, one must be able to keep the balance, and this brings great benefit. That this is so can also be seen from the town-council representatives in Będzin and Sosnowiec. Będzin, whose present self-government is almost half Jewish, achieves very little for itself proportionally, whereas Sosnowiec, for example, which has [—] Jews, carries through systematically enough: thus, for example, Sosnowiec with [—] Jewish councillors obtained 1 ławnik [member of the municipal executive], while Będzin has no more than 1 ławnik out of 16 councillors.
That is the best proof that it does not always play an important role how many Jews we bring in as representatives. Of course it is absolutely important that the number be as large as possible, as broad as possible, but that is not yet everything; it matters much more that we should have conscious people who know what they have been sent into the town council for and what they have to demand there — that is what is more important than anything!
After all, we Jewish representatives in Sosnowiec are a zero even compared with you in Dąbrowa; nevertheless, not only will they not dare to humiliate us there, but individually we carry through relatively much — to say nothing of Jewish subsidies: those the Christian councillors in our town do tolerate.
If things in Dąbrowa have come to such a low state that Jewish subsidies are struck out in such an unheard-of manner, which gives the impression as if they wanted to provoke the Jewish population of Dąbrowa, then only the Jewish representatives are to blame for it, because, as said, they would not have dared to do it at a moment when they knew and saw that the Jews of Dąbrowa have conscious, honest and proud representatives who can stand up in the name of the whole Jewish people (Klal Yisrael).
The world says: as one greets, so one is answered; such representatives as one sends, such privileges do they obtain.
Had the Jewish councillors of Dąbrowa stood at the proper height, they would have had to feel insulted by such treatment of Jewish affairs, and in that case they would have had to react properly to the unheard-of injustices being done to them.
Dr. Papuri[?].
The Yiddish Scientific Institute.

Philological Section.

The Philological Section of the Yiddish Scientific Institute [YIVO] has printed a questionnaire on the gender of words in Yiddish. The purpose of the questionnaire is to establish actual language usage, and thereby also the principles according to which the use of grammatical gender in the Yiddish language should be standardised. The more replies the Section receives, the better it will be able to do its work.

Although this is a purely scholarly task, any intelligent person can nevertheless answer the questionnaire. No professional knowledge of philology whatsoever is needed, and yet with a little effort one can be of great use to Yiddish language research. We are therefore sure that many readers of this paper will respond and come to help.

All who are interested are asked to send their addresses on a postcard, and YIVO will then send them the questionnaire with the appropriate instructions.

YIVO's address:
Żydowski Instytut Naukowy
W Pohulanka 18, Wilno [Wielka Pohulanka 18, Vilna].
A Storm of the Dead at the Izba Skarbowa.

By A. Lemech.
(Not a fantasy).

In a Warsaw tax office ghosts appear every evening and pitiful wailing is heard.
(From the chronicle).

A heavy weariness has fallen upon the treasury chief [naczelnik skarbu], Mr. Racięchowski [?]. From early morning the door of his office moves without pause: one żydek [Polish slur for a Jew] out — the next one in. Like nasty flies they have settled on him and won't let him catch his breath for a moment. Day after day they torment him, each in a different style. Oh, how he already knows all those phrases by heart! "What do they want of me? Just as if I didn't know that they haven't a penny left to their souls." Ha, ha, ha! With their belongings they shall pay, the mangy żydki! I'll pull their guts out of them! Ha, ha, ha! — and he recalls a letter of thanks from the higher authority to him. A trifle? Since he came down to the town he has managed to increase the taxes tenfold. Ah yes, the żydki went to complain about him. Ha, ha, ha, they think, the fools [?], what a favour they are doing him by it. He can get for it... either a decoration or a higher post. And bright fantasies shine forth. A post perhaps even in the capital — he rubs his fleshy, pampered hands. Oh, he longs for a nap. He rings for the usher [woźny], orders him not to let in any petitioners, for he has to do extremely important work, he must not be disturbed.

Having had the usher lock the door, he stretches out in his soft, well-upholstered armchair, arranges his round belly, opens his mouth and gives a broad yawn, so that his jaws crack, and, putting a hand under his head, he dozes off to the sweet strains of fantasy about decorations, higher posts and [—] belongings.

...The door opens (that even annoys him! Who dares to disturb him now! But he lies powerless as if paralysed, unable to move from the spot) — in creeps some figure in a shroud, with potsherds on its eyes, a terrifying skeleton, and it lets fall words like sparks of fire: "For vengeance I have come to you, vengeance! I will kill you! Do you remember how a few weeks ago I stood on this spot, begged fervently, simply wept, that you should have pity and not take the last little bit of my goods and chattels, it is after all a man's [livelihood?], I wept, with what shall I pay! I won't be able to afford the wedding — and you, you tyrant, shrugged your shoulders: trudno [too bad], it must be paid. And when I threw myself at your feet, you ordered the usher to throw me out, you took everything, because of you I went bankrupt, couldn't bear it and died. What will my wife and children do now? — I will kill you, kill you, you tyrant!"

Soon the door opens again, this time a little old woman comes in, a shrivelled Jewess, wrapped in a dirty, patched shroud, and she shrieks: "Everything in my home was sold off, the bedding I had kept for my forty-year-old daughter, the bit of linen — my daughter's wedding trousseau — and not even a little bench was left in the room, oh, my poor spinster daughter! — Death to him, the cruel one, death!" —

A broad, respectable Jew with an aristocratic face floats in and sighs: Yes, for generations, generations long our wealth and lineage have lasted, hundreds [?] of families earned their living from us. And then he came, and sucked and sucked [?], we sold everything to pay them, and in the end they loaded the last bit of furniture onto the cart. Oh, how my heart cramped seeing the furniture carried out of my home, my heart burst — oh, you ought to be strangled!

The door is already wide open, a young couple flies in in a panic [?], and she says: "He had a fancy to be a merchant, so he — she points at the chief — left him empty-handed. No pleas helped, the whole dowry went into the treasury, we were left naked and poor, he couldn't bear it and shot himself, and afterwards I drank a little bottle of poison. Our blood we demand, our young blood! Kill him!"

Thus hundreds, hundreds of ghosts crept in. Each comes to claim his life, buried before its time. They all clamour, kill him! — the dead storm.

Mr. Chief Racięchowski [?] lies as if paralysed. They want to tear him to pieces and he cannot defend himself, powerless. All the dead float around him, any moment now they will strangle him, his throat is already choking. Most of all a young bagel-seller bustles about him, whose basket of bagels the chief had ordered confiscated for taxes. He simply wants to tear him apart. "Who will give my poor old mother food to eat?" — he shouts into his face. The hundreds of dead grow fiercer, more combative. Mr. Chief is paralysed with fear and terror. Yet he manages to let out a few stifled cries for help: Ratujcie! Ratujcie! [Help!] — — —

The stifled cries for help echoed into the neighbouring rooms. The usher knocks on the door and no one opens; only a hoarse "Ratujcie!" is heard. All the officials come running. They break open the door and find Mr. Chief lying unconscious, a cold sweat running down his face, and from his mouth come terrible cries: "Ratujcie!"..

Waking up and seeing his familiar officials around him, he breathes freely, wipes off the sweat and looks around. What happened? — the officials ask him.
— Eh, a bad dream...

He thinks to himself: a prank [kawał] those mangy żydki have played on him... Ach, ach, what those żydki are capable of devising [?]!...
Artistic Caprices

[Zangen — Literary Supplement. Literary criticism.]
S. Elide.
(Joseph Opatoshu — on his 20th jubilee).
We now wish to single out, from the field of Joseph Opatoshu's many-sided, colour-sparkling, variously-shaped literary creation, one thing and dwell on it: we mean his historical-artistic works. After all, they have an enormously large share in his success and popularity. From their pages a laurel wreath was woven for him, and, what is more important: in this kind of creation he is distinctive, original and very daring, deviating from the bounded path, breaking conventional reins.
Criticism has long agreed with the idea that the poet is permitted — when writing a historical tale — to sin to a certain extent against the truths of historical details, provided he does not falsify the general picture of the epoch or of the personality he treats, provided he stays true to the character, the train of thought and the colour of life of the generation concerned. One, a well-known Hebrew novelist, Dr. A. Kabak, once said that in his work — the famous trilogy "Shlomo Molcho" — he deliberately, consciously falsified historical dates, bringing together historical personalities separated by a considerable distance in time, because it served him[?] better[?] to draw the course of ideas of that period; he sacrificed individual historical exactitudes on the altar of the overall impression. Such[?] a literary giant as Gustave Flaubert, who worked for years on his world-famous book "Salammbô", studied a world of books dealing with the epoch concerned, studied thoroughly archaeology, botany and everything that had any bearing on his work, and travelled to the distant African region he describes — and when in the end hair-splitters of the well-known type nevertheless sniffed out and found scientific "inaccuracies", he answered the reproaches in a letter: against the general picture I have not sinned, the harmony is there — well[?], if so, my conscience is clean before the truth.
Joseph Opatoshu possesses an exceptional talent for bringing to life and refreshing past eras, breathing into them a warm breath and setting them living before us. Not only does his masterly pen draw the outward figure perfectly; he also sings out the melody of life, the rhythm[?], the sorrow and joy of that time. The whispering groan of the felled Polish forests, the decline of the Polish szlachta, the year of fire and blood 1863, the exotic Kotsk Hasidism — how strongly and sharply he depicts all this, how the streams of life called up from the abyss of the past well up in him. How joyfully[?] they splash and how melancholically they lull to sleep, so that it seems to us that we stand beside them, that we hear[?] their fresh pulse of life.
But he has a caprice, Joseph Opatoshu: to take his heroes, historical personalities by name, and smear them with a foreign colour, to attach to them things that never happened, which even contradict the essence and character of those personalities. What can be more contradictory than the ascetic, intellectualized[?] Kotsk and eroticism? True, mysticism and eroticism have always been intertwined. But Kotsk, after all, bit out mysticism from Hasidism and preached an abstract life of the intellect. With everything Kotsk's opponents fought it — but what, eroticism of all things was never ascribed to it. It simply does not stick, and that already means sinning against a general character, not merely against a detail. Or, for example, hanging a cross around the neck of R' Jonathan Eybeschütz.
Such a poetic caprice: throwing into the middle of the wonderful historical depiction an incorrect splash of colour. A kind of pleasure in sinning against historical truth.
But from what has been said one must not yet conclude that Joseph Opatoshu wrongly grasped the specific essence of Kotsk Hasidism, or that he wanted to interpret it wrongly. First of all, he does not at all presume to give a treatise on the Kotsk doctrine as such. He is interested only in people, living beings, and the powerful, prominent features of the old rebbe, the lonely man of intellect of Kotsk, are true and honest. Like a God-anointed master he uncovers with one gesture, with one short sharp word, a small chamber in the mighty figure of the Kotsker's soul [printed "gshome", misprint for "neshome"]. The court, the surroundings are sharply and faithfully drawn. The contrast between the stern rebbe who drives people away and shouts "What are you doing here?" and the warm, lovely disciple who wants to gather Jewish souls around him is honest and deeply true. Opatoshu has also penetrated the deep teaching of the Kotsk "heder" down to its deepest depths. Select few know that from one of the Kotsker's disciples a drastic idea was voiced, that erotic love is a degree, a rung for reaching the high ladder of supreme love. But that in and of itself carnal, sinful love is also a degree — this sharp[?], inaccessible idea, which stormed the Hasidic world — is likewise not hidden from Opatoshu, and he puts it in the mouth of R' Itche the kabbalist. Proof that he knows genuine Kotsk Hasidism thoroughly, only — Opatoshu feels like playing a prank. Just like that, to come out[?] with a little jest — and an ugly, coarse one at that — at the Kotsker's address, just like that, a caprice. Like a mischievous boy he likes to play a prank, be it even with such giant — and perhaps precisely because of their giant stature — personalities as the old Kotsker or R' Jonathan Eybeschütz. Like a spite-doer he feels like playing such a trick. But the deeply penetrating reader recognises that these are merely caprices: — artistic caprices.
Leo Speyer — In Harness (A Fragment)

[Literary prose — allegory.] Leo Speyer[?]
In Harness. (A Fragment).
One walks slowly with chopped steps, like a dried-out, bony and hunched nag, its head hanging down and its legs buckling; another with hasty, sure steps like a calm[?], healthy horse, straight-backed, with long legs, strong and stiff; and another leaping, dancing along like a young, nimble foal, tossing its little head in constant restlessness.—
So people stride, harnessed to the wagon of life, chained into the hard, straight shaft, the mouth cut by the bridle. And on the wagon of life sits a poison-soaked, evil driver who lashes the air with the whip: hup[?], little man! Hey, giddy-up! Onward! Don't stop: onward! Giddy-up! — Down from the „kelnia“[?] fall sharp lashes, the body burns[?] and the horse-man strains to run away from the raining lashes. But the horse's head forgets that by running he drags along with him the angry[?] driver and his stinging whip..
So he strides, the horse-man, drags the heavily laden wagon of life, strides so beastly-submissively, the eyes covered, as with a horse, with leather blinkers, so that he should, God forbid, not cast glances to the side, off the highway, but must fix his eyes ahead of him, downward.
Sometimes the mystical[?] driver grows a little tired and lets the little horse-man catch his breath; the horse begins to neigh[?] a little, stamps his feet and thinks to himself: why always thus in harness? Why hurry, why drag heavy loads? What is this command? Always running, rushing — for whom? For what?
At once comes a crack of the whip: don't dawdle, horse's head! Away with the foolish thoughts! It is not for you to ponder such things, onward! Giddy-up! Onward! Don't dawdle, horse's head! Giddy-up! Onward!
A. W. Wertheim (Radom).
A Silhouette (A Poem in Prose)

[Literature — prose poem.] A Silhouette (a poem in prose).
From amid the half-quiet rustle of wings, from amid shadowy, whispering trees, on a tranquil summer night you stole out, surfaced[?] angel-pure and light of step, and appeared before me.
Your soft, elastic steps merged with the mysterious twilight-murmur of the leaves swaying toward one another.
Slowly, quietly your silk-soft hair glided over my face, like the caressing, blowing breeze soaked through with a fresh, pearly-juicy scent of grass, and its dark sheen blended with the half-shadowed contours around, which lure with their calm sweetness...
Your voice spread[?] in waves through the air and echoed far, far away in the stillness, and your white, marble neck shone out of that secret-whispering haziness like a bright gleam, and as it stole between the shadow-wrapped trees it stretched out like the half-floating grotesque crags in the azure, quiet sky...
In my brain a whirl arose — a storm that resounded again and again like the [?] of a waterfall after a downpour. My eyes lit up like torches, like the lightning — before the storm breaks out with crashing thunder[?], and I was wholly as if carried off by a whirlwind. — — —
My hands stretched out like two outspread wings and clasped your body, and my voice resounded mightily in the stillness:
„You I have awaited; in the eternal unrest of searching, for generations and longer, my soul has yearned for you, and in quiet minutes of sadness, when my heart overflowed its banks like a river, it longed for you. Your form lay in my depths like a hidden treasure and was cherished through long years... It is you! cries every drop of my blood. It is you! cries my whole being. Come! The hour of our union has struck“. — — — —
Notes: „Gallim“ / The Echo of an Article in „Zangen“

[Hebrew literature — press; notes.] Notes.
„Gallim“ [Waves] — a Hebrew literary weekly, Vilna[?], under the editorship of S. Czurner[?].
Hebrew literature in Poland has reached the last stage of decline. Complete stagnation in the whole Hebrew movement. Apart from „Tarbut“, which conducts a more or less lively activity. But that, after all, is limited only to the school sphere and education.
Has interest in Hebrew creativity really died out among us? Really died out altogether?
No; true indeed, the camp of Hebrew sympathisers is not overly large. But such a camp does exist — and a loyal camp, which would answer every call. Only the organiser, the gatherer, is missing; so they remain scattered and dispersed, and little by little the light of longing for the Hebrew word and creativity flickers out, little by little.
Who is to blame for this?
— Our generals[?], who would so much like to stand at the top with the golden sceptre in hand; but when one must first plough the field — for such „black“ work they are not willing. And when they are not granted [the honour] and their work is not done by others — well, from them too, at best, never mind: there is no lack of work and no lack of benches.
And what can bind together and gather more than the printed word? We had a Hebrew daily in Warsaw — true, far, far from a rich one, but in time it would have raised a creative Hebrew generation; it would have grouped rising talents around itself, and we might perhaps have seen the awakening of Hebrew — were it not, were it not for the treacherous, indifferent attitude of our Zionist leaders, who let the Hebrew newspaper quietly, modestly[?] die out, and — rid of its yoke! (Yes, a sad chapter — but a short note is not the place for it.)
So a group of young Hebrew writers, headed by the talented poet S. Czudner[?], has undertaken it, and with self-sacrifice they simply publish a Hebrew literary weekly; and what is most important: they have taken the organising shofar in hand and call for consolidation, for gathering the forces. Thus they now proclaim a „Sefirat ha-Ivrim“ [census of the Hebrews], a count of all Hebrew sympathisers in Poland; they call on whoever has even a bit of love for Hebrew to register in the „Camp of the Hebrews“, and on the activists in the towns and shtetls to send in a list of everyone with a positive attitude toward Hebrew. In a word: a lively newspaper that does not sit in a squashed armchair.
Mocked from the left and ignored by its own comrades — owing to the dismissive attitude of the Eretz-Israel comrades — it leads an embattled existence. We send it our heartfelt blessing:
May your hands be strengthened! — Y.

The Echo of an Article in „Zangen“.

Literary News

„First Snow“.
Some time ago a small booklet (17 pages in all) of poems by young beginners appeared under the title „Ershte shney“ („First Snow“). The critics received it warmly. S. Niger writes about them in „Der Tog“: „All are genuine poems, and each one — with its own tone, its own manner. A small booklet with a great promise, five poetic promises with one mouth“.
It is good that our young people remember at all that „if I am not for myself, who will be for me“, and do not wait for the favours of those sitting on top.
The youngest Jewish poet.
The youngest Jewish poet is Ezra Gutman of New York. He has only just turned bar-mitzvah and has already published a very promising little book, to which Mani Leib writes an introductory poem:
„...Poet, you are the king,
the whole world is your land,
and everything is subject
to the sign of your hand“.
A quotation from the child-poet's poems:
„I look at the world from
the distance
I look back
I walk on the bridge of history
on the eternal pavement“.
Henri Bergson on laughter.
The brilliant Jewish-French philosopher Henri Bergson, as is known, wrote a book on the philosophy of laughter — why and at what people laugh. The book now appears in a new edition with a new chapter on the well-known American movie-star comedian Buster Keaton. The means by which the said comedian provokes laughter (he plays like a sleepwalker[?], like a person who goes through life as through sleep) confirm Bergson's theory.
A new war book.
When it comes to fashion — there is no arguing. After the impression made by Remarque's „All Quiet on the Western Front“, Barbusse's „Under Fire“ and Sherriff's „Journey's End“, another new book has appeared in English, also based on life at the front. The book is called „Good-bye to All That“. The author is called Robert Graves and is counted among the talented young poets in England. Just like all the authors, Graves too served in the army himself and lived through the war himself, which he depicts — unlike all the war-writers — without heat[?], without passion.
What does the “Polonia” have to say about the Jewish-Arab conflicts in the Land of Israel?

The sad, bloody events in the Land of Israel last year do not cease to be a subject for the antisemitic writers of “Polonia”, which appears in Katowice. More than once we have already had occasion, in the columns of our paper, to expose the ignorance of the antisemitic writers about Palestine in general and about the August events in particular. In issue No. 27 of “Polonia” we find a rather long article entitled “The Struggle for Palestine”, in which the author gives a historical survey of the rights to Palestine, displaying in the process his ardent sympathies for the “poor”[?] Arabs...

“The struggle — so the article begins — that is now being waged over Palestine is in fact a struggle between close relatives, since both the Arabs and the Jews are Semites, whose ways parted thousands of years ago and who now meet again on the narrow strip of land, for which they fight with all[?] the force innate in the Oriental races.”

“The struggle is absolutely not an even one. True[?], the Arabs, who are distinguished by their beauty and the delicate[?] build of their bodies, constitute[?] a huge majority, amounting to over 80[?] percent of the inhabitants; moreover, the Catholic Arabs show solidarity with the Arabs of the Mohammedan faith. This element, however, has a very hard struggle to wage against the incoming Jewish element, which not only has huge capital collected all over the world, but also uses the newest technical equipment for field work.”

Despite his great hatred for the Jewry of the Land of Israel, the author must nevertheless admit that every guest who merely comes to Palestine will at once recognise the difference between the gardens and sown fields of the new Jewish colonies and the desolate Arab fields. Having further discussed the internal[?] situation of the country, as well as the system by which the Jews are colonised — the colonisation[?] of one colonist amounting, by the calculation of the article's writer, to over 20 thousand gold francs (!) — he comes to the conclusion that:

“The Jewish-Arab struggle is not confined to the mere soil of Palestine, but embraces[?] the whole Jewish people of 15 million scattered throughout the world, which wants at any price to possess a state of its own, as well as the whole Arab people, which lives around Palestine and numbers over 20[?] million inhabitants, territorially united, and which also strives for the political unity of the Arab people.”

“After last year's bloody events the struggle for Palestine has passed into the stage of an economic struggle, which which [sic] is being waged still more sharply and with more hatred; what will come of it is hard to foresee.”

It is already simply ugly and tiresome to argue with the people of Korfanty's “Polonia”. It is a miracle for us that the author has at least once admitted that he does not know what will come of this struggle, for what could we have done, for example, if he had prophesied that we would not conquer the Land of Israel?!
S. Shtroykh.
District conference of “Gordonia” in Będzin.

Last Saturday night the second regional meeting (pegisha glilit) of “Gordonia” opened in its own premises; over 200 members from Zagłębie and Częstochowa came to it. The first session was devoted to the yahrzeit of the creator of the Eretz-Israel labour movement, Aharon David Gordon, of blessed memory, whose name “Gordonia” bears. After the singing of “Hatikvah”, Comrade Kutner opens the memorial evening in Hebrew, and the delegated member of the National Central Committee, Comrade Ze'ev Goldberg, lectures on Gordon's life and work.

The 2nd festive session took place later in a packed hall holding up to 300 people. The session is opened on behalf of the District Committee by Comrade M. Hampel, who discusses (in Hebrew) the tasks of the Gordonist world. After the opening speech come greetings. On behalf of “Hechalutz” Mr. M. Boym greets; the League for Working Eretz Israel — Comrade Groyer; “Hashachar” — Berliner; “Herzliya” — Olszewski[?]; “Hitachdut” — B. Lichter; and “Keren Kayemet” — Golberd[?]. Written greetings from the “Gordonia” organisations in the Kresy and the Lublin region are also read out. Comrade Goldberg then lectures on the situation in Zionism, in Eretz Israel and in the “Gordonia” movement. The festive session closes with a “hora” dance and pioneer songs.

Sunday was devoted to ideological matters and practical work.

The 3rd session, which lasted 8[?] hours, considered the position of “Gordonia” in the United Eretz-Israel Workers' Party, the movement's view on the kvutza question and the situation in “Chever Hakvutzot”. The session also dealt with the questions of “Hechalutz”, hachshara and aliyah.

In the discussion, which was lively and serious, many delegates took part, expressing their opinions on the questions raised by the speakers Goldberg and Hampel.

The 4th and last session heard reports of the District Committee and accounts of the individual branches. The reports show that the young organisation “Gordonia” numbers 600 members in Zagłębie; 20 are on hachshara, 40 are preparing in the coming weeks, and 10 comrades are taking part in the current aliyah.

Messrs A. Lichter and Nachum Klarman (Częstochowa) lecture on educational and organisational problems. With the vote on the resolutions and the election of the regional secretariat, which includes Messrs Yitzchak Landger[?], Yitzchak Cohen and Tzvi Kutner, the meeting closes in an elevated mood. All the “Gordonists” present link hands, break into a little dance, and until late at night the singing of “Mi yivne haGalil” and “Olam hafukh” resounds.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Mishpatim, Shekalim)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion.
Collected by Y. L.[?]
Parashat Mishpatim.
—o—
A.
"Now these are the ordinances" (21:1)
At the end of the previous portion [Yitro] it speaks of "gods of silver and gods of gold ye shall not make unto you", and at the beginning of this portion — of ordinances [laws]. The juxtaposition comes to teach that one should not admit rabbis who buy their posts with money.. ("Elohim" — explicitly: rabbis [judges], see further 21:6[?]; so it means: gods of silver — rabbis for money — ye shall not make unto you.)
Baal ha-Turim.
—o—
B.
"If thou buy a Hebrew servant" (21:2)
The ordinances begin with the law of the Hebrew servant, because servitude is the most tragic thing in the legislation[?]: for there is nothing harder for a man than to serve his own equal.
Ibn Ezra.
—o—
C.
"Eye for eye" (21:23 [sic, should be 21:24])
According to the interpretation of the Sages it does not literally mean an eye for an eye in the plain sense of the word, but money: the one who knocks out an eye pays as much as a man's eye is worth.
— Why not simply knock out the criminal's eye in return; why money of all things?
— When someone knocks out his fellow's eye without why and without wherefore, just like that — he is a murderer. And if they rule that his eye be knocked out in return out of revenge, is that payment in like measure[?]? The other knocked out an eye for no reason at all, while from him, the criminal, the eye is put out for a reason: because he did such a thing to the other... Since an evenly weighed revenge ("nikmat ha-shekel") does not exist anyway, let it be the value of the eye: money.
Divrei Shaul.
— A difficulty: from where did the Sages deduce that money is meant and not an eye?
Because it says "ayin tachat ayin" ("eye under/for eye") and not "ayin be'ad ayin". This is to say: "tachat ayin" — the letters following the letters ayin-yod-nun: after the letter ayin comes pe, after yod — kaf, after nun — samekh — that gives: KESEF, money.
The Vilna Gaon.
—o—
D.
"If thou lend money to any of My people" (22:24)
When Dr. T[heodor] Herzl founded the first Colonial Bank [the Jewish Colonial Trust], the Lida rabbi, R' Yaakov Yitzchak [sic, = Yitzchak Yaakov] Reines, said: a Jew is accustomed to put on a girdle [gartl] before a mitzvah and to say "le-shem yichud". A mitzvah that he performs only from year to year — is very precious to him, and he makes greater preparations. And here is a mitzvah that we have not fulfilled for two thousand years: "If thou lend money to My people" — to lend money to the people; so we must perform this mitzvah with great[?] enthusiasm!
—o—
E.
"If thou lend money to any of My people, even to the poor with thee."
All the early commentators [Rishonim] explain: "If thou lend money" — if you lend someone money — "to My people": see that someone be present at the lending, for lending without witnesses is what the Gemara calls "they cry out and are not answered"[?] — one shouts afterwards and gets no answer.. Whereas "the poor" — when you go to give a poor man alms — see that it be "with thee", that you yourself alone be present. Nobody needs to know about it, so that the poor man should not be ashamed.
Korban ha-Shem[?].
— "If thou lend money to My people": if you lend money just like that to all the world, just to the whole people — "the poor with thee": the poor man will go along with you, you will become poor yourself..
Melekhet Machshevet.
—o—
F.
"Neither shall ye lay upon him interest" (23:24 [sic, should be 22:24])
A usurer of olden times, a bloodsucker, died in Posen [Poznań]. The kehilla demanded a very large sum of money from the heirs: what he did not give in his lifetime, let them give after his death. So they did not bury him. The heirs informed on them to the authorities, and Rabbi Akiva Eiger was summoned to the authorities [the "nachalstvo"]. He answered thus: when an ordinary Jew pays for a plot of earth, he pays for no long time, for we hope that we shall rise at the resurrection of the dead, and the plot of earth will become free. A usurer, however, according to Jewish law will not rise at the resurrection of the dead, so he will lie in the earth forever; therefore he must pay many times over...
Heard.
—o—
G.
"Thou shalt not curse a ruler of thy people" (22:27).
"A ruler of thy people" — when[?] you are a nasi, a rabbi — "thou shalt not curse": you should not scold, not be too expansive.
Sifrei Musar [books of ethics].
—o—
H.
"For a bribe blindeth the clear-sighted" (23:8).
A Lithuanian petty rabbi, known for his taking of bribes, became lame in his old age. People wondered: according to the Torah he ought to have gone blind, not lame. Said R' Yoshe Ber [Soloveitchik] about it:
According to the Gemara (Shabbat 113b) one goes blind from too quick steps, from "large strides". Well then, had our little rabbi gone blind straight away, people would say it is because he walks with large strides; but now that he has become lame and so cannot walk fast anyway — now, when he goes blind, everyone will know it is because of his taking bribes.
—o—
I.
"The first of the first-fruits of thy land... Thou shalt not seethe a kid in its mother's milk" (23).
Everyone wonders at the juxtaposition of first-fruits with meat in milk. Rabbi R' Yonatan Eybeschütz said that he had once read in the work of a botanist that there are plants which, if one cooks meat in milk and pours the broth onto the plant, grow fat fruits. That is what the Torah means: that even for the use of the soil one may not cook meat in milk.
—o—
J.
"Keep thee far from a false matter" (23:7).
An author came to the Rabbi of Brisk [Brest] and asked for an approbation. The Rabbi of Brisk looks into the book and sees nothing but false conclusions. But he cannot refuse the author, so he writes a few words of approbation and moves them far away from the text. The author asks: why does the Gaon move the approbation away from the text? In order[?] — he answers — to fulfil "keep thee far from a false matter"...
—o—
Shekalim.
"On the first of Adar they announce concerning the shekels and concerning diverse kinds" (Mishnah Shekalim)
Why are shekels coupled with diverse kinds [kilayim]?
Every Jew gave only half a shekel, to show that each one by himself is nothing: one Jew alone is half a thing; only when he joins the community, when all are united, is it a whole thing. So the meaning of the shekels is — unity. But when the unity has to come about between unequals, between one kind and another, between diverse kinds — then it is better that the union does not come about... Therefore they proclaimed shekels and kilayim together: union is not always desirable.
Rabbi Yonatan Eybeschütz.
What's New in Zagłębie?

[Right date box:] Friday, 30 / 30 Shevat 5690. [Left date box:] Piątek 28 lutego 1930 [Friday, 28 February 1930].
Będzin
—o—
The Water Question Is Settled.
A New "Gift" from Our City Fathers.
At Tuesday's city council session the statute of the waterworks commission was discussed; it set the price at 50 gr. per metre [cubic] of water, with one room consuming 4 metres of water a month, i.e. from a single-room flat the poorest [?] tenant will pay 2 zł. a month for water.
The statute was in fact already settled two weeks ago at the councillors' conferences held at the Magistrat, but only at Tuesday's session was the item adopted in the third reading.
The debate on the question lasted 3 hours; every councillor took pains that the gallery should hear that he alone defends the city's interests, but in the end the Magistrat's proposal was adopted.
Starosta Sends Back the Resigned Community Elders.

Some time ago the members of the kehilla council, Messrs. Ch. Szajn, Sz. Frenkel, G. Rechnic and others, applied to the starosta [district head] that he should respect [?] their resignation as members of the kehilla council.
The starosta sent the resignations back to the kehilla council with the instruction that the council must decide on the matter.
Celebrating Marshal Piłsudski's Name Day.

Under the chairmanship of Dr. Jarzębowski [?] a meeting was held at the starostwo [district office] to create a committee that is to arrange for Marshal Piłsudski's name day to be a festive one.
For this purpose various commissions were elected, such as technical, propaganda etc., in which only the school principal Mr. Rapaport is represented; whereas the finance commission was joined by vice-president Rubinlicht, Izaak Szpigelman and Bażykowski [?].
Are Our Lives Fair Game? So Cry the Merchants of the Old Market.

On Wednesday a group of merchants from the Old Market came to us at the editorial office with the request that we should not again pass over in silence the acts of revenge against those merchants who do not want to be in contact with the "customer-grabbers" (kunim-khapers). Such an act of revenge was carried out on Wednesday against the ready-made clothing merchant Szykman [?], who received a murderous beating from a "grabber".
"Ba-agala" u-vizman kariv...

This week "Grabski's wagon" [the tax-distraint cart] again appeared in the street and paid visits to a series of Jewish merchants, from whom furniture, coats and in general everything that has any value at all was taken away.
A Boxing Section at "Hakoach".

Thanks to the present board of "Hakoach", headed by Dr. Rechtman, a boxing section has been founded.
The board, wishing to give the members a rational and systematic training in this sport, has provided the section with a special trainer, Mr. Szkater [?] of Katowice.
The Competition Is Void — Politics Is What Counts...

Several weeks ago the kehilla board adopted a resolution to publish a competition for a shochet [ritual slaughterer]. As authoritative circles inform us, the shochet is completely superfluous, because the 4 shochtim our kehilla has can perform their duties without any difficulty; but when a new [?] "action" has to be carried through, one does not reckon with logic.
The competition that the holy kehilla published at the time stated that the newly engaged shochet must be 30 years old and possess proper qualifications.
But, as we are informed, the content of the competition will remain in the "historical kehilla archive", and the post of the new shochet has been given to someone whose qualifications and age are in contradiction with the competition...
Dvora Dimant performs — tomorrow.

The recitation evening of the Berlin word-artist Dvora Dimant could not take place on Wednesday for technical reasons, and will be held this Saturday at 2 p.m. at „Nowości“.
The evening has aroused great interest, if only because everyone is curious to hear the artist, who, incidentally, comes from our town.
District conference of „HeHalutz“.

Next week a district convention (kenes mehoz) of „HeHalutz“ of the Zagłębie district, including Częstochowa and Radomsko, will take place. This convention, which was called by the Warsaw Central Committee, will consider the most topical questions of the halutz movement and will also discuss plans for intensified halutz work in our region.
The Warsaw centre (merkaz) as well as delegated members of the Palestinian „Histadrut ha-Ovdim“ will take part in the convention.
Meeting of Upper Silesian traders.

On Sunday, under the chairmanship of Mr. Schnitzer, the general meeting of the section of Upper Silesian traders took place at the „Merchants' Association“ (Sokhrim-Farayn).
The floor for the report is given to the vice-chairman Mr. Seliger, who gives a general survey of the board's activity and sharply criticises Mr. Briner, who disregarded the board's decisions and committed irresponsible acts on his own authority.
The treasury report is given by Mr. Jangster[?], who says that although Mr. Briner received a considerable sum from the board, he nevertheless did not carry out the board's decisions.
Messrs. Herszlikowicz, Izraelewicz, Friedrich, Meitlis and others also take part in the discussion, criticising Mr. Briner. Finally Mr. Briner is given the floor; he does not answer the accusations but only tries to defend himself. Amid shouts of „Down! Away from us“ he ends his defence. A resolution is then adopted: 1) the meeting expresses no confidence in Mr. Briner, and 2) to expel him as a member of the section. Then elections are held, with the following result: Schnitzer, Seliger, Jungster, Meitlis, Friedrich, Danziger, Herszlikowicz.
From the celebration into hospital...

On Katowska[?] a name-day celebration was held at a local Christian family. When the guests were drunk, a brawl broke out among the friends and one of them struck the other with a knife...
The wounded man was taken to the municipal hospital.
Lecture at „Tse'irei Mishmerei ha-Holim“.

Next Sunday Dr. Paul will give a lecture on „Alcoholism“ in the school hall at Kołłątaja 43.
The lecture is organised by „Tse'irei Mishmerei ha-Holim“ (Young Guardians of the Sick).
Sosnowiec — When the gallery got a „tongue“, the kehilla council became powerless...

On Saturday night, under the chairmanship of Mr. L. Szwajcer, a session of the kehilla council took place, which was to determine the new budget. Apart from the parnassim[?], a rich gallery came again this time: representatives of the klei kodesh (religious functionaries) and of various institutions and societies.
The first items, such as pensions, the rabbinate and office employees, were adopted en bloc according to last year's sum. When it came to the pension for the moreh tsedek Halberstam (a son-in-law of R' Itzikl of blessed memory), the chairman wanted to hold a vote on whether the item should remain or be struck out. But here came the outburst[?] of the gallery, which began to storm against the chairman; a tremendous uproar arose, shouting, curses, abuse, and in such a chaotic situation the chairman — despite the opposition of a majority of the parnassim — closed the session.
The further continuation of the „attraction“ was to take place yesterday, Thursday evening.
—o—
The question of a new timetable.
On the 24th of this month a conference was held at the Chamber of Commerce on how to improve the train timetable in the Kielce voivodeship. Delegates of the Warsaw, Radom, Kraków, Katowice and Poznań railway directorates took part in the conference. The memorandum of the Chamber of Commerce was accepted, that from 15 May a direct train from Zagłębie to Kraków be introduced. The travel time to Zakopane and Krynica will also be shortened: instead of 12 hours the journey will last 7 hours.
In summertime the number of trains from Katowice to Ząbkowice will be increased at the hours 7, 8, 13, 14 and from 18—19.
The delegate of the Radom directorate announced that from 15 May the carriages of the night trains will be of the corridor system.
Left a wife in Łódź and married in Sosnowiec.

A few months ago a certain Weingarten came here, a Jew already in his sixties, with a white-grey beard, a ben Torah (learned man) too, and took up selling lottery tickets.
The collector (ticket seller) struck up acquaintance with various people, to whom he apologised for looking „run-down“ because he had no home: if I came across — he said — a decent match, an older woman who has her own flat, I would get married.
Good people are always to be found among our brethren the Children of Israel; it did not take long before they found for the [—][?] poor fellow a suitable match, the woman Chava Barankiewicz, also of the same age...
The match pleased both sides, a wedding took place, even with sheva brakhot, and the old couple lived like two doves...
But the Łódź rabbinate „could not begrudge“ such a little couple living „like God in Odessa“ and wrote here to the Rav R' Yehoshuale Glicksman that So-and-so son of So-and-so had left a wife in Łódź and, according to their information, had married in Sosnowiec.
On receiving such information the Rav R' Yehoshuale informed the shammes R' Yakl Gartman that he should announce it in the synagogue.
R' Yakl went up onto the bimah and announced that the Łódź rabbinate asks anyone who knows whom a certain Weigberg married in Sosnowiec to report it.
— Oy vey — came a cry from the old collector — I know that person, he married Barankiewicz's sister and lives on 3 Maja[?] street.
When the news spread, the „bridegroom“ vanished[?].
And the woman weeps and laments: whom could it have occurred to that such a Hasidic Jew would commit such an evil deed...
—o—
Convention of the small traders' association.
Next Sunday the local Christian Small Traders' Association is calling a convention of all small traders' associations in Zagłębie. The convention will discuss the catastrophic situation of the small traders and various economic questions, and a convention of the Kielce voivodeship is to[?] be set.

The number of unemployed is growing.
On the 22nd of this month the number of unemployed increased by 580 persons. In total there are some 20 thousand unemployed in Zagłębie.
Zawiercie — The "Ahavat Shalom" Synagogue to Be Named after Louis Marshall.

On Sunday the annual general meeting of the "Gemilut Hesed" (free-loan) fund took place here; the fund operates in the building donated by Mr. Wolf Stopnicki. Invited to the meeting was the president of the Sosnowiec free-loan fund, Mr. Leibish Zegrel, who has great merit in the founding of this aid institution. The meeting, chaired by Mr. Zegrel, was exemplary and should serve as a model for other meetings of institutions, which should take from it a lesson in how honest, conscientious people work intensively [?] solely for the good of society.
The report shows that the fund possesses a capital of 16 thousand zł. from collected groszy, and from "rushpings" [?] — 14 thousand zł. Besides this, the management, especially Mr. Yosef Liberman, built a whole storey for the free-loan fund out of various side revenues. After the reports, those assembled did not allow elections to take place, but with great gratitude granted them their continued trust.
A longer discussion developed around the proposal of Mr. Giterman, who had proposed a few weeks ago that the "Ahavat Shalom" synagogue at the free-loan fund be named after Louis Marshall. The proposal was adopted. It was also resolved to immortalize Mr. Stopnicki with a marble tablet and to enrol Mr. Zegrel as an honorary member of the free-loan fund in our town.
This week the management received word from Mr. Giterman that he is sending 400 dollars for the building of the "Ahavat Shalom" synagogue.
Also taking part in the meeting was the treasurer of the Sosnowiec free-loan fund, Mr. Yisroel Mikhl Berkowicz.

Sławków Welcomes Its Rabbi

[Sławków — rabbinate.] In Sławków great disputes took place over the vacant[?] local rabbinate. But with a majority of votes the rabbi of Sirog[?] was elected.
On Tuesday a delegation of Messrs. A. B. Sokolski[?], A. Hercinger[?] and B. M. Rozenberg handed the rabbi of Sirog[?] the letter of appointment (ktav rabbanut) with 130 signatures.
The rabbi, who arrived here with a great parade, drove to the beit midrash, which was decorated with various decorations. He was greeted by: Mr. A. B. Sokolski[?] as representative of the Jewish kehilla, Mr. N. Grosman on behalf of the artisans, Mr. Mendel[?] Sożodski[?] on behalf of the "Agudah". The last also demanded of the rabbi that he found a Shomrei Shabbat [society] and [a branch of] PAI [Poalei Agudat Israel].
The rabbi delivered a sermon and thanked the town for the honour[?].
Cantor H. Fruchtsztajn[?] with the choir sang several chapters of Psalms, and in an elevated[?], enthusiastic mood the rabbi was escorted to his temporary residence.
In the evening the rabbis of Olkusz and Wolbrom came and conducted the din Torah (rabbinical lawsuit) between the former moreh tzedek R' Yosef Lederman, may he live long, and the rabbi. The rabbinical court ruled that the rabbi must give the moreh tzedek 400 złoty as conciliation money.

News of the Week

The Palestine (Eretz Israel) government has approved the new communities (kehillot) law. Men and women over 20 years of age will be allowed to take part in the elections.
—o—
In Russia 2 Jews, leaders of the workers' „krasen“[?] (perhaps: workers' funds), were sentenced to be shot for helping private trade.
—o—
In southern France violent storm winds raged. Many towns and villages were flooded.
—o—
16 March has been fixed as a day of protest of American Jewry against the religious persecutions in Russia.
—o—
During a masked ball in Angers[?] (France) a balcony collapsed. Many people were injured.
—o—
In New York a conference of Polish Jews took place. The conference resolved to turn to the Polish government asking it to grant Jewish citizens equality with non-Jewish ones.
—o—
„The Jazz Singer“ staged by Ida Kamińska.
Lately the Jewish play „The Jazz Singer“ by S. Raphaelson, which depicts the life of a cantor's son as a „jazz singer“, has become very famous on all foreign stages. The play was staged on the English and German stage with enormous success, and its content served as material for the first sound film „The Jazz Singer“ with Al Jolson. Now Ida Kamińska has received the right to perform this play in Yiddish. Ida Kamińska plays „The Jazz Singer“ with a first-class ensemble. The musical illustration was created by the well-known musician Józef Kamiński; the sets were specially painted by the well-known painter Y. Shliwniak[?].
„The Jazz Singer“ will be performed in Będzin, Katowice and Sosnowiec.
Olkusz — From the „Folksbank“

Olkusz.
To the board of the „Folksbank“ (People's Bank) were elected: Berish Heislfish[?] (chairman) and Avromle Banker. To the supervisory council: Adam Blum, Akiva Kazhma[?], Itshl[?] Blumenfrucht, Dr. Y. Kain, Meir Szerman and Yisroel Kajzer.
—o—
From the „Dobroczynność“ [charity society].
On Sunday, 2 March, the „Dobroczynność“ organised a fund-raising drive for the benefit of the society. Taking part in the collection were: Patak, Perlsal[?], Gliksman, Flaszenberg, Mrs. Lender[?] and Mrs. Volpin. In total up to 500 zł was collected.
A ball has been set for 8 March.
It is desirable that the Jewish population support this philanthropic institution, which does a great deal[?] in the present hard times for the poor Jewish population.
A. B.

Purim ball for the Keren Kayemet (JNF).
On Shushan Purim the local JNF (KKL) committee is organising a Purim ball with a very rich programme.
A large number of young people from Będzin and Sosnowiec are preparing for the ball.

Today, Saturday, at half past two in the afternoon („half 3“), a lecture will be held in the premises of the Zionist Organisation in Będzin, Kołłątaja 9, by Miss Magister Albek, who will speak on „The tasks and aims of WIZO“.
The same lecture will take place on Sunday, 9 March, in the premises of the Sosnowiec „Maccabi“.

Meeting of commercial employees.
Next Sunday, the 9th of this month, at 6 o'clock in the evening, a meeting of the trade union of commercial employees in Będzin will take place in the premises of the Right Poalei Zion („P. Ts.“).
—o—
District conference of „HeHalutz“.
The first Zagłębie district convention of „HeHalutz“, which gathers tomorrow and on Sunday in Będzin, has aroused an understandable interest in all local circles. In the secretariat of the Będzin organisation, which has already completed all preparations. Many delegates from 13 towns and hachshara (training) points have registered for the convention, and many guests from the whole region have also ordered entrance tickets.
The festive opening session of the district convention (kenes mehozi), in which Mr. Paluszka[?] on behalf of the C.C. and Messrs. Dvubni[?] and Rozensztajn as representatives of the Palestinian „Histadrut ha-Ovdim“ will take part, will be held tomorrow at 2 o'clock in the afternoon in the „Corso“ cinema, and the other sessions will take place in the premises of „Hitahdut“.
The first session in the theatre hall will be devoted to the 10th anniversary (yahrzeit) of Yosef Trumpeldor and his comrades, who fell heroically in the defence of the Upper Galilee.
