The District Conference of HeHalutz in Będzin

[Będzin — Zionism, HeHalutz.] To the first Zagłębie conference of HeHalutz, convened by the Warsaw Central Committee for 8 and 9 March, came dozens of delegates and guests from all of Zagłębie as well as from Zawiercie, Częstochowa and Radomsko. The festive opening session, dedicated to the memory of Joseph Trumpeldor on his 10th yahrzeit, took place in the "Kursal". Even before the appointed time the theatre hall filled with hundreds of young people, who sang Hebrew songs until the presidium arrived.
At 8 in the evening the stage is opened, decorated with the pictures of A. D. Gordon, Borochov and Trumpeldor, the Będzin HeHalutz committee and the representatives of the Central Committee and of the "Histadrut ha-Ovdim", Messrs. Lewite and Paluska. The gathering is opened with "Hatikvah". The chairman of the Będzin HeHalutz, Mr. M. Hampel, delivers the opening speech in the name of the organizing committee. The speaker [?] talks about the August events in Palestine, to which the pioneering youth reacted with an intensified aliyah. He speaks about the historic mission of the Jewish worker in Palestine, and at the end of his speech Mr. Hampel gives a description of Trumpeldor's pioneering activity (the assembled honour Trumpeldor's name by rising).
Then come greetings. In the name of the League for Labour Palestine Mr. Baum greets; the Zionist Organization — Mr. Brassa [?]; Poalei Zion — Gutman; "WIZO" — Mrs. Goldsztajn; Keren Kayemet — Mr. Berliner; "Gordonia" — Kutner; "Hashomer Hatzair" — Mr. Landa; "Freiheit" — S. Gutman; "Hashachar" — Grauer; "Herzliya" — Miss Langer; Association of Commercial Employees — Mr. Cukierkandel. A written greeting from "Tarbut" is also read out.
After the greetings the floor goes to the guests Paluska and Lewite, who describe the hard and serious hour, the situation in Zionism after the latest events, and sharply condemn the Revisionists as the "genius politicians" of yesterday [?], gravely [?], as well as the Zionist liquidators of "Brit Shalom". The speakers talk about Trumpeldor's life and achievements for Labour Palestine and call on the Jewish youth to rally around the banner of HeHalutz.
The opening is concluded with the singing of the "Internationale".
The second session took place in the premises of "Hitachdut" with the participation of 250 registered members, and was devoted to ideological questions and problems of the Palestine labour movement. Mr. Lewite gives an introduction to a members' discussion on the subject "The social foundations of the Palestinian working class". The speaker talks about the creative [?] power of the Palestinian worker and the pioneering aliyot; he speaks about the greatest work of the Jewish working class — the "Histadrut ha-Ovdim", about the various forms of colonization, and about the union of the two parties "Ahdut ha-Avoda" and "Hapoel Hatzair".
A lively, interesting discussion developed around these questions. Taking part in the debate were M. Hampel, Kakatek (Będzin), Dzialowski [?] (Częstochowa), Intraligater [?] (Sosnowiec), Lustiger (Dąbrowa), Liberman (Radomsko) and others.
The other sessions dealt with practical work. Reports are given by the HeHalutz branches in Zagłębie. It turns out that HeHalutz has grown stronger in our region.
With the election of a district committee, whose seat was fixed in Będzin, and with some resolutions greeting "Mifleget Poalei Eretz Israel" [Mapai] and calling on the halutzim in Zagłębie to stand ready for the call of the "Histadrut ha-Ovdim", the conference is closed to the strains of "Hatikvah" and the Internationale.
In an elevated mood and under the general impression that the district conference will be a driving force for intensive pioneering work in our corner, the delegates disperse to their towns, full of impressions of the successful two-day conference.

From 10 o'clock in the morning on, Jewish "cavalrymen" rode through the town and visited the rabbi and the town notables. The Będzin Credit Bank Sets About Building Its Own Premises

[Będzin — economy, cooperative bank.]
On Sunday the annual general meeting of the Credit Bank in Będzin took place in the hall of the "Będzin Merchants' Association". The meeting aroused great interest among the members, who came not for the sake of opposition, not for the sake of criticism, but to express their recognition of the leadership and the management, which has brought the institution to its present high standing.
On behalf of the supervisory board the meeting was opened by the director, Mr. S. Tenenbaum, who gave a long and businesslike opening speech, in which he touched on the following questions:
1) the present severe crisis for the merchants, and the fatherly relief they have received at the cooperative bank; and he stressed that when the members have the same earnest attitude toward the bank that the bank has toward the members, the institution will develop still further and will bring benefit for the members and for the whole Jewish community.
In the further part of his speech Mr. T. voices a protest against:
1) the new "bankomania" disease: instead of strengthening and securing the already existing funds, every party circle founds its own separate "little banks"; and
2) against the persons who make use of public money, with whose help a network of private little shops is being created.
The chair is handed over to Dr. H. Lewin [?].
Assessors: Szmul Piekarski and Szmul Krakowski; secretary — Moszel Preger.
The report on the management's activity in the year 1929 is delivered by the vice-president, Mr. Rubinlicht. He speaks of the bank's success in all fields and presents the following figures: in the course of the year the number of members rose from 361 to 437; shares from 68 thousand zł. to 107 thousand zł.; bills of exchange from 290 thousand zł. to 600 thousand zł. The bank had a turnover of 136 million zł.; net profit 51,000 zł.
On behalf of the supervisory board Mr. M. Galer [?] reports. It is not the dry figures — he says — that prove the bank's high standing, but something else: the secret is that the bank is a communal institution and always cares for its members. Mr. G. points to the good management and above all to the fact that neither members of the management nor of the supervisory board benefit from the bank's credits.
After Mr. Tenenbaum reads out the reports of the audit commission and of the Audit Union in Poland, a "discussion" develops. In the "discussion" only Mr. M. M. Zaks takes part; he says that the large profit is due to the bank charging high interest.
To the criticism Mr. Rubinlicht replies, explaining that the interest rate at the Bank Kredytowy is lower than at all the local banks.
Mr. Zaks regrets it and withdraws his criticism.
All reports are approved without discussion, and the meeting expresses its confidence in the management, and in the director, Mr. Tenenbaum, in particular.
The profit of 51 thousand zł. is, by majority decision, assigned to the reserve capital.
A longer discussion develops over the proposal that the bank should build a building of its own. The proposal is presented by Mr. Majek Szajn, who argues that the bank must have property so that the members with deposits can be secure about their capital.
The proposal is supplemented by Messrs. Tenenbaum and Rubinlicht; the latter points out that by law one third of the assets must be in real property. It is unanimously resolved that the management should carry out the proposal and begin building as soon as possible.
After the budget for 1930 was fixed at 72 thousand zł., it was resolved: 1) that a member may receive credit of up to 20 thousand zł., and 2) that the bank may take on credit obligations of up to 2 million zł.
The elections brought no change. By acclamation the same [officers] remained as until now.
Let the Prestige Be Saved!

(The city fathers. — The water question. — The Jewish people's delegates. — How to crawl out of the ugly situation.)
So the water question in Będzin is settled. The city administration's proposal that it should cost 50 gr. per [cubic] metre was adopted in the third reading, and there is nothing more to debate about the question.
To tell you the truth, we could in the end have accepted this price only on the condition that we had a meter or some other kind of measure with which one could measure the actual consumption of water. But we have heard that the most important thing is that consumption should be at a maximum, because the more water the city consumes, the smaller the amount will be; and therefore it has to be arranged so that every household needs 4 metres of water, which comes to 240 buckets [„wiadra“] a month. It goes without saying that this is an impossibility; but one could have overlooked such a lump sum [„ryczałt“] if the price had been considerably cheaper. The magistrate, however, did not want to give way [?] either on the price or on the norm. Such „taking of the measure“ means beating the population with two sticks, since it is out of the question that one should consume so much water, and the measure could only have been got around either through the price or through the quantity of water.
With all that, one must not forget that the magistrate deserves a „yasher koach“ for this: after all, it feels the burdens of the citizens, otherwise it could have made it all considerably more expensive, and that too would have been fine, for who knows better than they that what they do is done, what they want to push through is pushed through; they administer and rule in the city, and nobody says that it must and can be otherwise, that it must and can be done differently — and so it really would have been lost had they calculated it all more dearly.
Interesting, therefore, is the city council meeting of Wednesday a week ago [?], at which the final settlement of the water question was on the agenda: precisely this meeting was missed by about half of the Jewish councillors. Evidently, for our city fathers the matter is a side issue on which it is not worth spending an evening, and indeed they took it lightly, so it went through as the magistrate wanted.
And here the question arises: why did we send them there as our delegates? Why did we elect them? Why did they accept the mandates, once they knew that they do not want to, or cannot, be people's representatives? After all, the municipal economy is a huge apparatus which burdens the inhabitants, so that with the help of this apparatus life can be made easier or harder; one cannot reckon with our city council representatives happening to come to a meeting or happening not to be there. An economic order cannot exist or manage on chance.
Here one sees the failure the city has suffered when its representatives look at serious questions with indifference and apathy. And when one sees [?] that at the meeting, on such a question, so many representatives are absent — and precisely from the strata for whose voters the decision is of first-class importance — it follows of itself that the matter must be conducted on one foot [hastily]; and so the question was indeed settled: they approved what they wanted and were done with it — who is going to play with such trifles, who is going to get into discussions about the water question, which has to be approved as quickly and as well as possible.
It was truly a disgrace and a shame to watch how the meeting was conducted then, how the Jewish councillors who were present bit and tore at one another, cursed and quarrelled, so that the Christian neighbours sat quietly and watched the comedy. They took great pleasure in the dialogues and amused themselves splendidly; otherwise they would not have sat quietly, otherwise they would have shown that we can pay whatever it may be, while they cannot pay even a minimum.
Whoever was at the meeting on Wednesday and watched how Jews insult one another before the eyes of their Christian colleagues, who smiled contentedly [?] — those who felt and lived through all this could grasp what is meant by public pain, public humiliations [?], public brokenness, public lack of upbringing, immaturity.
Do our representatives really think that they are responsible to no one and for nothing? Do they not know that public delegates are responsible to the community, and every mistake caused by them is a harm to the community and to the interests of the people? By now they might have acquired a little routine, they might have taken a different view of public life. One must learn something, one must go forward, one must progress. If one wants to be a public representative in the twentieth century, one cannot keep going backwards like this all the time; and when our representatives conduct themselves in such a way that they take no account of anyone, the city suffers from it: on the one hand it costs the inhabitants' pockets, and on the other the people are not recognised as conscious representatives who are called to represent the local inhabitants.
It is out of the question that the people should regard such representatives as level-headed, conscious and shrewd delegates to whom we could entrust our problems.
How can the people entrust its local interests to such delegates, who do not care what our fate will look like? How can we have confidence in people who come to the meetings by chance, and hardly [„kum“, for „koym“] are they there — they are not in the proper mood; self-government does not interest them at all, and then one does not even try to think about which questions have been put on the agenda.
That is the chaos [„tohu va-vohu“] in which our self-government representatives, our city fathers, live. It is unheard of that people should take so little account of their prestige, should not weigh what mission they have taken upon themselves. From the moment they became representatives of this or that trend, of this or that party, people must after all know that they are responsible for their deeds, and that a time will come when the voters will come to their delegates and demand that they show what was done for the people during such-and-such a time, during such-and-such a period.
Had the representatives been level-headed people's representatives, they would have known that an end must be made once and for all, that one cannot always make so many mistakes.
It would after all be fair that people should come to [see] what [?; „tsu vaser“] is not in order; one cannot always live and carry on public activity in such a way. There must after all be a change [?], otherwise the population suffers, otherwise the people lose their authority as people's delegates, as representatives of those who sent them there to run the communal economy.
After all, care must finally be taken to find a way out of the terrible mess, bound up with intrigues and personal accounts, from which their Christian colleagues derive satisfaction.
Perhaps it would be right to sit down and think how to put an end to all that brings us shame, pain and humiliations, while we suffer economically at every step.
If one sat down seriously and sincerely to deal with the question, one would no doubt find a way out. And once one is convinced [?] of this — there is no doubt about it, and there are no two opinions.
Let us therefore try to save the prestige, which keeps [?] falling ever deeper.
Selekt.
Interviews with the Heroes of the Megillah

[Purim — satirical feuilleton.]
A. Lemech.
I received an assignment from the Mr. Editor to interview a series of prominent personalities who once played a first-rank role in the Persian kingdom. As I was informed later, these distinguished persons (for some incomprehensible reason) long ago left the Persian residence of Shushan and now enjoy the right of asylum on heavenly territory.
When I heard that this territory bears the name "the World of Truth" (olam ha-emes), all my desire to travel there vanished, for what could be more terrible for a person like me (a newspaperman, and a feuilletonist to boot) than the ugly word "truth"? But the editor's word cannot be refused — lost cause.
My first visit is to the consulate of the heavenly land, or as it is called, the "Chevra Kadisha", and an official (none other than R' Yedidya himself) informs me that entry into his country is entirely free of passport and visa; on the contrary, from there hundreds of thousands of invitations are still sent out day after day all over the world, emigrants are begged to come, and are even dragged there by force. For this purpose a special official is even employed, who bears a very drastic name: "the Angel of Death".
I provide[—] myself with provisions for the journey and [—]-clothes (exactly the way the government usually fulfils the promised tax relief), board the famous aeroplane "Journalistic Fantasy", and in an instant I am already standing before the heavenly border guard. Two flaming-fiery angels stand on guard, letting through thousands upon thousands of newly arrived emigrants wrapped in shrouds; two roads lead from the guard post: to the right into Paradise, to the left into Gehenna. Dazzling white little angels and black demons receive their guests. I also noticed a large return migration: many are sent back, little demons whip them along: back into the earthly hell, back to be reincarnated, "proshen gazar"[?].. (Since then it has become clear to me where so many truth-preachers among us come from — they are the ones driven back from the World of Truth.)
Looking at my journalist's card, they immediately wanted to show me the way left to Gehenna, the proper place for a writer... But I explained that I am only a tourist and that my only purpose is to visit the Paradise resident Mordecai the Righteous. A young little angel politely seats me in a lift.
A short while later I stand before a splendid little palace of pure gold, and in front hangs a small sign: "Mordecai the Righteous and Esther".
I knock and the door opens; before me, on a purple-and-gold armchair, sits a grey-haired[?] rabbi, and beside him on a Persian divan sits Esther with a royal crown of diamonds on her head.
— Aha — R' Mordecai's bony voice greets me — surely[?] from the World of Falsehood (alma de-shikra); I recognise it by the bowing; only they bow to one another[?], bow their heads supposedly for politeness' sake, while in their hearts each would like to level the other with the ground.
— But excuse me, R' Mordecai, where do you get such talk? As far as I know, you were not far from the Agudist method of crawling on all fours before the lord squire: after all, you adjured Esther, for God's sake, not to tell Ahasuerus that she is a "Żydówka" [a Jewess], not to betray her stock and people. You were always pushing about at "the king's gate", by the door — not, God forbid, inside; there they don't let in even a Jew-boy of their own.. You crawled among the "money-officers" [shotrei kesef], among the cabinet bigwigs, and wanted to accomplish something with them for the good of the Jews.
— True — R' Mordecai smiles — back then I was afraid to start up with Ger [the Gerer Rebbe], like a young rabbi.. So I was forced to go their ways, I had to dance after them the "Ma Yafit" dance. But I soon freed myself from their influence, and to atone for my earlier sins I made a point of hanging about before Haman's eyes and put on a proud face, and when everyone fell bowing before the wicked villain, I "neither rose nor stirred". From all sides they raised an alarm against me that, like Grünbaum, I was bringing danger upon the people, that with my "impudent" conduct I was slamming shut all the doors to understanding, that I was a traitor (you can see all these expressions in the "Togblat") — but my method is what brought the great victory. With a dignified head one can defeat even a Haman.
— Excuse me, Rabbi Mordecai, as I see you are well acquainted with Agudah affairs, so be so kind as to give your opinion on the peace between Ger and Aleksander that was concluded at the disarmament conference in Warsaw.
— I know about it. The "Heavenly Courier" gave an exact report. My opinion is that this peace has the meaning that stands in the Megillah: "words of peace and truth". "Words of peace" — talk, one talks about peace, but "and truth" — truth is already something else..
Wishing to snatch a flirt with the charming[?] Esther, I ask her:
— With what, if I may ask, did you so take Ahasuerus's fancy? After all, you are no beauty (on the World of Falsehood I could have got something for such a word.) In the Talmud you are called "yerakrokes", greenish — so what is the secret of your success?
— Hush... she smiles — I will tell you, it is of no use to me anyway today.. The secret of my success was: "Esther did not tell" (ein Ester magedes). When the old fool fawned on me: "Do you love me?" — I don't answer, I wrinkle my little nose[?]. "Who are you, pretty girl?" — again he is left without an answer, I shrug my shoulders. "Esther did not tell" — Esther does not answer. I play on his nerves, and with that success is assured..
Again I talked the old fool into believing that the viceroy Haman and all the general-satraps were casting an eye on me, and when Haman fell at my feet seeking rescue, I told him a story that he wants "to force the queen", that he wants to kiss me, and I supposedly beg him for protection — those are the charms for success...
We take our leave.
I ask an angel on duty about Ahasuerus. He is in the Gehenna for fools — that is the information I get. Curious what such a Gehenna can look like, I hurry there. In a big hall, on a burning floor, fools with calf faces are wandering about, Ahasuerus too, who strolls about with his Vashti, with a horn on his forehead. I ask:
— If you love your Vashti so much, why did you kill her?
— To blame for that are the "knowers of the times" (as it says in the Megillah) — the newspaper experts; they needed the scandal as a sensation for their newspapers. The editors Carshena, Schiper (Shethar) and Dererliger[?] (Admatha) egged me on. Oh, these newspaper people!
— And who gave the plan to gather all the Persian beauties into the royal palace?
— The young officials picked out for themselves the spectacle of gathering all the beauties into the royal palace. A real[?] delight they had of it!..
— Tell me, why did you issue a law about a tax on "the isles of the sea"?
— Because taxes are in the category of "all the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full" — everything goes in as into a sea, and the sea is not full...
From there I dash into the Gehenna for enemies of the Jews. There I see Haman hanging with his jewels.
— Haman! — how would you, as Persian premier, put together a cabinet today?
— The cabinet would consist as follows: Dalphon — finance minister, Parshandatha — justice minister, Vajezatha — well, he no longer lacks for posts. First of all he is due the portfolio of education minister, but he would probably choose to be a Sejm deputy.
— What greetings do you send to your spiritual grandchildren: the swastika-men, the "Razumaoykes"[?], the Cuzists?
— Tell them that I, the first Haman, did not have any excess of luck either..
Dr. Yehoshua Thon

(On today's jubilee of his 60th birthday)
About our leader Dr. Yehoshua Thon [Ozjasz Thon] a whole work, and a great work, should and must be written.
Dr. Thon — the great Talmudic scholar, the deep thinker and philosopher, the communal activist and politician, the classic publicist and famous orator.
Dr. Thon — the father, the brother, the great, warm Jewish heart, the people's fighter for the idea of national consciousness.
Dr. Thon — the collaborator of Theodor Herzl, Ahad Ha'am, Nordau, Wolffsohn, Marmorek, and now the right hand of Prof. Weizmann and Nahum Sokolow. Dr. Thon — the educator of the present young generation, the fighter for the living Hebrew language and literature, who can look with pride upon his fruits. All this on the greatest scale, all with the deepest honesty and soul, for his soul is deep, very deeply unfolded[?] and rooted in the soul of his poor, oppressed people. Dr. Thon is therefore everywhere much beloved, respected and highly esteemed, not only among Polish Jewry and in the high government circles, but also abroad, in the great wide world — "on the four corners of the earth". Wherever the great fighter comes into contact with any society and spheres whatsoever, everywhere he finds the hearts: among friends and strangers, among supporters and opponents, because his "weapon", his noble arms, with which he fights tirelessly, here and there and at all times, are his sure, fine tact, his wisdom and his spirit-rich reflections.
For the oppressed masses in general and for the Jewish people in particular, Dr. Thon is the warm-hearted, good father, — a father who with his love draws the child to himself. He is the good brother who cheers, who awakens and gives everyone confidence and comfort for life, for national life. He is also the good comrade who feels the troubles and sufferings of every single individual and rejoices in his joy.
And because of this the Jewish people came to love him, nestled close to him as to a true father and protector, because he feels and speaks to his people in its language and with the soul of its folk-spirit, because he is the outstanding connoisseur of Jewish folklore, because he himself is a piece of the people.
All this must be collected and described for our generation and for the coming generations. It is not possible in a newspaper article to enumerate all his deeds and merits for the Jewish people in general and for Polish Jewry in particular. That we must leave to the future biographer, to the historian, who will precisely research and describe the greatness of this genius, Dr. Yehoshua Thon.
Therefore we rejoice in today's festival on account of his 60th birthday; we rejoice and are proud that in our midst there is such a lofty spirit, such a personality and people's fighter as Dr. Yehoshua Thon.
As gratitude for his holy[?] merits and self-sacrifice, Polish Jewry in particular will always stand at the disposal of his call, in order to fight together for our cause, for our holy idea. And when we celebrate Dr. Thon's birthday today, we celebrate our national idea.
Józef Perlberger.
Kraków, Adar 5690.
The Secret of Our Existence

Dr. A. Jacobi (Jerusalem).
"And Haman said unto King Ahasuerus: There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of thy kingdom"
(Book of Esther 3:8)
"Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan."
(Book of Esther 4:16)
The two verses quoted above accompany the fate of the Jewish people. In the course of thousands of years we have constantly heard the "And Haman said", that we are "a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed", a scattered and spread-out people among the other nations of the world, that we are an unwanted element in all corners and parts of the globe. The concluding thought of this was: "therefore it profiteth not the king to suffer them" — it is not worth letting us live. The fate of our history has repeated itself again and again; Haman's "Torah" has remained for generations, and with the pretext "a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed" we have always been persecuted.
But in the very same place in the Megillah we find the secret of our existence: "Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan" — go, gather together all Jews. When the Hamans come and reproach us with our dispersion and scatteredness, when they invent blood libels against us and decide to destroy us, then let us remember the symbol of unity, the "Go, gather", and that will guard us from all evil. This very secret of existence has remained with us as a rule throughout our long life in exile.
A hard trial our small Yishuv in Eretz Israel had to endure in the course of the last half-year, chiefly in the sad days of August–September [the 1929 riots]. A certain part of the children of Ishmael wanted to carry out Haman's "Torah": "to destroy, to slay and to cause to perish all the Jews" who are in the country. But then the whole Yishuv stood up against them as one man. The command "Go, gather" had not yet been issued, but everyone gathered of their own accord and showed the enemy our unity.
We have again shown the world the secret of our existence, and a new chapter of self-sacrifice and heroism has been inscribed in our sorrowful history. We have shown that we bear with dignity the heritage of the Hasmoneans, that we are faithful followers of the Maccabees.
What have we learned from the events in Eretz Israel? What changes do we notice here in the course of the last half-year? One thing must be stressed here most sharply: we have penetrated still more deeply into the meaning of unity. I want to underline here an important episode.
In the first months of the Arab boycott, when Jewish industry in Tel Aviv went through hard weeks and months of crisis because no orders flowed in from Syria and Transjordan, in that hard time the Jewish manufacturers nevertheless did not stop their activity, so that the workers would not lose their livelihoods and employment. The manufacturers thereby rendered a great service to the honour of the Jewish people and to our political situation. Had there then been unemployment in the country because of the boycott, it would have had a bad effect not only economically but chiefly politically. Such an act of Jewish solidarity deserves[?] to be recorded!
And it is worth dwelling on yet another important phenomenon. As is known, the old Jewish colonists of Eretz Israel had always fought against the principle of "Hebrew labour", and an Arab worker who let his labour go cheaper by one piastre got preference over a Jewish worker. After the last sad events, the conservative elements too have realised that "Hebrew labour" is no empty phrase to be scorned — and they have changed their old opinions. Today there is no longer any struggle over this question. The principle of unity, of "Go, gather", has triumphed again!
One of the most important questions in Eretz Israel today is the land question. It is not true, as some maintain, that a difficulty has arisen in buying land. True, we have lately acquired a serious competitor in this field, namely the Armenian Patriarchate; but as far as our land purchase is concerned, precisely after the events in Eretz Israel large tracts of land were offered to us for purchase. Unfortunately we could not make use of the offer, because the Keren Kayemeth LeIsrael did not have the necessary funds for it. Moreover, one cannot yet speak of new purchases as long as we still have to pay off our old obligations.
Eretz Israel stands and now calls to the Jewry of the whole world: "Go, gather together all the Jews". Gather together, all Jews, around the building of the Land, and collect the necessary funds for it. Remember the blessed day, the miracle of Purim, the unity — which is the secret of our existence. The Yishuv risked its life to defend Jewish honour; that honour we now possess. But honour cannot hold on a weak foundation. The foundation of a people is its land. When we possess the land, then, despite all difficulties, despite all disturbances — "we will arise and build"..
Poland at the Leipzig Fair

[Poland — economy, Leipzig Fair.]
For the first time since the new Polish state came into being, Poland is represented with a national exhibition of its own at the greatest world fair, in Leipzig.
The Polish Consul General in Leipzig, Dr. Jerzy Adamkiewicz, today invited your correspondent to see him and asked him to pass on to the Polish-Jewish press the report on the first Polish exhibition in Leipzig.
Relations between Poland and Germany are improving from day to day. The trade agreement, which for the time being is only a provisional one, brings benefit to both states, and it is to be hoped that the great agreement, which will surely soon be concluded, will be of very great benefit both to Poland and to Germany.
Last year Germany supplied various products to Poland to the value of 450 million German marks. In the same period Poland shipped to Germany about 410 million German marks' worth. One sees, then, that both countries are able to export quite large quantities of products which are very necessary to both countries.
The present exhibition is to make clear to the great international mercantile world which products Poland is able to export and which products Poland needs from abroad.
Poland wishes first and foremost to export all kinds of products coming from the animal world, namely: live and dead domestic animals, poultry, butter, eggs, hides, smoked meat, furs, feathers and the like. Besides that[?] Poland is also able to export all kinds of agricultural products, such as: grain, beans, peas, turnips/beets, potatoes and all sorts of vegetables, hops, flax, fruit etc.
On the other hand, Poland urgently needs the various industrial articles which are made so beautifully in Germany and throughout the world.
All this has led Poland now, for the first time, to decide to step out with its products beyond the narrow bounds of its own land and to show the great world what it possesses.
The beauties of Poland's cities and spas, too, are to prove in pictures and displays that in this respect, too, Poland does not fall short of the other tourist countries.
The State Export Institute of the Warsaw central government has also assembled at the exhibition the finest and best that Poland can produce, and the exhibition is surely suited to bringing Poland closer to large-scale export.
A special section also shows the varied Polish folk art, from primitive handicrafts to the finest artistic creations in all fields of art.
In general one can say that this exhibition, which for the time being is only a trial and is still to be expanded, is a very successful one.
Z. Haber.
Leipzig, 3 March 1930.
Evening Courses for Illiterates at the Artisans' Association in Będzin (Impressions of a Visit)

[Będzin — education, Artisans' Association.]
As is known, the Artisans' Association in Będzin organized evening courses for craftsmen quite some time ago. I was therefore curious to see how our Reb Moshes and Reb Chaims — craftsmen of 50—60 years — are learning to write.
Coming one evening into the large, warm and brightly lit halls of the Będzin Artisans' Association, I was enveloped by a warm feeling, seeing how old Jews with grey beards sit around tables and sweat with great diligence over an "elementarz" [primer]. The teacher draws a letter on the "tablica" [blackboard], and the crowd of "big schoolchildren" strive in every way to copy the letter into the exercise book as beautifully and artfully as possible. On the furrowed[?] and wrinkled faces one sees a kind of scholars' rivalry; each wants to outdo the other in "education"...
The head of the Artisans' Association, Councillor Mr. Klajman, seeing my enthusiasm, agreed to give me some information about the organization and development of the evening courses.
"Pupils," he says, "there are 113; they are divided into two groups: those who cannot write at all and those who can already do something. Each group has its own teacher. Lessons take place four times a week."
After the lessons ended I struck up a conversation with the "pupils". To my question how the learning was going for them, they expressed great regret that the courses had not started several years ago, because — they say — "we would already today be able to read and write like all educated people." Some even remarked jokingly that they could already have been doctors and lawyers. In any case one sees that their faces are radiant with great joy and that the undertaking of the Będzin Artisans' Association is a complete success.
It is worth noting further that the evening courses are entirely free of charge, and the pupils even receive the writing materials and books free from the Artisans' Association.
Taking leave of the "pupils", I promised them that I would express in the columns of this newspaper, in their name, the heartiest yasher koach [well done] to the board of the Artisans' Association in Będzin for its cultural work among the broad masses of hard-working craftsmen, and special thanks to Councillor Mr. Klajman for giving me exhaustive information about the evening courses.
The broader public has a duty to support this very important undertaking of the Będzin Artisans' Association morally as strongly as possible.
A Curious One.
Czeladź Has Two Town Councils

(A monologue by one who is not drunk).

...Ha! Today, you say, is Purim? Don't believe it, you needn't believe it. I say that for me, for you and for all of us yesterday was Purim, today is Purim, tomorrow will be Purim. We have Purim all year round; everything and anything is Purim-like. It is Purim-like in trade — Purim-like merchants with Purim-like bills of exchange that only the Vayzathas pay...
Here we have a town council where Purim plays are staged all year: Haman settles himself comfortably in the magistrate's box and the little Vayzathas fill the presidium. Even Queen Esther cannot overcome Haman; she has already turned to the little Vayzathas to set conditions, not to carry out Haman's plans, but Vayzatha stays Vayzatha — they hand him a portion of what is left over from Ahasuerus's feasts, and Vayzatha rolls about with delight...
Purim won its greatest victory in the credit cooperative: the little Purim-banks are fruitful and multiply, the Ahashteranim conduct audits and write good tidings into Ahasuerus's Auditing Union.
This winter I became a “guild-registered” [cechowy] drunkard; I registered with the magistrate, with the województwo, but everywhere it is Purim-like. Yes, my guild, your guild, their guild — a Purim play! My brother is a “radny” [councillor] in the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce — look at him and you will see what a Purim-player he is!
Chałupnicy [home workers], manufacturers, house-owners, socialists, Polish-speaking Yiddishists, Tarbutists, all kinds of “-ists” — cursed Purim-players, stop it with your song:
All festivals will pass away, only Purim will remain — the Purim-players will never disappear, the Vayzathas are fruitful and multiply, and therefore the festival of Purim is the greatest festival; so let us raise a glass
— L'chaim!
Ma ka mashma lan? (What does it tell us?)

(A parody composed on a session of the Sosnowiec kehilla council).

“Ma ka mashma lan” [Aramaic: “what does it teach us?”] — the kehilla?
What does it give me to hear?
Benches thrown, slaps and curses,
Inkwells flying at the foreheads.

And they get heated and they boil,
And one is bored stiff by the debates,
And when it comes to the share-out
They curse each other's fathers' fathers...

“Ma ka mashma lan” — the speeches?
What do they give me to hear?
Old smells from bygone days
With a very heavy stench.

And the “gallery” shouts and clamours,
Lightning flashes from the eyes,
And people hold their sides
As the parnassim tell street jokes...

“Ma ka mashma lan” — the dozór [kehilla board]?
What does it give me to hear?
Sticky, tedious sermons from which
Anyone could go mad.

It is a wound-up contraption,
It has no sense, no feelings;
When the hour comes, it must babble
Against its will, against its wish...

In Honour of Purim — interpretations, quips and remarks on the Scroll of Esther

[Purim — witticisms and Torah remarks on the Scroll of Esther.] Interpretations, quips and remarks on the Scroll of Esther.
Collected and edited by Y. L.
—o—
A. — "For this deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all women, so that they shall despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall be reported... Likewise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day" (1:17–18)
The meaning of Memucan's[?] words is: the women of the common people will say to their husbands: "You see: King Ahasuerus had his queen Vashti summoned to him, and she did not want to come — see how much importance men have"... Whereas the ladies of Persia and Media, the aristocrats of high society, where one does not scold in plain language but diplomatically, etc.[?]... will say to their husbands only: "this day" — "Do you remember such-and-such a date?" — the day of Vashti's refusal to carry out the king's command? More than that they will not say, only hint...
Sichat Chulin ("idle talk").
—o—
B. — "There was a certain Jew in Shushan the palace" (2:5)
"There was a certain Jew in Shushan the palace" — was there really only one Jew in Shushan the palace?!
— There were many, but they all hid at home and guarded their own interests; only Mordecai was the one in Shushan the palace who stood on guard, ready to help every Jew, and did not shut himself up within his own four cubits.
Yaarot Devash.
—o—
C. — "Now when every maid's turn was come... Now when the turn of Esther was come" (2:12–15)
On the words "Now when the turn of Esther was come" — [the cantillation marks are] munach, munach. The other girls ran (kadma ve-azla — hurried and went) — a small matter, to be the king's wife! Esther, however, went reluctantly (munach, munach — calmly, slowly), against her will, because only to save her people did she offer herself as a sacrifice, a sacrifice.
The Vilna Gaon.
—o—
D. — "And the thing was known to Mordecai" (2:22)
According to the midrash, Bigthan and Teresh spoke between themselves in an old, extinct[?] language, so that no one would understand that they were poisoning the king; but Mordecai understood the language.
It is told that when Moses Montefiore was in Poland, a Hasidic delegation presented itself to him, with Rabbi Yitzhak of Warka (of blessed memory) at its head. Montefiore debated with the rebbes about the Hasidim's negative attitude to secular studies and used the above-mentioned midrash to prove that Mordecai the Righteous, too, had mastered many foreign languages.
"On the contrary," the Warka rebbe answered, "that is proof that Jews never learned foreign languages; for had they done so, it would surely have occurred to Bigthan and Teresh that Mordecai would understand them, they would have been on their guard against him, and the miracle would not have happened. It follows that Jews need not know foreign languages."
Heard.
—o—
E. — "But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence" (3:5)
Why "Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him"? Did Haman himself not see that Mordecai did not bow to him? Why did anyone have to speak to him about it?
As the midrash says, Haman wore an idol (cross) over his heart. Many said that Mordecai's not kneeling before Haman was because of the idol. So Haman deliberately took the idol off — and Mordecai still did not kneel before him. Then Haman became convinced that only motives of national dignity were at play here. "But Mordecai bowed not." That Mordecai would not bow down before him, and not because of the idol — this he could no longer bear, this he could no longer endure.
Rishon le-Zion.
—o—
F. — "Then was Haman full of wrath" (ibid.)
On this verse, about Haman's anger, Rashi says nothing — for what does Rashi care that Haman is angry?
Folk saying.
—o—
G. — "There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples" (3:8)
When they are "one people", united, there is discord among the nations; but when the Jews become fragmented and split, then all the nations become united — to do the Jews harm.
Sefarim (books).
—o—
H. — "To destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish... in one day" (3:13)
Why did Haman want to destroy the Jews in a single day? A slaughter of many days would surely have been much more expedient for his devilish[?] plan.
Haman knew that he was dealing with Jews, and he reckoned with the possibility that the Jews would come out the victors; then, he knew, the Jews would make a holiday commemorating their victory over their enemies. Haman was such a villain that he begrudged the Jews a long celebration; therefore his slaughter plan was for one day only, so that if the Jews won, their holiday too would last no more than one day... That's what you call a villain!...
Shema Shlomo.
—o—
I. — "Go, gather together all the Jews" (4:16)
"Go, gather together all the Jews" — assemble all the Jews, unite them in closed ranks — that is the one and only means of rescue in a time of trouble.
R. Yonatan Eybeschütz.
—o—
J. — "And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children" (5:11)
The rebbe R. Hershl was once told, as a little boy, to ask a question on the spot and to give an answer from elsewhere in the Scroll.
Says he: it is written "And Haman told them of the multitude of his children" — Haman told his wife Zeresh about his many children. Didn't she know? There you have a first question.
And the answer: from elsewhere... [i.e. the children were from elsewhere — not hers]
Heard.
—o—
K. — "To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?" (6:6)
How was Haman so sure they meant him? He considered either Mordecai or himself, and since Ahasuerus said "What shall be done unto the man (ish)", Haman said to himself: he cannot mean Mordecai, because a Jew he would not call "a man" — a Jew is not a human being...
Daat Moshe.
—o—
L. — "Then said his wise men unto him" (6:13)
Earlier the Scroll calls them lovers, friends (see 5:10), and now — wise men, no less?
That's how it is: earlier all the advice-givers[?] are lovers, good friends; but when their advice falls through, they all become wise men, each one says: that's what you should have done, you didn't listen to me — so there you have it; everyone becomes wise after the misfortune.
Folk saying.
—o—
M. — "And Harbonah said... Behold also the gallows... fifty cubits high"
The Gemara (Megillah 16) says that Harbonah had earlier been with Haman and helped him set up the gallows (tree).
— How did Harbonah know that the tree was exactly 50 cubits high? It can only be that he was the craftsman who built it.
Kol Rinah.
—o—
N. — "Wherefore they called these days Purim" (9:26)
The Torah calls Yom Kippur "Yom Kippurim" — a day like Purim (ke-Purim), for on Purim Jews disguise themselves as gentiles, and on Yom Kippur — gentiles as Jews...
"Riym Str."[?]
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: Session of the City Council

What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 14 Adar 5690. — Piątek 14 marca 1930 [Friday, 14 March 1930].)
Będzin
Session of the City Council.
Under the chairmanship of Vice-President Jakub Erlich a session of the local city council took place on Monday. The agenda consisted of a series of tax statutes, which were adopted „as if greased“ without any discussion. But when it came to the statute on the fee on goods brought by rail, the „socialists“, the PPS [Polish Socialist Party], found their tongue and came out with a proposal that the fee on freight be raised; no matter, the merchants — so they say — will earn less, as long as the „Kasa Miejska“ [municipal treasury][?] has more income, [and then][?] (original „עלפחיי“, unclear word) the unemployed will receive larger relief payments“.
Against the proposal spoke: Lewin, Klajnman, Gitler and the President. The President's arguments had their effect on their colleagues, and thanks to their votes the PPS proposal was rejected.
At the session it was resolved to acquire[?] 1016 tramway shares[?] of the new issue.
— A small remark: 9 Jewish councillors were not present.
—o—
„20 zł. Kehilla Tax, or Else — Out of the Kehilla“...
The kehilla board received a letter from a certain kehilla-tax („etat“) payer, who had been assessed to pay 300 zł. of kehilla tax. In the letter he writes the following words: „If the tax sum is not reduced to 20 zł., let the kehilla board strike me off the list of kehilla members“.
—o—
The „Merchants' Association“ Against a Protest.
At the „Merchants' Association“ (Sokhrim Fareyn) a joint meeting took place with the participation of board members of the „Merchants' Association“ and the „Small Traders' Association“. At the meeting, among other things, the proposal of the small traders' representatives was considered, to declare solidarity with the protest which the Jewish „Koło“ [the Jewish parliamentary club in the Sejm] has proclaimed against the tax decrees.
The representatives of the „Merchants' Association“ did not want to agree to the protest.
—o—
Extraordinary General Meeting of „Hakoach“.
Last Friday an extraordinary general meeting took place in the club's own premises. The meeting was opened by the association's president Dr. Rechtman, who explained that the main reason for the extraordinary meeting is that the audit committee has submitted its resignation. After the discussion, which was stormy, they proceed to elect an audit committee. List no. 1 won, and elected were: I. Erlich, S. Trauib [Traub?] and St. Sztajer.
Then also elected to the board were Messrs.: Dr. Rechtszaft[?], A. Kramałowski and Z. Lichtensztajn.
—o—
Permits to Bring Goods from Abroad.
Until Monday the 17th of this month there is time to submit applications for import permits, to bring goods from abroad. The applications are granted through the intermediary of the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce (misprint in the original: „נדער“ for „דער“). Further information — at the „Merchants' Association“.
—o—
Meeting of Commercial Employees.
Next Sunday, the 16th of this month, a meeting of commercial employees will take place in the premises of the Right „Poale Zion“, Modrzejowska[?] 64.
—o—
A Lecture.
Next Sunday at 6 in the evening Dr. Tajchner will lecture at the „Tse'irei Mishmerei ha-Holim“ (Young Sick-Watchers) on the topic: „How the watcher [the sick-bed attendant] should treat the sick person“.
—o—
Będzin Turns to Warsaw...
In connection with the establishment of mechanical bakeries in our town, the local rabbinate has turned to the Warsaw rabbinate with a question: how they make the mechanical ovens kosher (fit) for baking matzot.
—o—
Appeals Against the Kehilla Tax.
In the course of the week more than 20 appeals were lodged with the kehilla („gmina“) against this year's kehilla tax („etat“). The deadline for lodging appeals (recourses) is still until the 19th of this month.
—o—
The Magistrate Sells Cheap Potatoes.
7 groszy per kilo.
At Tuesday's session of the city administration, the instruction of the voivode [provincial governor] was discussed, that the magistrate [municipality] should begin a counter-action against the unjustified high cost of bread and potatoes. During the discussion of the question it emerged that the price of bread and white baked goods in Będzin and Sosnowiec is 20 gr. per kilo dearer than elsewhere; this is apparently owed to the mechanical bakeries, which the price commission wants to support.
At the session it was resolved that the magistrate should buy larger consignments of potatoes and then sell them to the population. The potatoes at the price of 7 gr. per kilo can be obtained by anyone at the „Merkury“ hall.
—o—
By Day for Money, by Night — for Free...
Next Monday the „tradition“ of enjoying water free of charge will be abolished. From that day on a fee for water will be introduced. For this purpose a supervisor will be stationed at every pump, who will sell the water.
From 11 at night until 5 in the morning the water will be free of charge.
—o—
A Christian Maid Throws an Axe at Jewish Children.
On Monday morning a group of Jewish children were playing in the courtyard of Herzberg's house on Małachowskiego Street. The noise of the playing children greatly annoyed Mrs. Saks, a resident of the house, and she turned to her Christian maid, telling her to chase the children away from her windows. The maid followed the advice of her mistress[?] (original „מאדאם“[?], madam), but instead of chasing them away she took an axe and threw it among the children.
At that moment Mr. Herszel Trajsman[?] was passing by, and the axe struck him in the foot. The blow was a light one, but he was the messenger who saved a child from a disaster...
Councillor Erlich took an interest in the matter; he brought a policeman and a report was drawn up.
—o—
Swore an Oath on a Torah Scroll That He Will Shoot His Partner...
Between the former partners Jehoszua Ratner and Hendel Szturner sharp disputes have prevailed for some time, arising from their former partnership business.
Last Sabbath, when the scroll was taken out for the Torah reading in Sercarz's[?] minyan, Ratner grabbed the Torah scroll and said in a loud voice: „I swear an oath that next Tuesday I will shoot Szturner“...
—o—
A Serious Catastrophe Averted.
On Monday, at the corner of „Kołłątaja—Małachowskiego“, there was a light collision between a tram and a passenger car. Fortunately the tram was stopped instantly, and thanks to that it did not come to any serious catastrophe.
—o—
A Representative of the Journeymen at the Examinations.
The Craftsmen's Council has received a circular (original „okólnik“) from the ministry, which orders that at the craftsmen's examinations a representative of the journeymen must also be present. Interested journeymen should look into the matter. Further information can be obtained at the magistrate from the official Mr. Janicki.
Sosnowiec: General Meeting of the Small Traders' Association / A Living Child Thrown into the „Przemsza“ / Activity of „WIZO“ / The First Masked Ball / Tel-Hai Academy / Caught at the „Hot“ Minute[?]

[Sosnowiec — local news: small traders' association, infant thrown into the river, WIZO, Purim ball, Trumpeldor memorial, burglary.]
Sosnowiec
General meeting of the small traders' association.
In the „Hotel Polski“ a general meeting of the local small traders' association took place on Sunday. At the request of those assembled, Mr. Kupermintz takes the chair and invites Messrs. Lampel, Gakhisarger[?], Goldberg into the presidium, and A. Chaim as secretary.
The report on the activity is given by the association's chairman, Mr. Aliner[?]. Interesting, however, is the sad phenomenon which [?] among us Jews: when Jews come, after a whole year, to a general meeting of their association, the chairman comes and delivers the report to them precisely in Polish... The small traders listen against their will and do not dare to utter a loud word — after all, a Polish speaker...
The report shows that the board was on guard, and in the course of the 9 months it has been at the helm the board accomplished much for the members; in particular, the board carried out a „May[?] revolution“ and expelled the board members who had taken the income for themselves.
The treasurer's report is given by Mr. Chanan Dvinski. Expenditure and income amount to about 7 000 zł. Cash in the till — 14 zł.
After the reports a discussion develops, in which Messrs. Vshelanka[?], Ganzweig[?], Dafner, Opatowski and others take part. Finally the following board is elected: Aliner[?], Rafner, Berkower, Dvinski, Skowron, Opatowski, Kimelman, Fuks, Schlesinger, Zielonka and Erlich.
—o—
A living child thrown into the „Przemsza“.
On Monday evening passers-by near the factory in Radocha noticed a white bundle floating on the „Przemsza“. When the bundle was taken out and unwrapped, a baby girl 2 weeks old was found. The little soul was taken into the hospital at Pekin.
—o—
Activity of „WIZO“.
The Zionist women's association „WIZO“, which was founded here a short time ago, is conducting active work; the ranks of „WIZO“ are growing with women who until today had not the slightest notion of what national work is.
Last Sunday „WIZO“ arranged at „Maccabi“ a lecture given by Miss Albek. The introduction, in fine Yiddish, was given by Mrs. Rosman, pointing out the tasks of the Jewish woman at the present moment. After Miss Albek's lecture Mrs. Rosner of Będzin delivered a [„sheherige“ — doubtful word] speech, which inspired the listeners.
—o—
The first masked ball.
This Shushan Purim, i.e. tomorrow evening, „WIZO“ is arranging a masked ball. This is the first masked ball in our town that will have a Jewish national character: Eretz-Israel dances, „Jewish“ masks, and above all Zagłębie elects an „Esther the Queen“. Besides the big buffet, which the „WIZO“ members are preparing at half price, there will be a bazaar — not the kind on Kowalska[?] Street, but a bazaar with products from Eretz Israel.
—o—
Tel-Hai academy.
On Tuesday evening a memorial academy dedicated to the 10th yahrzeit of Joseph Trumpeldor took place in the premises of the local Zionist Organization.
After the opening speech by Mr. Glidman the choir sings „El Male Rachamim“, and Messrs. Klarman, Feldman and Reizman speak about Trumpeldor's life and work.
Then Mr. Glidman reads Trumpeldor's biography. The academy ends with „Hatikvah“.
—o—
Caught at the „hot“ minute[?].
In the night from Monday to Tuesday a burglary was committed in the leather warehouse of Starostecki[?] on Warszawska Street. At the moment when the burglars were about to carry out the bundles of leather, worth about 20 thousand zł., they were stopped by a policeman, who arrested the „craftsmen“.
Dąbrowa: Bloody Clashes Between Communists and Police / A Children's Entertainment

[Dąbrowa — communist „Women's Day“ demonstration and arrests; Hashomer Hatzair children's entertainment.]
Dąbrowa
Bloody clashes between communists and police.
On Sunday, on the initiative of the communists, an „International Women's Day“ was organized. At 3.30 in the afternoon a fairly large crowd gathered on Żeromskiego[?] Street, with the communist Sejm deputy Kirzwolski[?] at its head. The demonstrators set off in the direction of Sobieskiego[?] Street, shouting: „Long live International Women's Day“, „Down with the fascist dictatorship“, etc.
At the corner of Żeromskiego–Sobieskiego the crowd was stopped by a mounted policeman, who, with drawn sword, called on the crowd to disperse.
At that moment the crowd threw itself on the policeman, beating him on the ground with sticks, [„sherfs“ — doubtful word] and the like. Several more policemen came to the spot and arrested the following persons: Franciszka Walczyk, Szymon Agisman[?], Frymet Trajman, Chana Wajzler[?]. The arrested were handed over to the disposal of the examining magistrate.
—o—
A children's entertainment.
On Sunday the local „Hashomer Hatzair“ is arranging, in the premises of the [—] association, a children's entertainment with a very rich programme.

Prices of Flour and Bread

A kilo of wheat bakery goods 80 gr. — a kilo of bread 34 gr.
Thanks to the intervention of the Będzin municipal administration, the price commission at the Sosnowiec magistrate has finally reduced the high, incorrect prices of flour and bread.

Which premises are exempt from the water charge?
At the last session of the Będzin municipal administration a series of amendments to the statute of the waterworks was adopted, such as: for garages and for cellars in which shops or workshops are located, one pays for water.
For cellars, storerooms, stables etc. one does not pay.
—o—
A new tax burden on the merchants of Czeladź
The town council of Czeladź held a session this Monday, at which a series of tax statutes was adopted: on patents (trade licences), registration cards, real estate etc.
In addition, the taxpayers of Czeladź (read: Jewish merchants and artisans) are burdened with an investment tax. During the discussion it nearly came to a brawl between landowners and workers'[?] councillors. It was resolved that 50 per cent investment tax will be levied on every patent.
— Not enough for you? Here, have some more..

From the Sosnowiec Artisans' Association
This Saturday night (motzei Shabbat) there will be a members' talk on important current questions.
The municipal tax lists for 1930 are at the Artisans' Association, where members can find out on Saturday night and Sunday how much tax has been assessed on them.
—o—
Regional conference of Esperantists
Under the chairmanship of Dr. Jungster, a regional conference of Esperantists took place in Sosnowiec on Sunday. The conference was convened by the Central Committee in Sosnowiec, to which Będzin, Dąbrowa, Sosnowiec, Zawiercie and others belong.
At the conference it was discussed to conduct a broad propaganda campaign for Esperanto and to create a union of all workers' groups in Zagłębie.
Afterwards a new Central Committee was elected: Dr. Jungster (chairman), Y. Kaulawski[?] (vice-chairman), Prof. Czechowski (secretary), delegate — Izraelewicz.

Next Tuesday there will be a session of the Będzin town council. On the agenda: tax statutes for the year 1930/31.

The President of the German Republic has ratified the Polish-German agreement. The law will be promulgated in the coming days.
—o—
State President Mościcki has accepted the resignation of Premier Bartel and of the entire government.

In Paris the Spanish dictator Primo de Rivera has died suddenly.

On the Statement of Dr. Papuri (A Letter to the Editor)

On behalf of the Jewish Councillors' Club in Dąbrowa I have the honour to ask you, Mr. Editor, to publish in your esteemed newspaper the following letter:
In „Zaglembier Tsaytung“ number 9 there appeared an article by your contributor Dr. Papuri under the title „When one does not understand the tasks“. In this article the writer attacks us with the sharpest criticism in connection with our activity in the sphere of the Dąbrowa town council.
We must therefore state the following:
1) It is false that Jewish subsidies have now been struck out of the budget for 1930/1, since the items continue to figure in the budget.
2) As regards social welfare: what can we demand, when we unfortunately do not have in Dąbrowa a single registered charitable institution? We therefore had to demand such [funds] in the name of the Jewish community (gmina).
And when the Jewish community in Dąbrowa submits to the voivodeship office a report for the year 1928 that it has a surplus of 8 thousand zł. for the year 1929, and forgets to include the subsidised sum of 1929 in its budget, the voivode says that a community which has a surplus of 8 thousand zł. from a previous year need not take any subsidies from the magistrate.
3) Do you know, Mr. Dr., that we Jews receive from general social welfare about 25 thousand zł. a year, for which we show[?] figures confirmed by the magistrate?
4) Do you know, Mr. Dr., that we in Dąbrowa have no legally recognised philanthropic institutions such as an old-age home, an ochronka [children's shelter], no charity society[?], and certainly no Jewish hospital — so for which institutions should we demand subsidies?
Must we, the Jewish councillors, create the necessary institutions? Is that our task? On the contrary, show me, Mr. Dr., one town in Zagłębie that would subsidise a Jewish cheder! And we in Dąbrowa did achieve that.
It is true that there was a tendency to strike out our item for social welfare because of the voivode's rescript, but we threatened consequences and obtained the item for the „kolonie letnie“ [summer camps].
It is easy to criticise another, but blessing does not rest on an empty vessel, and the empty vessel is the Dąbrowa institutions, which we do not possess.
As for the humiliation[?] of our pride, you, Mr. Dr., have been badly informed. To the incident that once occurred at a session of the town council we reacted at once, and the non-Jewish councillor who had used an improper expression gave us the fullest satisfaction: he went up to the rostrum and apologised to us.
In general it must be stressed that we did not enter the town council in order to conduct a brawl[?] there, but to pursue a purely economic policy for general Jewish interests.
We are sure that our brief explanation will convince you that our activity is a consistent one.
If you still have any doubts whatsoever, we are ready to meet you before an audience, before which we shall give explanations. You need not hide behind pseudonyms, but speak face to face.
On behalf of the Jewish Councillors' Club
Bernard Rechnitz.

Strzemieszyce

Strzemieszyce.
„Gdud Keren Kayemet le-Yisrael“.
On Thursday the delegate of the A. K.[?] of the Keren Kayemet, Rabbi Jakobson from Eretz Israel, stayed here and gave a lecture on the situation in Eretz Israel before a packed hall.
The lecture made a favourable impression on those assembled.
After the lecture, in the premises of „Mizrachi“ and with the participation of the distinguished guest, a „Gdud Keren Kayemet“ [JNF brigade] was founded, in which 36 persons enrolled.
A Jewish ball.
On Saturday night (Shushan Purim) the Jewish library organised a ball in a hall at the „Strem“ factory, which was a great success.
—o—
Ząbkowice.
JNF academy.
On Wednesday evening a festive academy of the JNF (KKL) took place in the Folks-hoyz, with the participation of the Eretz Israel delegate Rabbi Jakobson. After Aharon Kazhukh played the Polish anthem and Hatikvah, Mr. Yaakov Goldsilber opened the academy in the name of the Keren Kayemet commission with a greeting to the distinguished guest, the delegate, and handed the chair to Mr. Bugajski. Then came greetings: on behalf of „Mizrachi“ Dizenhoyz greeted, on behalf of the Right Poale Zion Chanoch Goldsilber, on behalf of the Revisionists Shlomo Ladn[?], „Frayhayt“ — Zelmanovitsh[?]. Then Rabbi Moshe Jakobson received the floor for a lecture on the topic „The situation in Eretz Israel“; he gave a 2-hour lecture, for which he was accompanied by strong applause. Then the chairman closed the academy to the strains of Hatikvah.
After the academy a banquet took place which lasted until 4 in the morning; with various hora dances and Eretz Israel songs the banquet was closed.
What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — news.]
At the sight of the bailiff she was struck by paralysis.
A bailiff (executor), accompanied by 3 policemen, came to the widow Anga[?] (probably Anna) Macholowa in Katowice, Wadna[?] (Wodna?) 6, to collect a tax debt from the year 1925. When the bailiff put a distraint on the furniture, the woman suffered a severe paralysis (stroke). Her son, who reacted to this, was arrested at the police station (commissariat).
—o—
5 years for killing a husband.
Before the district court in Katowice stood Mrs. Rozala[?] Miklisowa, who was accused of having deliberately murdered her husband.
The murderess was sentenced to 5 years in prison.
—o—
Meeting of Polish merchants
On Sunday a meeting took place in Rybnik, attended by delegates of all the merchants' associations in the Rybnik district (powiat), numbering 400 delegates. After the speeches of Korfanty and others, a protest resolution was adopted against the high tax assessment.
—o—
Visit of the adviser Dewey
This week the financial adviser of the Polish government, Mr. Dewey, was in Katowice, and acquainted himself with Upper Silesian industry.
—o—
Attack on a doctor.
On Sunday evening, walking from the Katowice theatre, Dr. Karsznia was attacked by several young drunkards, who gave the doctor a good beating.
—o—
Excursion to Westphalia
This week a delegation of the coal mines and industry of Upper Silesia travelled to Westphalia, in order to acquaint itself there with the technology of the local industry.

The Katowice merchants have expressed their protest against the high taxes, and against the turnover tax in particular, in the following way: in every shop window there is a protest poster addressed to the proper authorities, asking that the tax system be eased and the turnover tax be abolished altogether.

13 smugglers caught.
On Monday night the border guard at Lipiny noticed a group of smugglers loaded with packs trying to dash across the border.
The border guard signalled the smugglers to stop, and when they kept running the guard opened fire, with the following result: 13 smugglers were detained, from whom a great deal[?] of fruit, 253 kilos of raisins and 17 kilos of oranges were confiscated.
The arrested men, who come from Będzin, Czeladź and Grodziec, were put into the prison in Królewska Huta (Königshütte).

To Our Masters and Rabbis

[Sosnowiec — rabbinate; editorial.] (Addressed to the "Agudat HaRabbanim" [Union of Rabbis], concerning its intervention in the Sosnowiec rabbinate question.)
Very much is being complained of lately in Orthodox circles about the decline of rabbinic authority, about the fallen state of the honour of the Torah, about the weakening[?] standing of our religious leaders. Unfortunately there is a great measure of truth in this assertion, but we do not wish to dwell now on the many external causes that have led to it, for neither did their development come about by our declared[?] will, nor does their remedy lie within our powers. Rather on those who are the foremost[?] and direct culprits in the desecration of the Torah and the rabbinate. To their address we wish to say something, for the fate of the matter lies wholly in their hands — we mean the esteemed leading rabbis themselves.
Yes, it is most tragic when with one's own hands one undermines one's own authority, when one makes oneself a disgrace and a mockery, when one's own hands blacken the face — and that hurts the most[?].
For a number of years an Agudat HaRabbanim has existed here in Poland. As a union of religious leaders it ought to occupy a foremost place in the Jewish street. The Jewish people, after all, has always distinguished itself by unexampled discipline and obedience towards its rabbis, because the qualifications for a rabbi were always: only[?] crammed-full knowledge of Torah, broad erudition in ancient Hebrew literature, and then the embodiment of integrity; that is why they were held in such respect, that is why even our freethinkers bowed their heads before them.
Such a union of rabbis could indeed have accomplished much in the religious field: awakening the weakened religious feelings of the Jewish masses, taking the religious leadership into its hands and standing guard over it.
But that is not what happened. It shrank[?] into the narrow four cubits of "court" intrigues and petty politicking, isolated itself from Jewish spiritual life; instead of leading, it let itself be led by certain circles and crawled into a swamp. Has the Agudat HaRabbanim ever spoken up on topical Jewish spiritual questions? Has it ever let its word be heard on burning Jewish problems? What, for instance, has it done against the Sunday rest that forces a large part of the Jewish population to desecrate the Sabbath? What steps, for example, do they take on behalf of our robbed[?] brethren in Russia? Within whose competence does such a matter fall, if not the Agudat HaRabbanim? Do we hear their voice of protest against the sad Jewish situation? — No, such matters do not concern it; that is not its worry.
But let us assume that the Agudat HaRabbanim limits itself to the rabbinic field alone, deals only with rabbinic questions — that it is, so to speak, merely a professional association. That would mean it did not stand at the height of its tasks, but it would not have reached[?] a state of degradation.
Yet even assuming this, we still have the right to demand of it the highest objectivity, integrity in action, truth in its words and a clean conscience. On whose gates, if not those of the Agudat HaRabbanim, should be inscribed "Thou shalt not respect persons in judgment"?!
Let what happened here in Sosnowiec serve as a characterization of the Agudat HaRabbanim's physiognomy.
For a long time a regrettable rabbinate struggle went on in Sosnowiec — a struggle that brought no honour to the Jewish population, a struggle in which many kosher and non-kosher means were used. Someone was truly needed to intervene, an authority to speak its objective word of truth. And who is more called upon to do so than the Agudat HaRabbanim? But making peace, it seems, is not among its tasks. When one candidate was elected by a doubtful majority, the Agudat HaRabbanim did not come and say that there exists a ban (cherem) of the early Geonim, confirmed here in Poland by the Council of Four Lands and reinforced by the last great Polish sages, such as the Sochaczew Rabbi of blessed memory and others, that no rabbi may acquire the rabbinic seat by means of money — the Agudat HaRabbanim did not come and declare that such elections are not "according to law and custom", that this demoralizes, that such things must be fought. No, we heard not a peep, as though it did not concern it, as though it were not called upon to stand guard over rabbinic integrity.
— But when a large part of the community brought in, at its own expense, a rabbi who is a Torah scholar, a scion of great rabbis, who in addition possesses secular education and every ability to be a rabbi in Israel — suddenly the Agudat HaRabbanim appears — pushed by an intrigue — with a prohibition. No more and no less: — "it forbids the rulings (hora'ah) of all the rabbis in Sosnowiec except the as yet unconfirmed rabbi". Does it not make itself a laughing-stock thereby? Among the rabbis mentioned is the Koziegłowy Rabbi (author of "Si'ach HaSadeh"), a Gaon in Israel, who is one of the few great sages of Poland, with few, few equals in learning and now in simplicity, honest simplicity — and the Agudat HaRabbanim has forbidden him to give rulings, him and others too — how ridiculous! What contempt for the Torah!
Did the Agudat HaRabbanim delegate anyone here to investigate the state of affairs? Did it inquire of the kehilla? No. A representation[?] from one interested[?] party is already enough to issue prohibitions. Does this not weaken the value of prohibitions when they do, for once, come justly?
One recognizes at once in the notice that it was dictated by one side, that it appeared with someone's help and pressure. The second, corrected notice points still more to unfamiliarity with the real situation. What was forbidden yesterday they try to correct today: so it appears[?]. Thus does an Agudat HaRabbanim play with prohibitions, and thereby it trivializes its own prohibitions and bans.
That the Agudat HaRabbanim should make peace anywhere in a town — we have never heard; on the other hand, discord and intrigues — plenty, plenty. That the Agudat HaRabbanim should recommend suitable rabbis for towns — we do not know; but it does help to "install" such "fine" rabbis who cannot decide any ritual question, whose place is rather a Rebbe's chair with kvitlach than a rabbinic post, rabbis who would feel more comfortable distributing shirayim[?] than presenting themselves before the starosta, and who break their teeth getting out a word of Polish — that, yes. And the conscience does not tremble at it: after all, one causes the public to stumble, one causes a desecration of God's name. What is the simple Jew to say to this? Is it any wonder that he loses all respect for rabbis and Torah sages? Does this not lead him onto leftist paths?
The heart bleeds when one must say such things to the address of rabbis, but "where there is desecration of the Name, no honour is accorded to a rabbi".
There are, after all, enough honest and truly pious men in the "Agudat HaRabbanim" — how do they permit such wheeling-dealing? Such a desecration of the Name? Where are they? — It is all the more astonishing when we see the signatures of the venerable Płońsk Rabbi, of the Gawidzów[?] Rabbi Gejfeler[?]. How do they allow such a dangerous game to be played with their names?
One is reminded of the words of the Mishnah:
— "Sages, be careful with your words"!
