Our Panorama

[Humorous feuilleton — Zagłębie and Upper Silesia, Purim.] (Purim is a holiday. — Great events. — An outburst at "Ahasuerus's question". — You listen to me, I'll listen to you. — A "child" without a name. — Grown-ups playing like children. — Fooled into the sack. — Purim joy or a "yahrzeit"? — Measure for noodles. — A library is treif and "a voice in a shiksa" is kosher. — "Had Gadya" before Passover.)
A folk saying: "Purim is no holiday and a fever is no illness." That is a lie — Purim is a holiday no worse than Simchat Torah. The best proof of it are the post-Purim reports, from which we learn of "important events" no less than from all the holidays of an entire year.
Take, for example, the "great event" in the big Ger shtibl in Będzin. It is a known fact that in no "shtibl" does such "unity" reign as among the Ger Hasidim. Nevertheless, on Purim something happened there that deserves to be immortalized in history.
And the story went like this.
The Megillah on Purim morning was read not by the regular Torah reader but by a stranger, who read it with such a tune that some of the worshippers did not even know whether it was Purim or Tisha b'Av. And when the Megillah reader had reached "Ahasuerus's question": "Who is he", one of our people asked: Who is this Megillah reader? One does not fulfil the duty this way! Gentlemen! Why are you silent?..
And the public was not silent; they got it off their chests. The first to take the floor was "Harbona", who related that among the king's princes there is one who wants "to destroy all the merchants"..
The revelation caused such a storm that the "court people" left the shtibl, went into a neighbouring apartment and finished the Megillah there..
The epilogue was "staged" before the rabbinate. The leading roles were played by "Harbona" and his partner. The content of the epilogue is: "You listen to me — I'll listen to you"..
———
The Jews of Königshütte [Królewska Huta, today Chorzów] had a very hard question to decide in Purim week. The question is this: Königshütte faces city council elections, and since the Jews form a significant force there, they set about creating a united Jewish front.
For this purpose a meeting was held at which the unity bloc was to be created. After long birth pangs the "child" was born, but when it came to giving the child a name, the real fun began. Those from Grünbaum's [?] "cheder" clamoured that the child be named "National Jewish Bloc", while those from Wiślicki's "cheder" shouted "Jewish People's Bloc"..
As we write these lines it is still not clear to us whom the "child" belongs to. But be that as it may, all that remains for us is to call out to the local Jews:
— Grown-ups! Don't forget yourselves in children's games...
———
The KKL committee in Olkusz no longer busies itself with "nonsense" at all. They are strong adherents of the saying [?]: "The world stands on three things — on money, money and money"...
They arranged a Purim ball not for the sake of dancing but for the sake of a mitzvah, in aid of the Keren Kayemet. Invitations were sent out to all the Jewish diaspora and also to Będzin. In the invitations the committee proclaimed Ahasuerus's manifesto — "to do according to every man's pleasure"...
The "manifesto" had an effect on a group of members of "HaShachar", and they travelled to Olkusz. On the way an extraordinary "Purim miracle" happened, and instead of Olkusz they arrived at "Magrushev", where they were charged the following:
For stepping over the threshold — 2 zł.
For taking off the coat — 1 "
For sneezing — 1/2 "
For coughing — 1/2 "
"And as soon as the dawn (HaShachar) rose" — when the members of "HaShachar" realised that they might end up becoming "Magdzhev" residents, they hurried home, came into the editorial office and told of the great "miracle"...
———
A great "miracle" also happened in Katerynga [?]. Some time ago a library was founded in that place, crowned with the name "Library in memory of Dr. Perlman of blessed memory". The library developed very well, grew in quantity and in quality, until..
Here we give the floor to our correspondent, who relates that
"Elements forced their way into the management who have not the slightest notion of how to run a library. A fact is what happened last week. The whole management together with the librarians turned the library into a drunkards' house. They went on drinking until they started smashing windowpanes, and [?] then
What will happen next we do not wish to prophesy; we are very curious to know whether it was a "Purim celebration" or simply a "yahrzeit celebration"..
———
Czeladź too has a Jewish library; it was founded by a group of young people, lovers of Yiddish literature.
Well, that's good! But there are several young little "Agudah" agents there who do not rest and work deeds to the detriment of the library. Well, that's not good again! But there is a rule that one is paid measure for noodles [a pun on "measure for measure"]... So the Sitra Achra latched on to the persecutors and dragged them to a Polish public school, where girls (read: shiksas) sing, and the yeshiva boys listen with great devotion and are roused by the "beautiful melodies" — well, that's good again:..
— Of course it's good — say the youth of Czeladź. — We have lived to see a bit of consolation: they, the Musar people, fight the library, and bareheaded they listen to gentile songs...
———
In the Dąbrowa synagogue they have already reached "Had Gadya"... only instead of:
"The farmer won't pick the apples, the puppy won't bite, the water won't extinguish, the fire won't burn" — one must sing:
"The cantor won't pray, the gabbaim won't hand out aliyot, the dozores [synagogue board] say 'yes' — the congregation says 'no', and — Had Gadya, Had Gadya!..
Ben Amotz.

Otto Weininger

[Zangen — literary supplement; essay.] "Zangen" [Ears of Grain] — literary supplement.
Sh. Elide.
(On his 50th birth-year.)
With pure gall [?] his doctrine bubbled forth, his unique conception of sex and character; yet not from a shadowy spring, not from a dark abyss — the perpetual primal springs of hatred — do the streams of hate gush. A deep light of thought accompanies them, much acumen flashes above them, torches of life-truth and philosophical brooding shine over them, and therefore his hatred sweeps one along, convinces.
Otto Weininger did not divide his hate between equal categories of people. He preached hatred of the most beloved human kind — women, and of the most hated and tormented part of mankind — Jews... And just as he is not the first with his opinion of the Jewish people (from which he descends), so too he is not the first with his bad opinion of the female sex. Does Schopenhauer revile woman so little? He sees in her an ugly, inferior creature; he goes so far as to strive to assert that even in the physical, aesthetic sense woman is a hideous creature. And all those world artists who are so enraptured by the feminine beauty with which nature endowed her — that enthusiasm is merely a product of sexual lust; it is what blurred the truth, it is what falsified art. In reality, however, the bodily build of woman is a faulty work of nature. So does the philosophical genius Schopenhauer see woman, and through the same black spectacles — trained on woman's face — (naturally each one wears different lenses) look Nietzsche and Tolstoy.
Opponents of sexual cohabitation are found among the world's poets too, such as Strindberg and Maupassant, who see only ugliness in sexual life together and call for prohibitions [of abstinence]. In Maupassant's opinion mankind ought to curse bodily intimacy [?] as nature has cursed it, because instinctively we feel the unparalleled coarseness and loathsomeness of these acts [?].
But Otto Weininger's argument for the baseness and inferiority of woman impresses by its wealth of ideas. He called his whole great scientific erudition to his aid: philosophy, physiology, psychiatry, anatomy, medicine, anthropology. With great toil and diligence he gathered all the ideas and philosophical premises ever voiced against woman, and out of it all built a giant edifice that arouses astonishment, if not even recognition.
It is not woman as such that Otto Weininger is an enemy of, but womanhood, femininity. In it he sees a curse for mankind, and this depraved femininity need not be possessed by a woman alone — men often possess it too, and such effeminate men are not a hair better than real women. And there are also "medical" [?] [probably a misprint for "masculine"] women, free of all women's faults.
Sexual relations, against which he has nothing in and of themselves, nevertheless bear a loathsome character into which woman's natural baseness has transformed them; and as the consequence of mutual [?] influence, sexual relations are indeed one of the factors in woman's fall. He sees no boundary between mother and prostitute. We merely distinguish between them, but in truth there is no difference between them, and therefore he advises the prohibitions. Perhaps in this way woman will rise to a higher level; perhaps in this way she will overcome the femininity within herself.
He is also an opponent of women's emancipation; he does not want to rob her of her rights, but woman's lack of perfect talent hinders the carrying out of an emancipation that can come only when woman has completely freed herself from her curse: femininity.
On the same argument his antisemitism is also based. Against the Jew as such he has nothing — only against his Semitism. And indeed, in his opinion, there are Jews who are pure Aryans in their character, and non-Jews who are Semites in their essence; the Jews must tear [?] out their Semitism, and then they will be healed.
He sees a strong resemblance between the Jew and woman. Both are shallow, not deep, [not] rooted. Neither loves the fundamental, the immovably firm, but rather the light, the external. The self-esteem of both has its source not in nature but in conceit — an artificial one. Let the Jew go deep into himself, get to the bottom [?] of his own self — that is the way to his redemption.
But as well as Otto Weininger knew woman, so little did he understand Judaism. It is a fact that he possessed quite little knowledge of the Jewish "sb"y" [?] [perhaps: past], of its original character. He judged by the Jew's exile-shape, and not thoroughly at that. He held the Jew to be an element "unfit" [?] for a state society, and therefore he did not believe in Zionism. Yet we see how mistaken this claim of his was. Zionism faces various obstacles to its realisation, but a lack of understanding of statehood — no.
Whatever false accusations he may hurl at us, however many buckets of black paint he may pour over us, we do not hold it against him too much, because — as we said at the beginning of the article — his hatred does not stem from dark sources. And in his paradoxical arguments about Semitism and Judaism, too, we find traces of truth — mere traces, but interesting and instructive in and of themselves. Among them, his opinion about antisemites. Otto Weininger holds that all the enemies the Jewish people has — its own as well as strangers — are precisely those who are most severely [?] stricken with the Semitic plague, whose character contains a large dose of Semitic essence. It is like one who constantly shouts against stomach disease — the best sign that he himself suffers from his stomach... We often hate the one in whom we feel our own shortcomings, in whom we see a mirror of our own faults. Our hatred is then only a kind of protest, a struggle.
———
"Between genius and madness there is but a hair's breadth" — someone once said. And this mixture of grandiose genius and extreme [?] madness is found in Otto Weininger. It is interesting that nearly all preachers of prohibitions ended in madness. Maupassant was a neuropath and died of madness. The same fate befell Friedrich Nietzsche and Otto Weininger.
This coming 3rd of April will be fifty years since his birth. He was born in Vienna (3 April 1880) to Jewish parents. On 21 July 1902, the same day he received the title of Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Vienna, he adopted the Protestant faith. Soon afterwards he published his work "Sex and Character," which made a tremendous impression in literary and scientific circles. He then let fall the following words: "This work is a death sentence: it will strike either the work or its author"... And indeed it struck the latter: on 4 October 1903 he committed suicide, already in a state of madness.
Literary Notes

[Zangen — literary news.] ○ The 8th of Shevat marked six years since the death of the well-known writer Ze'ev Yavetz — he was born in Kolno, Łomża district, in 1847 to a family of distinguished lineage; in 1881 he went to the Land of Israel, where he conducted a broad, many-branched "Mizrachi" activity.
In literature Yavetz was active in many fields. A "holy" [?] [perhaps: first and foremost a] poet in his "Sichot Mini Kedem" and others, with which David Frischmann was enthusiastic. His rare aggadic style is very original. In his "Divrei ha-Yamim le-Am Bnei Yisrael" he renders Jewish history in the spirit of the Talmud and Midrash. He also wrote much journalism. He also composed many children's poems, upon which a special charm rests.
○ Sholem Asch's son, Nathan, has now published his second work, "Love in Chartres," which was warmly received by the critics — both his works appeared not in Yiddish. Such, then, is the tragedy of our great ones: that their children become estranged from their people!
○ The "Pinchas Graubard" publishing house has issued a drama by M. B. Stein entitled "Di Khurbe" [The Ruin], in which a well-known tragedy of the Ruzhin rebbe's court plays out. A review of the drama will appear in the next number of "Zangen."
○ The second booklet of "Ershte Shnit" [First Harvest] has appeared, a collection of poems by young poets, edited by Sh. Zaromb.
A Tear.

[Literature — poetry.] Yosef Elshade.
A Tear.
The bright day
suddenly went dark,
like an eye snuffed out
by the Angel of Death's
hasty breath.
Between me and the sun
a wall has grown up,
upon it casts a shadow,
pours out heaps of darkness,
a black hand.

At such a moment —,
I hear a fall —,
aha, my soul
slipped out and went off
somewhere into the universe.
I rummage every place,
every corner —
empty and bare,
so that at times I cannot
even search,
when it is so dark.

Suddenly there appears
a shining tear,
it then kindles
my thought-swaying[?] —
I no longer need
to search for my soul —
in a crack
it had been hiding,
caught up in a musing...
Yashe the Watchman.

[Literature — story.] Binyomin Rozentsvayg.
Yashe the Watchman.
(A novella).
Everyone in town knew him, Yashe, but did not know what he was. He lived secluded, kept little company with people, never spoke about himself[?]. People even wondered at his behaviour. But who had him in mind — there were more important worries than delving into the heart of Yashe's secluded life.
Yashe lived on what the shopkeepers paid him for keeping watch at night over their shops and storehouses. Yashe lived in a separate small, clean little room. He cleaned it himself, polished it, cooked for himself, everything alone, alone.
The only joy[?] Yashe possessed was a large, ornate picture of a beautiful woman. Gazing at the picture he would recall his youth, in a town far, far from here, where he had lived so happily with his chosen one, Royze. Yes, Yashe had once loved. Love had once been the holiday of his life, and Royze — the queen of his life's holiday. But it was fated that the holiday should not last long; it was cut off in the middle. Royze died on him, his dear Royze.
He then remained living with his wife's mother, and like all mothers-in-law — she was a witch. She always needled him, only stabbed him with little words, with looks. She felt envy that her daughter lies there in the grave while he, Yashe, goes about alive... So she began to wear him down over the years, wanted to bring him too to the grave... She began to torment him with such words as wrung his heart. From her mother-in-law's mouth one always heard: "Yashe, because of you Royze went young into the grave".. This hurt him so much that he did not know what to do, what to answer. He kept silent and suffered, but had no strength to bear it, and once, during a quarrelsome scene, he resolved: far away from here. Away, away, never to marry again and to live secluded. Before he wandered off he first went to Royze's grave, took leave with boiling tears that burned through[?] the four ells of earth.
Chance brought him here, into this town. He took over the post of watchman, and for decades now he has been at his post. Meanwhile he has grown grey. He felt fine, dozed by day and by night strolled alone through the town, absorbed into himself the secret of the night, and his silence congealed still more. —
In a winter of steady snow[?]. Boys were playing in the snow at the bend of the alley and mischievously set up a slender snow "man", and one of them, a prankster, threw a hair wig onto its head. Merry childish laughter accompanied the creation of the "snowman". Done playing, with little noses red from frost, they went off home and forgot about their "creation".
Night wrapped itself deeper and the time came for Yashe to go out into the town. He walks about the alley, tries the padlocks hanging on the shop doors. That same night the sky poured snow upon snow. The snowflakes sparkled, glittered, and Yashe trudged through the white carpet of snow. He paced slowly, with measured steps. Head bent, his gaze gliding over his long beard. A frost cut into his old bones, and his thoughts he handed over, as every night, to the dominion of his fantasies, which always circled only around his unforgettable Royze, just as always, as every night.
Sunk in memories he strode with bent head, with lowered eyes, not looking where he was going, until his feet unnoticed brought him to the bend of the alley where the "snow-woman", the boys' creation, stood right by the church wall. Yashe strides along the wall, sunk in a sea of memories of his Royze. Suddenly his eyes lift and through the stringy snow-rain he sees... his.. Royze... He lurches[?] forward, a stagger and a stifled cry: My Royze! Mine!..
— — — — — — —
Next morning a gentile, going at dawn to pray, saw lying in the snow a man frozen to death, pressing a hair wig to his breast...
The "snowman" the boy pranksters found melted, and the two eyes (two bits of coal) now showed black out of the dazzling collapsed snow.
No one knew what had happened here[?] with Yashe. All only muttered: "A pity about Yashe, a pity".
A New Day.

[Literature — poetry.] Ch. V. Eisenman.
A New Day.
Like ploughed-up sands
of the sea shores,
fettered days lie
at my feet and beg for release.
Bloody drops of
new dawnings
split like smears
the iron nooses
that tightened
around blue necks,
on the bound heels
of the world — —
through the midnight rustlings,
nocturnal wailing, sea echoes,
hear the call:
A day is coming, it is on its way!
———
—o—
L. Kerner.
* * *
Days go past me,
I lose in the tumult
their way.
With laughter they run
over my door,
it is a mockery of me
that years come and go away
and I am still at the shore
like a child in the middle of the street
who has lost his mother
and does not know where to go,
and dissolves in weeping.
A Forced Reply.

[Dąbrowa — town council; polemic.] Mr. Dr. Papori tried, in the columns of the paper, to give the Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza] public representatives a lesson concerning their duties on the town council with regard to the Jewish population. He had barely given the brains a stir when Dąbrowa's one and only public-spirited activist jumped up from his lethargic sleep and, instead of rubbing his eyes and seeing how far and how deep he has, God help us, sunk, he sits down with loins girded, rolls up his sleeves and writes "a letter to the editor". It recalls that anecdote about a communal worker who always used to doze a little at meetings; once, on the Sabbath after the meal, his "so-and-so" [his wife] woke him from his sleep, and instead of rubbing his eyes and seeing where he was, he cried out: "I request the floor." I must add that our bridegroom in question [?] has one more virtue: not only does he himself doze off, but his dozing also has an influence on his fellow members...
Not with any too great a desire do I take the floor in this not very pleasant affair. I do it only because the content of the "letter" cries out "expound me!" But before I go over to the matter itself, I want only to recall in general that "a thing that is bound to come to light — people do not lie about it." Now I will go in order:
You say that Mr. Dr. Papori attacks you because of your activity in the field of the Dąbrowa town council. Most honoured Mr. Chairman, you have understood very badly: not because of your activity, but because of your non-activity, the esteemed doctor is trying to drum into you the rules of the Jewish national tasks on the town council.
You "establish" that in Dąbrowa there exists not one single charitable, philanthropic or communal institution that is legally registered, and therefore you have no one for whom to demand subsidies. And we ask you, Mr. Club Chairman: have you taken account of the fact that the "Z. C." [Zaglembier Tsaytung] is read by the greater part of the Jewish population of Dąbrowa, and that it is precisely informed that we possess, thank God, a fair number of legally registered institutions? Legally registered here are: Tarbut, "Tsiyog" [?], a library, "Beit Lechem", "Bikur Cholim", "Gemilut Chasadim", "Hachnasat Kallah" and many others besides. Have you forgotten that "he who wishes to lie places his witnesses far away"!
You ask whether Mr. Dr. P. knows that the Jewish population of Dąbrowa enjoys 25,000 guilders [złoty] a year from the magistrate [municipality]. Do you think that the "Z. C." appears on Mars, or in Honolulu, or do you want to throw sand in people's eyes? On the contrary — show your figures confirmed by the magistrate!
You ask Dr. P. to point out to you which town in Zagłębie subsidises an Agudah cheder and you missed it. For that you want [?] such a hearty "yasher koach"? Firstly, one would have had to drum the political ABC into you; then you would not have put such questions to Dr. P. And secondly, if these are to be all the subsidies, we must tell you: "Take your favours away"...
You say that there was a tendency to strike out the subsidies (which ones?), but you threatened consequences and got the items back. If so, if you really possess such power "with consequences", why did you not obtain even 1 grosz for the above-mentioned registered institutions? Do you know that we bear the burdens of the town proportionally, like the non-Jewish population? Where is our equivalent?
You say that you went into the town council not in order to conduct a "bayzukhke" [?], but to conduct a purely economic policy for Jewish interests — and that is precisely what we sent you for, and in no case to conduct a "bayzukhke" [?]. But show us something of the fruit of your economic work!
And now, after you have enumerated such a long list with such "convincing proofs", you believe that Mr. Dr. P. will no longer have any doubts at all, and if, God forbid, he does, you are ready to give him further explanations. Why, we ask, do you want to give them precisely to Mr. Dr. P. and not to your voters? Why have you not to this day convened even a single report meeting, where you would tell the Jewish voter of Dąbrowa what "salvations and consolations" your sitting on the town council brings? If you do not do so, we must tell you that you are not worthy of this mantle.
Veritas.
P.S. You demand of Dr. Papori that he should not hide behind any pseudonym, but speak with you face to face. Do you know that Mr. Dr. P. has been writing for years in the "Z. C." under that name, always stands on guard and says his stern, steely [?] word on every Jewish communal matter? Why do you want precisely to crawl into his heart with your boots? It is not moral! And perhaps it is his real name?..

From the Gemilut Chesed Fund in Strzemieszyce

[Strzemieszyce — free-loan fund; followed by a news item: railway accidents.] In recognition of the active and fruitful work of the local Gemilut Chesed [free-loan] fund — the "Joint" sent 175 dollars in the last few days.
At the same time it is also worth mentioning that the local "Bank Spółdzielczy" and "Bank Kupiecki Spółdzielczy" lent the fund, the same week [?], considerable sums of money for interest-free [?] long-term loans.
—o—
Two Accidents on the Railway
Last Friday a tragic accident occurred in Strzemieszyce to a railway worker, who, while two wagons were colliding, was crushed to death by the buffers.
— A second accident occurred to an unemployed man, who threw himself under a moving train and was left lying with his head cut off.
From the Będzin "HeChalutz".

[Będzin — youth movements; HeChalutz.] After the last district conference, the Będzin "HeChalutz" has set about intensified organisational and cultural work. Besides the regular meetings in the kvutzot, members' talks on current problems take place every Sabbath. At the last members' meeting Messrs. T. Baum and M. Tempel reported on the session of the Actions Committee and the Administrative Council of the "Jewish Agency". Mr. M. [?] Baum also devoted a few warm words to the late friend of the Jews, Lord Balfour, whose memory was honoured by standing.
Tomorrow a talk on the subject "Parliamentarism and the Land of Israel" will take place in the premises of "HeChalutz".
Committee to Celebrate the 50th Jubilee of Yitzhak Gruenbaum. / Appeal to the Jewish Population of Sosnowiec!

For 30 years now Yitzhak Gruenbaum has stood in the unceasing service of the Jewish people. For 30 years he has been waging the great, stubborn struggle for Jewish rights, for the Jewish revival, for a better and finer tomorrow. His whole life, his great soul and all his extraordinary abilities Y. Gruenbaum has placed at the disposal of his people. Not for one day, not even for one hour, has he interrupted his strenuous work for the liberation of the Jewish nation. Always vigilant, always faithful, forever and everywhere the honest, crystal-pure activist and fighter — Yitzhak Gruenbaum is not the property of one party — he is the property of the entire Jewish people. He has opponents, even many opponents, but even his sharpest opponents must acknowledge the greatness of his achievements for the good of the Jewish people and must bow their heads before the earnestness and honesty that mark his whole lifelong work.

The name of Yitzhak Gruenbaum is inseparably bound up with the greatest and finest ideals of the Jewish people, with its striving for revival and liberation in Eretz Israel and in the lands of the Diaspora. The finest pages in the history of the Zionist movement in the Diaspora lands and in the history of the struggle for our national and human rights in the lands of our dispersion — were written by him and his courageous, great deeds over the entire last thirty years.

The Committee to Celebrate the 50th Jubilee of Yitzhak Gruenbaum has proclaimed a popular collection for a fund to acquire a homestead (nachala) in Eretz Israel for Yitzhak Gruenbaum.

It is the duty of every Jew to take part in this collection — some with thousands and some with groszy — in order to show thereby that we Jews know how to appreciate and honour the great and honest work of one of the best sons of the Jewish people.

The local committee: Y. M. Weigreb [?], Mrs. L. Rotman, Natan Abramczyk, Moshe Reicher, Levi Jungster, Mordechai Hillel Spigelman, Yosef Klarman, Yaakov Kramalowski [?], Yaakov Shimon Feldman.

Donations are accepted at the "Bank Kupiecki", Sosnowiec, Targowa 11.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: City Council Meeting — Broken Off

[Head of the local page; Będzin — municipality, kehilla, economy and local news.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 28 Adar 5690 — Piątek 28 marca 1930 [Friday, 28 March 1930].)
Będzin
City council meeting — broken off.
On Tuesday a meeting of the city council took place under the chairmanship of Mr. Fürstenberg. At the meeting the PPS [Polish Socialist Party] members submitted an urgent motion and an interpellation.
The content of the motion is that, because of the unemployment, the administration of the magistrate [town hall] should be reformed in the sense that a married couple should not hold 2[?] posts.
Mayor (President) Michał[?] declares that the matter does not lie within the competence of the city council, but belongs to the city administration.
Secretary Łazkowski[?] says that because the mayor ignores the PPS's motions, they will draw more serious consequences.
The interpellation is addressed to the city administration: why the magistrate was not working for a whole day on 19 March (the name-day of Marshal Piłsudski).
When the mayor declares that he will give an answer at the next meeting, the "consequences" are carried out: the councillors of the PPS and the Left Poale Zion leave the meeting, and no quorum remains.
—o—
The kehilla parnassim must sit on the benches...
So says the voivode.
Some time ago the parnassim [board members] A. Szein, S. Frenkel, G. Rechnic and B. Rembiszewski[?] turned to the starost [district head], asking him to release them from activity in the kehilla.
To this the starost replied that the question belongs to the competence of the kehilla council. But this week the voivode announced[?] that the resignation petitions[?] are not being taken into account, and they must fulfil their duties as kehilla parnassim.
—o—
An interesting trial.
Next Tuesday the trial against Dr. Ferber[?] will take place in the local municipal court; he was sued by the children of the suddenly deceased Mrs. Welgrin.
The suit states that Dr. Ferper[?] refused to give help to the deceased.
—o—
Recognition for the city administration on account of the waterworks.
The government waterworks company in Katowice wanted the city administration to conclude an agreement with it on carrying out the waterworks. When the magistrate concluded the agreement with the Italian-French company, the said company undertook an obstruction campaign. In connection with this a delegate came here from the Ministry of Public Works [lit. "of public affairs"], who acquainted himself with all the work concerning the waterworks agreement and its installations.
This week the city administration received a report from the ministry, which highly praises the good management in general and the waterworks installations in particular.
—o—
The gmina's correspondence must be in Polish.
This week the vice-starost Mr. Magdyszewski[?] sent the gmina [Jewish community] the result of the inspection (lustracja) which he carried out in the gmina a few weeks ago.
Among other things it is pointed out that all the correspondence, even to the members, must be written in Polish.
—o—
Support the Kimcha [de-Pischa] campaign.
As every year, this year too the Kimcha [Passover flour] commission has begun its activity. Because of the great crisis that has lately prevailed in our town, many respectable[?] families have now been added who in earlier years belonged to those who gave. Considering the great need in the Jewish street, it is everyone's duty to help according to his means and to lessen the cup of tears.
—o—
A jubilee committee created at "Hakoach".
In connection with the 15th anniversary jubilee, a special meeting took place last week with the participation of Messrs. Chairman E. Fürstenberg, Dr. Rechtszaft[?], J. Erlich, P. Trajb, S. Sztajer and others[?].
Chairman Dr. Rechtman reported on the preparations and the programme of the jubilee committee.
After the report a provisional jubilee committee was created, consisting of Messrs. Ławnik[?] Goldsztajn, Dr. S. Weinzieher, Gustaw Weinzieher, S. Trajb, J. Erlich, Director Patak, Chairman Fürstenberg, Vice-Chairman Rubinlicht, D. S. Ratner, Mrs. Ratner, Dr. Rechtszaft, Chaim Szein, A. Szwarcbaum, L. Szpigelman and Marek Szein.
The first meeting of the committee will take place next week. Since the public's interest in "Hakoach" is very great, it was decided to expand the activity of the society.
It is characteristic that at this meeting 100 (one hundred) active gymnasts were admitted.
—o—
Did its "duty" with a dog...
On Potocka[?] street the tram was going at full speed. At that moment a dog ran across the rails and was crushed.
—o—
The "Beit Lechem" Passover campaign.
The board of "Beit Lechem" [Bread House charity], considering the present hard times, has decided to organise this year's Passover campaign in such a way that above all the needy who are going hungry in silence will be supported.
For this reason the board asks us to call on the gabbaim of the minyanim and shtiblekh to report their needy.
Applications are accepted only during the coming week.
—o—
The assessment commission dissolved.
On the basis of a decree, the "Izba Skarbowa" [Treasury Chamber] in Kielce announced that the local main tax-assessment commission is being liquidated.
In connection with this, the Merchants' and Small Traders' Association submitted a list of candidates, which has to be approved by the Kielce Izba.
—o—
Auctions from tax distraints.
Last Friday almost all the furniture in Moshe Rapaport's apartment on Zawale street was sold for tax debts.
— On Monday a tax bailiff, with the help of several policemen, hacked off the lock of a cellar at Kołłątaja 48. From that cellar 14 sacks of flour were taken out, which belong to Leah Damskurski. Because the flour was seized on the account of A. Damskurski, the matter will probably come before the district court.
—o—
Meeting of the Discount Bank.
Next Sunday the annual general meeting of the local Discount Bank will take place in the city council hall (in the "Piast"). Very important questions will be dealt with, which have a very important significance for the members.
—o—
The takings are small, the bankruptcies — big.
In the course of the past week a number of old ready-made clothing (konfekcja) firms in our town again suspended their payments. As people say, it is already hard to find a merchant on Kołłątaja street who "has not yet fallen"...
—o—
Both legs cut off.
While freight wagons were being shunted on Gutman's siding (bocznica) on Kościuszki street, the worker Szczanka[?] got caught[?] in a wagon, which cut off both his legs.
—o—
A daring bandit attack.
On Tuesday at 9 in the evening, when the machinist of the "Paryż" coal mine, Stanisław Gwakowski[?], was going to "kaver"[?], he was attacked by several Christians, who demanded money from him.
At first Gwakowski thought his friends were playing a "joke", but only when he received several heavy blows to the head did he "get wise" and hide 550 zł. on his person.
The bandits tore open Gwakowski's clothes and took 100 zł. out of his waistcoat pocket.
The bandits are already in the hands of the police.
—o—
Troubles with a caretaker.
The residents of the house at Kołłątaja 41 have "plenty to tell" about the caretaker of the house. The gate is locked punctually at 10 o'clock, and when one of the residents wants to get out of the "fortress" he must depend on the caretaker's "grace", and whoever comes late must pay a higher "ransom".
Such a thing happened to Mr. Merkin, who wanted to give the caretaker 20 groszy for opening the gate, but the caretaker declared that "now it already costs 50 groszy"...
Then Mr. M. turned to a policeman for intervention, but the latter also agreed to the "ransom", only he ordered the caretaker to give him 30 groszy on credit.
Should the city council not concern itself with such a matter?
Sosnowiec

A post-office building of its own in Sosnowiec.
The local Chamber of Commerce has addressed a memorandum to the Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs on the question of allotting an investment sum for the local post and telegraph office.
The ministry sent a reply explaining that the present premises of the local post office will be enlarged in the near[?] future.
At the same time the ministry approaches the Chamber of Commerce with the proposal that it, together with the Kraków Post Directorate, take an interest[?] in finding suitable premises for the various postal departments.
—o—
Repercussions of the abuses at the „Bank Ludowy“
As is known, the „Bank Ludowy“, where abuses took place, was liquidated a few days ago. But the investigating authority took an interest in what had happened at the bank and ordered the arrest of the former bank director Elazar Grincajger and also of the whole management.
After the interrogation the management was released, except Mr. Grincajger.
As we write these lines, Mr. Grincajger has not yet been freed.
—o—
Sessions of the Kashrut Committee.
As we have already written, a committee of rabbis has been created, in which are represented: Rabbi Hager (chairman), Rabbi Frommer (vice-chairman), Rabbi Halberstam (a brother-in-law of the Radomsko Rebbe), Rabbi Schwarz and Rabbi Glicksman.
The committee holds sessions every day in the kehilla premises, where kashrut matters are dealt with, such as supervision of the Passover flour, koshering ovens and the like.
The income from koshering an oven (25 zł.) and from Passover flour (40 zł. a wagon) is entered into the kehilla's treasury.
Hooligan attack on Jewish young people.

On Saturday evening Messrs. M. Glidman, Y. Klerman, Zalman and Franya Zilbergold were strolling on Sienkiewicza („Sheni-kevitsh“) Street. On the way they were attacked by 2 hooligans armed with knives. One of those attacked, Mr. Glidman, put up resistance, and with the help of the police the hooligans were detained.
—o—
Accident at work.
The foreman of Rutshinski's business fell during work and broke a leg.
—o—
Bread and roll prices — raised.
The price commission at the Sosnowiec magistrate at its Monday session again raised the price of bread and rolls. A kilo of bread 36 groszy, a kilo of rolls — 90 gr. A single roll of 100 grams 9 gr., of 50 grams — 5 groszy.
—o—
The Kimcha campaign begins on Sunday.
As every year, the Kimcha [Passover-flour relief] campaign has been organised in the community, and from Sunday on specially delegated collectors will collect Kimcha. Needless to say, everyone will understand to support the campaign and give according to his means.
—o—
The first „signs“ of spring.
The first teams of Będzin „Hakoah“ and the local „Shamayim“[?] play [unclear word, „ki-mpgrign“[?]] on Sunday at the „Hakoah“ sports ground the first match of the current season.
The reserves of the clubs play tomorrow on the same ground.
—o—
An „honest“ servant.
The Sofer family on Marshavka[?] Street hired a maid, who stated that she came from Grójec („Groytse“). Later it turned out that the servant is a professional thief, who comes from Lemberg [Lwów], and the police have been looking for her for quite some time.
A building of its own for the sick fund.

The board of the local sick fund (Kasa Chorych) has bought a large plot on the „Haldes“ [mine spoil heaps], where a building of the sick fund's own will be erected.
Construction is to begin in the days of next month.
—o—
A year and a half in prison for 78 eggs.
Before the local district court stood a certain Łaszczyk, who had stolen 78 eggs from a peasant's cart. For the theft Łaszczyk was sentenced to a year and 6 months in prison.
—o—
Already baking the „bread of affliction“... A kilo of matzot 1 40 zł.
From Tuesday on matzot are being baked. At a conference between community representatives and bakers it was established that a kilo of matzot should cost no more than 1,40 zł. a kilo.
It is interesting to note that a kilo of flour costs no more than 66 groszy...
The reckoning is „just“ — after all it is Passover's „bread of affliction“, and everyone must tear [i.e. toil] on the poor old nag...

Theatre Note.

[Sosnowiec — theatre and revue.] "In May! In May!"
Sosnowiec has lately had a "sensation". A revue theatre called "Arlekin"[?] has been opened.
The latest programme being staged there, despite bearing the name "In May! In May!", has nothing whatever to do with spring, in which nature awakens to life. Nor has the title anything in common with the "political May"; these are simply the words of the refrain sung at the end of the programme.
The programme consists of various sketches, tableaux and monologues, but the greater part of the programme is taken up by the very nicely executed dances, which the public (read: the men) applauds very warmly.
Very charming was the tableau "Gypsy Camp" with the prima ballerina Valeri at its head; the costumes make a very good impression.
Not bad either is the sketch set in a prison, in which Miss Żukowska and Mr. Giskarski[?] stand out.
A very successful attraction was the singing of Miss Kowalska, who with her lovely little voice sang several sentimental songs.
One must also mention the only Jew who contributes to the success of the revue: Mr. Szpilman, under whose direction the orchestra plays excellently.
The general impression is a very good one; the only shortcoming one could point out is the decorative side, which ought to have been better suited to the character of the revue.
X. Y.

Conference of Friends of the Yiddish Secular School in Będzin.
Under the chairmanship of the president of the Y.Sh.O. [Yiddish School Organisation], Mr. B. Grojbart, a conference took place on Saturday night in the premises of the Będzin "Merchants' Association". Taking part in the conference were representatives of Jewish workers' organisations, teachers, friends of the Yiddish secular school system, and the delegate of the Central Committee, Mr. Mandelman.
Mr. Mandelman illustrated with facts the internal and external persecutions and harassments concerning the Yiddish secular schools, pointed to the large network of Jewish schools in which about 25 thousand children study, and called for the 750 zł. that Będzin must give to the relief campaign to be raised.
Then the question was raised of creating a branch of the Y.Sh.O. in Będzin; on this spoke city councillor Rozenberg, Wajcenberg, Pesachzon[?] and others. The contribution sum was raised on the spot, and it was decided to start a campaign to open a Jewish elementary school.

Visit of Dr. R. Feldschuh (Ben-Shem) to Sosnowiec.
The Revisionist activist and founder of the youth organisation "Ha-Shomer ha-Le'umi", Dr. R. Feldschuh (Ben-Shem), visited Sosnowiec at the invitation of the local Revisionist organisation.
On Saturday afternoon the Brit Trumpeldor, under the command of Commandant Glidman, carried out various "drills"[?] on the "kordon"[?], in the presence of the chief commandant Dr. Feldschuh.
In the evening the guest gave a lecture in the hall of the Hotel "Polski" on "The Moral Revolution in Jewish Life". Even before the lecture began, Mr. Klarman devoted a few warm words to the recently deceased Lord James Balfour, which the assembled audience heard standing.
In very fine and humorous language the lecturer spoke of the enormous moral upheaval in Jewish life from the most ancient times to the present day. The speaker holds that thanks to Zionism a generation of proud Jews has grown up, who are proud of their Jewishness.
After the lecture a banquet took place in the Zionist premises. Toasts were given by Messrs. Jungster[?], Klarman, Feldman, Rozman, Glidman.
At the end Dr. Feldschuh replied to all the speakers, and with "Ha-Tikvah" the banquet ended at about 2 at night. (Sh.)

What's new in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — news.]
A tragic incident.
A car killed a Jew.
On Saturday night at 7 o'clock in the evening the Jews of Königshütte [Chorzów] were shaken by the terrible news that Itshe Lempel had been killed by a car. The news spread like lightning, and Ligate[?] Street, where the accident happened, was black with people.
The tragic accident happened in the following circumstances: Itshe Lempel was walking home from the beth midrash accompanied by another Jew from Rishe[?]. As they came onto Ligate[?] Street, 2 Christian hooligans ran up to them shouting "Zhidushe, dai braden" [roughly Polish for "Jew-boy, give us your beard"]. The two Jews, wanting to protect themselves from the attackers, stepped off the pavement. At that moment a passenger car came racing up, ran over the Jews, and the result was terrible: Lempel suffered a concussion and died a while later. The Jew from Rishe[?] had a leg broken and his body injured.
The tragically killed man had lived in Königshütte for only 9 months. During that time he was much liked there, but because of the frequent antisemitic attacks on him he sought to move to Sosnowiec, so as to be in a Jewish environment. A month ago he wanted to leave Königshütte, but the local moreh hora'ah R' Yosele Blumenfeld persuaded him not to leave them before Passover.
Itshe Lempel was 58 years old; at the request of the local moreh tzedek he was brought for burial in Sosnowiec.

The Consequences of Fragmentation

[Sosnowiec — Economy; opinion piece on the Jewish banks.]
(Our financial institutions. — We have made harmful toys of them.)
When children get a toy, they smash it; it goes without saying that this annoys the parents — after all, they spent such-and-such, here the thing was bought [?] new and already it is destroyed — but one gets used to it; one knows one is dealing with children, who can never be compared to grown-up, level-headed people.
On the other hand it annoys us when we see how grown people make toys of their own works, how they destroy and smash their own deeds.
It is [?] some years now since we began intensively to build financial institutions. People among us tried systematically to create banking institutions, which began to develop well, thanks to the fact that the builders understood their tasks. They grew step by step, until the Jewish street began to grasp that useful people's institutions were being created — institutions which are, incidentally, a result of the antisemitic oppression in the economic field.
We truly took pride and joy in watching the banks spread across the towns and townlets of Poland, but "there is no joy in Jacob" — apparently it is not destined for us to delight in our own work, to take pleasure in our fruits, and a tendency arose to overturn what had been created among us with so much love and devotion.
The institutions came to such a degree [printed "מורגה"] that both the new and the old ones began to sink. The prestige was lost, and the lustre we had known to grant the leaders who managed the banks. One noticed at once that the fine and useful ideal had been exchanged for small, childish toys, with which one can do whatever one likes. A bank became a kind of little shop, and just as Jews once set up one store next to another, one stall next to the other, and each dragged customers to himself, exactly so the banks do it now — banks that are not very sensitive, that take no account of prestige and tact and public opinion.
We saw the danger and foretold it already then, when the development began too rapidly, when it did not go along the normal road, when we saw that a tendency had been created to separate one from another. The Agudah man must have his own bank, and the big merchant his bank, and the small and still smaller merchant must each have separate banks. And so people began to follow a peculiar line of thought: that a Zionist and an artisan and a small trader and a Radomsk [Radomsko] and an Aleksander [Aleksandrów] and a Krimilov [Kromołów] Hasid must each have his own "little bench" [bank], so that he knows he comes to his own and depends on no one. And, of course, this had to reach even the level where private persons take the public into their own breast pocket and so operate at the expense of the community.
Of course the population — the simple, naive Jew, who knows nothing of tricks and dodges — cannot make sense of things here; he does not find his bearings as to place and position, and does not even know that he needs to find his bearings in anything here. So as soon as an opinion forms about a bank that is unfavourable to the public, the simple Jew at once loses his sympathy for the public banks; he does not know that he must sort things out and distinguish the bank where lawlessness reigns from [? printed "until"] the institutions that understand their tasks and their responsibility to society.
And therefore the Sosnowiec bank, where malversations were committed that went so far that the leaders of the institution have had to be arrested for illegal acts, is doing enormous harm to society. True, the simple Jew does not find his way, and at once he forms the opinion that one public institution is no better than another, not paying attention to the fact that one is never responsible for another; and we say that we can have no complaints against him — when he is not versed in these matters, one cannot demand of ordinary people that they be able to afford to spend time and take lessons in order to sort out where responsibility reigns and where — lawlessness.
It is, after all, much more practical and more restrained that society should react to unheard-of deeds when they are done in the name of the people, in the name of a public institution to which society gives trust and sympathy.
Does one really understand the defeat that w e suffer when a people's bank is branded with the stamp that malversations took place there and that people who had been chosen by the people took part in them?
Nobody, after all, is interested, and in truth it need not concern anybody either, to which tendency the bank belonged. For the street, for the public, it is a public bank, and if public — then Jewish society is to blame for it. Do we really understand the disgrace and shame this means for a people, when any [?] public institution, whatever tendency and outlook it may belong to, is reckoned as a lawless one? Do we know how this looks in the eyes of the community? Do we give ourselves an account of how this looks in the financial world?
What does it mean to commit unheard-of deeds in the name of the people, in the name of society, so that they should reach as far as the defendants' bench? Are only those who sit on the defendants' bench then accused? Are not, in that case, all the members of the bank dragged along, and perhaps even the whole of Jewish Sosnowiec — since the whole of Jewish society is responsible before the community, regardless of a small group saying that they are the community.
And therefore it used to pain us so when we saw the abnormal founding [?] of Jewish banks, which took on an epidemic character. We saw in it a dangerous disease that tears whole pieces off a healthy body, just when it is in full bloom and development.
One should, after all, have imagined that we are not children and that nobody buys us a toy that does no harm if it is smashed. One should, after all, have realised that when grown-up people play like children, it can take on dangerous forms.
And if we did do it — if we adopted the tactic of breaking up and fragmenting, of disrupting and destroying fine ideals for petty things — it must lead to ruin.
One should not have allowed our financial institutions to be fragmented into small miniature shops, out of which caricatures have emerged, from which we have disgrace and shame.
Once we let ourselves be led onto so dangerous a road, nothing better could be hoped for — and would that, would that this be our last shame...
Dr. Papuri.
An Entertainment Evening at the Będzin “Hitachdut”.

[Będzin — Zionism; social life.] Because city councillor Dr. Rechtman, chairman of the Będzin Zionist labour party “Hitachdut”, has been admitted to the Warsaw Bar (chamber of advocates), the “Hitachdut” held a banquet last Saturday night (motzei Shabbat) in its own large hall. At 9 in the evening Mr. Bergblat's orchestra “Hatikvah” plays, and Mr. Y. Gertger [?] opens the evening with a short Hebrew speech. The banquet master, Mr. Israel Gertler, delivers a longer toast and finally presents the advocate Dr. R. [Rechtman], in the name of the entire organisation, with a gold token (jeton) engraved with suitable Hebrew words of its own. Further speeches are made by Messrs. M. Rosenker, D. B. Fischel, A. [?] Milsztajn, M. Ch. Schnitzer, A. Grauer, Miss Hollender and others. Dr. Rechtman answers all the greetings, declaring his readiness for further Zionist work in general and for the benefit of Labour Zionism in particular.
After the serious part comes the material one. The gathering of 120 people enjoys fruits of the Land of Israel, wines and other delicacies [?]. The Misses Puterka and Prachcwajg entertain the guests with brilliant parodies and song numbers. Mr. David Liwer reads out a topical humorous “living newspaper”, “Der Knayper” (“The Pincher”).
With a “hora” the banquet ends at 5 in the morning.

Homely Letters.

[Satirical feuilleton — Poland, Hasidism, the press; Sosnowiec — rabbinate and community.] B"H, for the portion “of the cattle, of the herd and of the flock shall ye bring your offering”..
Reb Shloyme! You surely remember those sweet childhood years, how much joy we pupils had when we reached the portion “Vayikra”; like prisoners we counted the hours until the rebbe would finally issue the manifesto: — Children, go home, we stop learning, the cheder must be cleared for Passover”...
Those times are gone, but in history they repeat themselves. Today too, with the coming spring, the “children” are being driven apart and sent home. Not by the rebbe, but by our “Grandpa” [Piłsudski, “Dziadek”], who can no longer bear “the follies of his 400 pupils” [the Sejm deputies]. He, “Grandpa”, has been drilling them for almost 2 years now, teaching them the rules of good manners, and they, the “pupils”, have no mind at all for what is being taught to them, but busy themselves with vanity, with this-worldly things, such as democracy, parliamentarism and the like, and forget entirely that it is spring in the world..
And to tell the truth, we too forget that it is spring; were it not for the [Sai?] events we would actually not know that we are living beings. That is precisely because of this week's portion, where we find the detail “of the cattle, of the herd and of the flock shall ye bring your offering”. This is very strictly observed. Exactly in the week of this portion the tax-assessment commissions were active throughout the Jewish diaspora, examining every single person as to what kind of hide he has on him.. a hide like a cow's or like a sheep's.. First of all [?] one has to know what kind of sacrifice the assessed person must bring: a sacrifice of all his goods and chattels] or a real sacrifice — simply throw himself down from the fourth floor and be done with it..
* * *
This [?] week the telegraph brought the joyful tidings. Marconi, sitting in Genoa, lit electric lamps in Australia. It is — as Y. M. Nayman puts it — an achievement of His Majesty the Spirit. Naturally the experts will still try to explain Marconi's wonder, for the wonder [touches?] millions of people in every corner of the world. It gives us hope that Marconi's invention will also have very great significance when, by electric power, one will be able to see the true faces of today's party leaders and public figures, who do things that ought not to be done and nevertheless roll their eyes up to heaven and cry “we owe God our soul”; and if that is too little for you, they, today's public figures, have a better means, and the means is called “the press”, a very marketable commodity nowadays. It plays the same role as the “callers” [touts] and customer-catchers. The merchant who does not give the touts a tithe gets thirty-nine lashes from them.. The same role is played among us by the “press”, so to speak [?]. There are such public figures who hate reproof and cannot bear it when someone points out a fault in their public deeds; well, they — the so-called public figures — have at their disposal such sold souls, types like the popular Będzin “Megdele the mi-sheberakh maker”. The only difference is that the Megdele of old made “mi-sheberakhs” in the middle of the street for a few groszy, while today's Megdeles do it the modern way: they print the “mi-sheberakhs” in the “press”. A “[?]-letter” is not expensive: for a [decent?] dinner and a couple of gulden the “press people” are transformed, fall into hysteria too and sing songs of praise.. Therefore I ask you, Reb Shloyme, please take the trouble to find out whether the opinion is true that Marconi's invention will hurl right and left, and that the Ineffable Name will be wiped off the golems..
* * *
Now, Reb Shloyme, let us also chat in passing and hear what is going on in the political world. On the eve of the present spring two events of first-rank importance took place. The year 1930 will take an honourable place in history. In this year 2 peace agreements were concluded: 1) peace was made between Ger and Aleksander [Hasidic courts], and 2) the trade treaty between Poland and Germany.
Both agreements were concluded at one and the same time, on almost the same foundations, and may I turn out a liar, both agreements will have the same “longevity”.. for the blessings that Germany wishes Poland, and Ger — Aleksander, should go into the desolate deserts.. But be that as it may, Aleksander has already obtained a piece of ground on “Ger territory”. In Ostrów Mazowiecka, with the votes of the Ger parnasim, a rabbi from the Aleksander court was accepted. In return for this favour they count on Aleksander's forces when they come to “occupy” Łódź. For this purpose friendly relations were also established with the Radomsko side, recognising [?] him as moreh hora'ah. The post was taken by a brother-in-law of the Radomsko rebbe, Rabbi Reb Moshele Chaim, a grandson of the Berezhany rabbi, the author of the responsa “Maharsham”. With these coalition forces they want to set up a united front against the rabbinical seat in Łódź..
You also want to know about neighbouring Sosnowiec? Then I inform you that in Sosnowiec too a coalition government has been formed. Rich America (Radomsko), beggarly [?] Austria (Sochaczew) and warlike Germany (Mizrachi) have united, as my grandmother, may she rest in peace, used to say: Torah, greatness and wisdom in one place..
Almost the whole Jewish community of Sosnowiec is satisfied with this union. Except for a “group of householders” who “sit” shut away in innermost chambers and from there cry out in a still small voice:
— “Jews, why are you silent”?
And the Jews are not silent, and they answer with strong, bold voices:
— It is the noise of them that sing that I hear.. Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp..
About the rabbinate affair there is much to write, but this time I must be brief, because at this very moment I receive a polite invitation from the “Uzhanr” [?] [probably “Urząd”, the tax office], which invites me as “posek” (assessor, in the vernacular); one must go there, Reb Shloyme, and together with my fellow assessors fulfil our duty, defend with all our strength and rescue the remnant that escaped — the exhausted, benighted Jewish masses — from ruin.
Well then, [—] me [—]
[—]
Our Passover Relief Actions

(The participation of the Jewish population. — In the distribution a systematic order must prevail)
[—]s, as Passover approaches, [—] already [—][?] on one's neck, and [—] the situation is so hard, so [—]bitter, so tense, that the [aver]age[?] Jew sees no [—] which way to turn [lit. "how in and how out"]. You talk with [—] — he does not know how he will [—] get to Passover. He cannot picture [even in] thought how [—] he will bring Passover [into hi]s home, when he cannot [ma]nage with today's day. [—] How can such a Jewish fa[mily] [—] persuade itself[?] to prepare for eight [days of] Passover — matzo and eggs and potatoes — [—] when it has no livelihood for [to]day. The situation is [—] not a favourable one at the pre[sent mo]ment, and for that very reason the relief action is not[?] [ea]sy to carry out, because when one con[sid]ers all this one must after all come [to] the conviction that this year there are [—] [u]nconditionally[?] more receivers than givers, more hungry than sated. There are, after all, many, many Jewish families who in past years still gave a quite respectable kimcha [kimcha de-pischa, Passover flour charity], and this year not only will one not visit th[ose][?] families, but one will even have to think up ways how to reach them in order to smuggle the "bread of affliction" to them secretly.
The relief actions in Zagłębie in honour of Passover are in full swing; people have also already begun to consider how they should be carried out, and without doubt the leaders would surely want as many[?] people as possible to benefit from their activity, as many [hun]gry[?] as possible to get to eat their fill. Considering all this, however, one must come to the conviction that satisfying all who are hungry will not be so easy now, because one must not forget that this time we have in all the towns of Zagłębie considerably fewer givers than a year ago, and in their place, on the other hand, receivers have been added.
Among the receivers, as always, the professional beggars take the top place; they know how to manage quite well in their town[?] and [ex]ploit every opportunity to push in everywhere; they will also turn up everywhere and get the little there is everywhere. There is also a sort of professional "bebire"[?] [perhaps: big shots / charity bosses] who are everywhere "the top of the pot" and play their roles excellently.
And since we are now living in an extraordinarily bad time, a time when "lion" and "eagle" firms [i.e. old, well-established businesses] are leaving the arena and their roles are played out so tragically — in such a time, one must know, it is very hard to collect money that is designated for the public good, and however much is raised, it must be treated with respect. One must not forget that the groszy now being collected from the people are groszy of tears, soaked with grief and suffering; with pain and anguish they are taken out of Jewish pockets. The people, the ordinary citizens, give them not because they can but because they must, because they feel the nation's troubles on their shoulders, because they feel the suffering in their hearts, in their souls — and therefore one must treat these hard-earned groszy with responsibility, and they must be spent on the most essential needs.
From this standpoint precisely it is important that the relief actions carry out their work in a planned and systematic way. Around the committees there must gather people who know the town and who will pay no attention to what some Shmerl [i.e. any so-and-so] demands on his own account — support for a whole series of people; if this is done at all, it must be in a strictly limited number and only through people in whom there is the fullest trust. Besides all this, it is also not practical, because as long as the committees do not know for whom this or that support was taken, how can one know whether several people did not take for one and the same person, for one and the same family? As long as one does not know for whom one is taking, how can one know whether the most essential has been provided to those who needed to be provided for? Just as one cannot allow one family, be it the most important, to receive several times, so it cannot be permitted that another family should receive nothing and, God forbid, have to go hungry.
A definite system must absolutely be introduced[?]. Order in this field — otherwise it will be of no use, otherwise the action will be a failure, because the support will not reach those who need to be supported, those who need to be provided with the most necessary products for Passover.
And attention must be paid to the silent sufferers, to the modest poor and to the fallen [i.e. impoverished] who do not catch the eye, those who languish in silence and go hungry when nobody knows and nobody sees. One must not forget those who are ashamed and do not want to show themselves in the street, reckoning that people will point at them because they are hungry. These silent sufferers, the modest hungry ones who make do with anything — them one must remember. Them one must keep in mind; those who stand at the head of the relief actions must remember well that first of all the relief actions must provide the families mentioned with the most necessary.
This is one thing that must be kept well in mind; a second thing is the support itself. The actions must be properly supported so that they have the possibility to do what must be done so that our poor brothers and sisters do not go hungry at a time when everyone who can afford it eats his fill. Let our wealthy men remember what obligation they have towards the impoverished people of the nation, who always lived by the toil of their hands, and that now the time is a bitter one and people wander about without a scrap of work and have nowhere to earn a grosz.
Our rich Jews must take into account the present situation, in which, owing to the hard times, many givers from the middle strata of the population have dropped out — people who every year used to offer their support with warm love; now they are not in a position to come to the aid of their poor brothers, since they themselves have become impoverished and have nothing to get through the day.
Let our wealthy men not forget that they must now come forward to meet the hungry and that through them these must be rescued — that at least they should not be the cause of oppressed families having to go hungry at Passover in the innermost rooms [i.e. in secret]. That would after all be a pain and a grief and a "rasgut"[?] [possibly a misprint for "wickedness" or "worries"], which none of us may permit, to which no one may remain indifferent.
Let none of us forget the "Kol dichfin yeitei ve-yekhul" ["Let all who are hungry come and eat"] which every Jew says so comfortably while sitting at the seder on Passover.
"Everyone who is hungry, let him come in and eat" — let this not be merely a phrase that one must say out of the Haggadah to fulfil one's duty. Let every Jew be able to say this sentence with his whole heart, knowing that he has taken part in the great mitzvah of giving food to his hungry brother.
Let the Passover actions in Zagłębie be supported with a full hand and with every possibility, and let the leaders of the relief actions properly use the support raised for the benefit of the poor population.
Selekt.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Vayikra)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and edited by Y. L.[?]
Parashat Vayikra.
—o—
a) "And He called unto Moses" (Lev. 1:1)
He who chases after honour and dominion — they run away from him; but he who hides from positions of authority and honour — they chase after him. When God revealed Himself to Moses through the burning bush and called him to be the Jewish leader, Moses refused and begged for mercy: "Send, I pray Thee, by the hand of him whom Thou wilt send" — I do not want to be a leader. And seven whole days went by until the Almighty succeeded in persuading Moses to become a leader. And therefore, although in Moses' time there lived the seventy elders, Bezalel, Aaron, Hur and other great men, nevertheless — "And He called unto Moses": only Moses, the one who flees from honour, did God call unto Himself. Tanhuma[?].
• • •
A Jew, a foolish Hasid, came to Rabbi Bunem [of Przysucha] and asked him: Rebbe, it is said that "whoever flees from honour, honour pursues him" — whoever runs away from honour, honour chases after him. Now I run away from honour for miles, so why does it not chase after me?
— Because — came the answer — while running away from honour, you keep looking back to see whether it is already chasing you.. and when you turn around to see whether honour is already there, it [promptly] flees back...
• • •
There are those who know in their hearts that they are "fine Jews", that they are scholars, that they possess good qualities; only because according to the moral teachings one must be humble — well then, they are humble. "Surely[?] the greatest honour is due to us — so they think to themselves — only we run away from it.." That is no "flight from honour" at all. The truly humble man knows in his heart that he is a nothing, a putrid drop, a sinful creature of flesh and blood; he knows that no honour whatsoever is due to him...
That is why the aleph of the word "Vayikra" is written small in the Torah: because Moses was truly lowly and small in his own heart, he merited that God should call him and speak with him. Me'or va-Shemesh.
• • •
The Radomsko Rebbe, author of "Hesed le-Avraham", had [—] with a well-known Hasidic court (the match[?] [—] [—] his a man [—] to test[?] the bridegroom. [—] Rebbe! — it is true [—], that [—]
[word fragments on the folded scrap of paper: "back[?] [—]" … "[—] it is said that [—]" … "[—] himself as nothing[?] [—]" … "that one [—]" … "[—] answered [—]"]
[—] humility[?]: people pose as those who think nothing of themselves, but — they think others even more of a nothing..
—o—
b) "If any man of you bring an offering" (Lev. 1:2)
The letters of the word "mikem" [of you] say: measure for measure. For the very ancient man, thousands of years ago, who sinned with the full strength of his body, being physically very strong — had to bring a living animal for his sins. Later, when the generations had become somewhat weakened physically but much more hot-blooded in spirit[?], they had to fast and mortify themselves for their sins, measure for measure for the hot-bloodedness of the sin. Today's generations, when there is no more spiritual[?] joy[?], people are feeble, their understanding petty, and consequently their sins too are bloodless — the atonement is only to repent before God with a broken heart, and not to fast, for "fasts harm not only the body but the spirit as well". Irin Kadishin.
• • •
Rabbi Elimelech [of Leżajsk] said that if he had had two[?] more like himself, he would have abolished all the fasts.
Ibid., in Ohel Elimelech.
—o—
c) "If his offering be a burnt-offering.. and if of the flock.. and if of fowls" (Lev. 1:3, 10, 14)
Three kinds of burnt-offerings are listed in the Torah: an ox, a lamb and a bird. The rich man, who is puffed up and even boasts of his sin, must bring an ox; the middling man, who no longer sins with such pride — a lamb is enough for him; the poor man, who even when sinning is downcast in spirit, brings only a bird. Zohar.
—o—
d) "But its inwards and its legs shall he wash with water... and the inwards and the legs shall he wash with water" (Lev. 1:9, 13)
Whoever wishes to rebuke others, "to wash with water", to cleanse someone and preach morals to him — first: "its inwards" — he must first of all wash himself, cleanse his inner conscience, and only afterwards: "and the inwards and the legs shall he wash with water" — only when he himself is clean will he be able to [cleanse] others [—]
[—] of Worms[?] ("mi-Germayza").
—o—
e) "And when anyone bringeth a meal-offering unto the Lord" (Lev. 2:1)
Of the meal-offering, which is brought precisely by a poor man, it says "and when a soul bringeth", because even an offering of just a little flour costs the poor man his very soul; it is hard for him even to scrape together a pitiful[?] bit of flour. Ba'al ha-Turim.
—o—
f) "A sweet savour unto the Lord" (Lev. 1:16 [as printed])
On this the Gemara says in Menahot (111 [as printed]): both for the offering of an ox and for the offering of a bird it says "a sweet savour", because before God everything is equal. "One who gives much and one who gives little — provided he directs his heart [to Heaven]": both the one who gives more and the one who gives less, provided he means it for God's sake.
To this Rabbi David of Kotsk [Kock] said: the Gemara does not mean that the one who "gives little" should mean it for God (although that is the usual[?] sense of the Gemara), for the poor man always means his meagre donation purely for its own sake; rather, the one who "gives much", the rich man, who always gives only for fame and honour — it is to him that one says he should direct his intention to God. Nifla'ot Hadashot.
—o—
g) "If the anointed priest shall sin — so as to bring guilt on the people" (Lev. 4:3)
"If the anointed priest shall sin" — you see that the leader, the teacher, is sinful; the reason for it is "the guilt of the people", because the people is so base and sinful. The leader always wants to adapt himself to the masses, therefore he is influenced by the masses and takes over their criminal traits. Melekhet Mahshavot.
• • •
The Midrash says that God showed Adam "each generation and its expounders" — the generations and their representatives. The question arises: surely God ought to have shown the leaders first and only afterwards the generations — that is what honour requires.
Had God shown Adam a present-day leader, he would have spat: Ptoo, this is supposed to be a Jewish leader?! So he was first shown the generation, and with such a generation such a leader can indeed exist.. R. N.[?] of Ropczyce.
• • •
There is an expression in the Gemara: "The face of the generation is like the face of a dog." What is the meaning of this saying? —
A leader must walk ahead and show the masses the way, and when the masses sometimes want to stray, to go down a false road, he must lead them onto the right road. But there are leaders who want to please the masses, and they sniff out which way the current of the masses is flowing — and go along with it. Just like a dog that runs ahead and keeps turning around every moment to see where its master is going, and runs along there. The dog runs ahead, and yet it is no guide but a follower: of such "faces", such leaders, it was said: "The face of the generation is like the face of a dog."
Heard.

A Sosnowiec Big Industrialist Rescues a Jewish Daughter
The tragic story of a Łódź Jewish magnate's daughter who became the wife of a Christian dancing-hero and swindler.

[Sosnowiec / Łódź / Częstochowa — life story; apostasy.] In one of the Częstochowa cabarets a second-rate dancer began to appear under the pseudonym "Magi Werli"[?]. The dancer's performances were a great success with the public, but it did not even occur to anyone to take an interest in who this dancer was and how she had come to the stage. Her black hair and her burning, restless eyes merely bore witness that the dancer had a connection with the Jewish people, and her manners and movements convinced one that the good upbringing she had received did not fit a second-rate dancer of a provincial cabaret.
The dancer would have gone on earning her living from the stage like this who knows how long, were it not for a small coincidence: last week one of the most respected industrialists of Sosnowiec came to the cabaret, and when he saw the dancer's performance he could not hide his great astonishment from his acquaintances. After the show the industrialist went to the dancer's dressing room, and she, on seeing the industrialist, broke into spasmodic weeping. The following story came out:
The dancer is the daughter of one of the former biggest industrialists in Łódź, an owner of one of the largest cotton joint-stock companies in the "Polish Manchester", and this is how this very rich Jewish daughter came to the point of having to appear as a dancer in a cabaret.
The founders of a well-known Łódź joint-stock company were the brothers G. The firm became very large and was reckoned one of the richest in Łódź. One of the brothers did not live in peace with his wife, who came from a rich assimilationist family; her husband's Jewishness did not suit her, and she decided to separate from him for as long as he would not agree to convert. By then G. already had a little daughter, Marila, with his wife; the girl stayed with her father, and the mother lived separately. Mrs G. converted and waited until her husband and her child would do the same. Meanwhile the war broke out. During the war, and then in the inflation years, G. got entangled in bad business. On the other side he had great troubles from his estranged wife, the convert, and one fine morning in the year 1924 it became known in Łódź that the big industrialist G. had been found shot in his room — G. had committed suicide.
Marila was by then already a grown-up girl, without any supervision on the part of her mother, to whom the daughter in no way wanted to return; but she lacked nothing, for as the sole heiress of her father's fortune she was provided for all her life. But only now does the girl's tragic story begin.
Marila began going very often to dance halls. This was at the time when the tango, the shimmy and the foxtrot were at the centre of fashion; the young rich girl was carried away by dancing and it became her whole pleasure. But in the dance halls blackmailers always hang about, lying in wait for prey. So it was in this case too.
A certain Karel S., an elegant, slim and handsome young man, cast an eye on the black-haired, charming Marila and little by little spread[?] his net over the victim.
As time went on Karel turned the girl's head more and more, until he had her firmly in his clutches. Marila by then had truly fallen in love with Karel; Marila converted, the couple married, and Marila signed over her share of the fortune — consisting of a big house in Łódź, a second big house in Warsaw and a large number of shares — to her husband Karel S.
Soon Karel's blood made itself heard. He moved with his wife to Warsaw and began to do "business". That, of course, is what it was called for Marila. In reality Karel's occupation was cabarets and card-playing; his "fartentserish"[?] (rakish) blood awoke in him, and with pockets full of money he became one of the biggest Warsaw playboys, and this cost him a great deal of money. First he sold his large number of shares, and when those ran out he sold his house in Warsaw. His wife had already begun to understand that she had been trapped; Karel did not stand on much ceremony with her. The "Żydówka" [Polish, "the Jewess"] counted for little with him, and he did whatever he pleased.
For whole weeks Karel did not come home, squandering in the meantime the great fortune of the Jewish big industrialist's daughter. Marila already began to lack the most necessary things, until she began to "buy out" [sic; read: sell off] everything from her home, sold her flat and lived on that. On top of all this Karel declared that he had had enough of the "Żydówka" and vanished somewhere, running away from his creditors.
Marila was left desperate in the street with no means of living; she had nowhere to turn, because by that time the joint-stock company "G." had passed into other hands, and Marila did not even have anyone to talk to.
Until Marila decided on the last step: a few weeks ago she attempted suicide in one of the Warsaw hotels, but she was rescued in time. Having no other way out, she made use of the fact that she could dance and joined the Częstochowa cabaret as a dancer under the name "Bagi"[?] Werli.
Now that the Sosnowiec big industrialist, who had been a good friend of Marila's father, has recognised her, he has decided to take her to himself and to look after her future fate.
